...Miss Jessie, what is your relationship to that "Zoey" girl? I became the "Big Sister" of a girl on our ship without even meaning to.
...I didn't expect you to be friends with a younger girl, Miss Jessie. "Zoey," was it? We have a Plutonian girl named "Misty" who looks up to me.
...Your enthusiasm is nice, Miss Jessie, but I don't just hand out firearms. I'm sure Earth has the technology.
...You wanted a laser ring from me, Miss Jessie? Earth has plenty of advanced technology---I'm sure you can find one here.
...I'm sorry, Miss Jessie, but our crew's resources are too limited to give away weapons. Does Earth not let citizens possess any?
...You must be able to get a laser ring for yourself on Earth, Miss Jessie. It takes technology from its colonies, after all.
...It's quite fascinating to see how my various pilots perform in different situations, Miss Jessie. But work is still necessary, even if it's boring.
...It doesn't matter if flight data is interesting or not, Miss Jessie. Dread piloting is a matter of life and death.
...Miss Jessie, if I don't know how my team needs to manage its resources, we'll be caught with no ammunition during a dogfight. "Boring" is irrelevant.
...I'm sorry you don't find my work stimulating, Miss Jessie, but I'm not forcing you to do it. It's part of leading a Dread team.
...Saki, did you recommend a restaurant to me earlier? I have no Earth money to pay for it...I was hoping for landmarks.
...I'm glad there's a chicken restaurant you enjoy, Saki, but I can't pay for that. I meant natural landforms I can fly to.
..."Drive-In Tori" wouldn't happen to accept Mejarian credits, would it, Saki? Natural landmarks are my only tourism option...
...I'm sorry, Saki, but I can't afford any chicken. I don't have Mejarian money, let alone Earth...do you know any scenic flight routes?
...Miss Misato, you mentioned your organization's headquarters? I'd like to see those "Evas," but aren't they under security?
...I'd very much appreciate a chance to look at the "Evangelion" units at your headquarters, Miss Misato, but would I be allowed anywhere near them?
"Tokyo-3"...and the "Geofront." Do you have the authority to grant me clearance, Miss Misato? This "NERV" sounds rather clandestine.
Your technology does sound fascinating, Miss Misato, but "NERV" sounds like they'd attempt to shoot down my Dread. Could you admit me?
...Chazz, you recommended the "Duel Academy"? Our ship has passed by volcanic planets, if that's the main attraction.
...Chazz. Does the "Duel Academy" you mentioned have other sights besides a volcano? Many planets we pass have volcanoes.
...Volcanic activity is a fairly common sight among the uninhabited planets our ship passes by, Chazz. What's taught at your "Duel Academy"?
...The "Duel Academy," you said? Plenty of planets have volcanoes---even Mejare's unterraformed areas do. What could I learn about "dueling"?
...Chazz, I don't appreciate joking answers to a simple question. What did you say about a "separate dimension of purple"?
...A "separate dimension of nothing but purple." Just when I finally start to ask men for advice, I get a snide answer.
...What's this about a "purple dimension," Chazz? Is Earth more advanced than I realize, or are you just making fun of me?
...What technology has allowed you to develop a "separate dimension," Chazz? I could believe it...if you weren't the type to tell jokes.
...I see. Wouldn't she gain more muscle by being the one who beats monsters up?
...That doesn't sound very regimented, Megumin. A brief session of squats might do more to help her---or just being on the offensive.
...Getting beaten up by monsters? I'm sure it builds strength to slaughter animals, but anyone can be knocked around.
...Do you mean "beating up monsters"? I gained much of my strength from streetfighting---and losing a fight just means broken bones.
...Yuelia, you asked about my tablet, right? I use it to store and analyze the performance data of my pilots.
Dita's shot accuracy has been going up...Yuelia, you expressed interest in this tablet? I'm organizing squadron data with it.
...Yuelia. You wanted to know more about this device? It's a personal data organizer---Dread team leaders are given them to manage pilot information.
...Yuelia, you brought up my tablet earlier. It's just a simple personal computer---I track pilot efficiency and lethality figures with it.
...For the record, Yuelia, I don't expect my laser ring to malfunction. But as this is a hostile planet, I want to make sure I'm armed.
...If my ring were to malfunction, Yuelia, it simply wouldn't work. But Earth is too dangerous a planet to be without a weapon.
...Yuelia, you sounded worried about my laser ring malfunctioning. The only one who would be in danger would be me, unarmed on a foreign world.
...A pirate cannot afford to be stuck on a hostile world without a functioning weapon, Yuelia. This place alone seems to house dangerous threats.
...Laser rings are reliable firearms, Yuelia. I don't expect any malfunctions...but still, being stuck on Earth would be the worst time for one.
It's easy for you to say nothing bad will happen, Yuelia. Our crew has been attacked by forces from Earth many times now.
"Nothing bad will happen"...a likely story from an Earth girl. Earth fleets have attacked our ship numerous times now.
I hope you're only ignorant of my situation, Yuelia. I'm wary of this planet because Earth has regularly sent fleets after us.
I am an officer on a ship targeted by Earth for opposing its Harvest fleets, Yuelia. Don't tell me "nothing bad" will happen if I'm unarmed...
..."Have fun." From an Earth girl, any reassurance is disingenuous. This planet has made a target out of our crew.
It's not in my best interest or my job description to "have fun," Yuelia...especially on a known aggressive planet.
...I appreciate your wish for me to relax, Yuelia, but it's hard to do so unarmed on a hostile world. Earth does not tolerate our crew's resistance.
..."Have fun" is something my crewmates tell me, as well, Yuelia. But I am an officer of a ship resisting Earth---I'm vulnerable here.
...I am frequently busy, Yuelia, yes. Leading a Dread team is a lot of work, so I'm multitasking.
...It was not my idea to come here, Yuelia, so I am behind on work in addition to being generally busy.
...I am busy, Yuelia, but it's none of your concern. As Dread team leader, I'm accustomed to multitasking to ease my workload.
...It's true that my work as Dread commander keeps me busy, Yuelia. Being a pirate doubles that...so I'm taking advantage of lulls in the game.
...I don't have time to be playing this, Yuelia. But I can manage my workload---even if I may have to sacrifice some sleep.
...I don't have time for many hobbies in general, Yuelia. I do my best just to make time for exercise.
...My personal time is a low priority regardless, Yuelia. Leadership leaves little time for that.
...Thank you for your concern earlier, Yuelia, but my time management is not an issue. I exercise, eat, work, and sleep.
...Panty, what did you say earlier? Men have "flavors"? As in, different body types, or literal tastes...?
...Panty. I hope you didn't mean it literally when you said men have "flavors." What about them are you tasting?
...Panty, you said men have "flavors." Do you just mean their personalities, or is there some...oral aspect to being with them?
...Men have "flavors," Panty? Oral sex makes sense between two girls, but...with a man? Do you mean their seed?
...I appreciate the explanation you gave earlier, Tomoko. It makes sense that Earth would have a term for women in love...if an insulting one.
...Based on the tone you took, Tomoko, "lesbian" doesn't sound complimentary...I guess Earthlings wouldn't encourage Mejarian love.
...If men and women are supposed to live together on this world, then it's no surprise a word like "lesbian" exists to insult girls who don't oblige.
...Is "lesbian" meant to be an insult towards Earth girls who ignore men, Tomoko? It didn't sound like a compliment.
...You may not have dated a man, Miss Miko, but you've been one.
...I think your experience being a man would still offer a lot to us, Miss Miko.
...The fact a whole country believed you were male has got to count for something, Miss Miko. Even if you never dated one.
...Maybe you could tell us how you got your subjects to believe you were male, Miss Miko.
...If violence towards men made them fall in love, Saki, all of planet Tarak would be obsessed with us. Then again... maybe they are.
...It's been my impression of men that violence garners their respect, Saki. Tarak sees Mejare's women as worthy opponents, after all.
...You may have revealed why Tarak continues to fight us, Saki. Apparently men seek women who are just as aggressive as they are.
...You may need to be even more aggressive to find a man, Saki. Based on Tarak and Mejare's war, men respect women who stand up to them.
...Wishing for everyone's wishes to be granted is very sweet of you, Tomoko. Not many girls your age would think of others in that moment.
...You asked if I had any questions, Miss Jessie? Well...how forceful do men tend to be? How soon do couples start having sex?
...Miss Jessie. You wanted to know if I had any questions about dating men...how quickly do relationships with them become sexual?
I'm not sure if you're the best person to ask, Miss Jessie...but men seem so aggressive. Do they tend to pressure girls into sex soon after dating?
...Rainbow Dash, you mentioned someone's male sibling making advances on you. Is it typical for men to approach women?
...I've only made acquaintances of men, as well, Mary. But what did you mean when your friend was "concerned with dying"?
...Your male friend was "concerned with dying," Mary? You said that so casually that I assume it's not literal...
...What did you recommend to me, Mary? An "anna-may" convention? I'm not familiar with that term, nor how to spell it...
...Mary. What is "anime," and why would I fit in at a convention for it? Is it a fighter ship design show?
...Erufuda. You said you had a concealed weapon? You certainly have ample space to hide one on your person... and it can't be a bow.
...Erufuda, fitness requires constant vigilance, and it is paramount for combat readiness. Negligence presents a far greater danger.
...Erufuda. I understand your concerns over excessive exercise and eating disorders, but a pirate's food is scarce, and combat is constant.
...Men are attracted to girls smiling and laughing, Erufuda? I guess that's one reason I haven't received much attention from our prisoners...
..."Smiling and laughing." Our male prisoners have each taken interests in other girls, so your theory may hold some water, Erufuda.
...My own crewmates regard me smiling or laughing as a shock. If that's what men seek, Erufuda, it's no wonder our prisoners aren't fond of me...
...I think the man you know preferring overweight women is an outlier, Erufuda. You should still slim down for the sake of your health.
...I hope you're not seriously maintaining your unhealthy weight for the sake of one man's fetishes, Erufuda. No partner should demand that.
...I'm no expert on men, Erufuda, but I haven't seen much evidence that they like overweight women. Your partner may, but it's still unsafe.
...Erufuda, I don't have any Earth money to pay at a restaurant. I can fly to landmarks in my Dread, if you know of any.
...I'm not interested in junk food, Erufuda, nor do I have any Earth money to pay for it. Are there natural landmarks near "Tokyo"?
...A firm butt is important, Erufuda. You wouldn't want flab on such an important muscle.
...Why would I not train my butt, Erufuda? Not only do girls find it attractive, but it's a large muscle, constantly in use.
...Yes, Erufuda, of course. The butt is a strong, important muscle, even though a pilot spends most of her time sitting on hers.
...A fat backside isn't any use, Erufuda. Muscular butts are just as attractive, but with utility and strength. Of course I train it.
Mejare rarely teaches pre-interstellar history...Shouko, what historical events occurred at the "Kyoto" site you mentioned?
"Kyoto"...thank you, Shouko. I now know exactly how to spell that, as well...what's the history that occurred there? I know little of Earth's past...
...I think I know what a man "cumming inside you" means, Moon...but I don't expect a good explanation from you regardless.
...I'm not interested in your attempts to shock me with purposefully degenerate stories, Moon. I doubt two of those rods could even fit in a girl.
...Whatever number of men you've had sex with at once, Moon, I'm sure you're exaggerating to mock me. Don't answer if you aren't serious.
...I hope men aren't uniformly drawn to what you might give them, Moon. Surely some have a sense of romance.
...I'm well aware that men come in different sizes, Moon. The man in my squadron is quite short...but I'll take your word for it on how he might "stretch me."
...I'm surprised that got your attention, Moon. Tropical islands would be a nice vacation... but I won't be having sex with the wildlife.
...That was a more introspective response than I expected of you, Moon. Island ruins would be fascinating... I'd like to go there and reflect myself.
...Moon, how many girls have told you that they enjoy the company of "horny ghosts"? I am not among them.
...If a strip poker bar is the best place this planet offers, Moon, then apparently Earth's devastation in my time was not much loss, after all.
...Tarak's "wild men" is propaganda from my homeworld, Moon. If you went there, you would be captured and executed for being a woman.
...Moon. Tarak's men aren't "wild" because of sexual prowess---it's Mejare's labeling of political enemies. You would be killed on Tarak for being female.
...To put your mind at ease, Erufuda, the men on our ship were captured, but we now treat them as crew members.
...I don't want to date our prisoners, Erufuda--- they're just a sample of men's behavior. Regardless, they're not treated as prisoners anymore.
...It's strange that you would group blue-haired girls into some collective class, Cynthia. What experiences have led you do that?
...From your earlier comments, Cynthia, it sounds as if a specific group of people with blue hair have left an impression on you. I'd like to know the story behind that.
...I understand focusing on your work at the expense of relationships, Cynthia. Mejarians date other women, but I'm in the same situation...
...I haven't had much time for relationships myself, Cynthia. That's with other women, but still...I see it can preclude chances with men, as well.
...I appreciate your interest in our crew's exploits, Cynthia, but I can't justify bringing aboard another woman to just tag along. Our food is limited.
...Thank you for your interest, Cynthia, but the Nirvana is a pirate ship cut off from our supply lines. You would need to fill a role to be worth having aboard.
...The Nirvana isn't a science vessel, Cynthia. You'd be another mouth to feed---and as our quartermaster likes to say, everyone has to work to eat on our ship.
...Pure science wouldn't justify you tagging along in our current situation, Cynthia. Maybe if you were a refugee, but otherwise, you'd have to work in the regisystem to eat.
...As I understand it, Cynthia, our laser rings did go through numerous iterations to make them safe and effective. That research has paid off substantially.
You were talking about ring-based weapons, Cynthia? Our laser rings are superior technology to mechanical firearms, but it's true it took time to develop them to that point.
...If you're still curious whether I have any appointments, Cynthia, I am essentially always on call in case we need to scramble.
...I schedule flight practice and patrol timeslots on this device, Cynthia, but my work is otherwise on-call. Enemy fleets don't take out appointments for their attacks.
...I'm sorry that happened to you, Jolyne. I'd heard that men were a proud race who wouldn't sell out their companions.
...I'm sorry, Jolyne. It wasn't my intention to pry like that...would you say most men would do the same in his position?
I understand if you have other obligations, Pyrrha. It's a shame, though---a girl with experience on a combat team would make an excellent pilot.
If you'd rather be a "huntress," Pyrrha, I won't hold it against you. It sounds as if it's required you to hone skills that'd be useful for a pilot, however.
I don't mean to judge you about your romantic life, Pyrrha. Has a man ever caught your interest, at least?
...There's no shame in having limited romantic experience, Pyrrha. But even if you've never been with a man...have you met one you considered dating?
...There's no need to apologize, Pyrrha. I haven't had much time for relationships myself. Have you met a man that seemed like a good partner?
...Isn't this planet Earth, Pyrrha? Maybe it's the historical name for it, and you've adopted a different one since.
...Pyrrha, this is planet Earth, isn't it? The coordinates match historical accounts. Or do only colonists call it Earth now?
...Is this planet not called Earth anymore, Pyrrha? You sounded confused---it might be an old-fashioned name that's survived among descendants of colonists.
...Pyrrha, did you ask about my laser ring? It's a standard firearm on Mejare. I thought they were produced here, as well.
...Pyrrha, you asked where I "got" my laser ring. Energy weapons have been mass-produced on my homeworld for years. Is that not true for Earth?
...Pyrrha, you mentioned this tablet before. Since poker has so many breaks in its action, I'm organizing some simulation data for my squadron.
...If you're still interested in my tablet, Pyrrha, I'm using the time between rounds to prepare future flight simulations. Our discovery of Vandreads has presented opportunities for new formations.
...Stella, did you say you've visited other versions of Earth? The one in my time is devastated and needs machinery to maintain an atmosphere.
...The Earth of this time is unfamiliar to me, too, Stella. Where I come from, the planet is hardly habitable at all, and its people can no longer reproduce.
...The "island of Cyprus," Galatea? Beauty is a perfect reason to go---my home planet Mejare is known for the same reason.
...There's no reason to denigrate your birthplace, Galatea. Mejare has its issues, but it's a beautiful blue planet.
...I'd be happy to visit "Cyprus," Galatea. My homeworld is beautiful, as well, but there are reasons not to go there.
...I don't begrudge you for not being familiar with men, Neptune. It was a question directed at Earthlings, since this planet is known to have men and women living together.
It's no issue if men aren't common on your homeworld, Neptune---I didn't meet any men myself until I was nineteen. I only asked because Earth has large male and female populations.
...I understand if you're dedicated to your position, Neptune. What exactly are your duties as "goddess"?
...I understand if being a fighter pilot is not as glamorous as a goddess, Neptune. On the subject, what are your responsibilities to your nation?
You seem like a smart girl, Shouko, but I wouldn't have considered you for a piloting role unless you overcame your speaking issues.
We have many less dangerous roles on our ship, Shouko, but most of them would still require you to speak to others. We all have to rely on each other.
...I wasn't really considering you, Shouko. You're intelligent, but pilots can't communicate just by writing. That goes for jobs in munitions, engineering, and on the bridge, as well.
...I don't know much about computer games, Erufuda. We do run flight simulations, if that's what you were talking about.
Space Battles 4 would have to be a robust flight simulator with physical feedback for it to reflect much on your piloting potential, Erufuda. That's what we use on our ship.

condition.saying: So, Meia, what kind of ship do you fly?

case.state: ...I pilot a custom Dread assault craft, Mk IV. Earth may have similar fighters like your "B.E.S.", but Dreads are an Imperial Mejarian design.
Our team uses Mk IV Dread fighters with customizable parts, such as thrusters or missile capacity. It was developed on Mejare, so it may not resemble Earth's B.E.S. ships.
I appreciate your earlier confidence, Miss Miko, but we're satisfied with our current leadership. You could possibly command a Dread team.
Our captain and commander are both respected members of our crew, Miss Miko. Your leadership qualities would be needed at lower ranks.
...Miss Miko, Magno's Family needs leaders at lower levels. Those who would be seeing combat.
...I'm sure your military experience is impressive, Miss Miko, but our current captain fulfills more roles than that. You'd need to be a field commander.
...I understand your concern, Deimos. We would not want to cause conflict with other armed groups by headhunting their members.
...It's for the best if we don't recruit from other organizations, Deimos. We have enough enemies as it is.
...Deimos. Are you saying defection would be met with punishment? We would prefer to stay out of Earth's internal politics.
...Yuri, you mentioned "Himeji Castle"? A "bird taking flight" is popular symbolism on Mejare...we keep them as pets.
...I'd like to visit that bird-shaped castle you mentioned, Yuri. I had a pet bird when I as a girl, like a lot of Mejarians.
"Mount Fuji"...capped with snow. That isn't a common sight on my homeworld, Yuri...thank you for the suggestion.
Mejare's terraformed areas don't have much snow or elevation, so "Mount Fuji" might be a good place to visit. Thank you, Yuri.
Your casual experience with men is enough, Yuri. Can you describe---the way they treat you?
...I've worked with men myself, Yuri, but they're like me---they don't know what to make of the other gender. How do they act around you?
You don't have to apologize, Yuri. Many of our crew members prefer to be in engineering or munitions. Still, you don't know what you have the courage for until you need it.
Most of the Magno Family would never have thought they'd have the nerves to be pirates in the first place, Yuri. But I understand not wanting to live that life.
...I understand why you'd want to learn more about yourself before leaving your homeworld, Galatea. Still, a pilot who could survive in a vacuum would be a great asset to our team.
...You should explore your homeworld if it's important to you, Galatea. An android would make an excellent pilot, though---you could survive accidents that would kill any of us.
...To answer your question from earlier, Brock, Dread fighters are personal gunships designed for space combat. Sleek designs, superior maneuverability.
...Brock. You asked what a Dread does, right? It's a personal space gunship I pilot, preferred by women. Men tend to use bulky mech-types.
...Regarding what you said earlier, Brock, laser rings are very much designed to not be "crazy." They achieve the same lethality as kinetic guns without the noise.
...I'm quite aware that not only men use "bulky" weapons like shotguns, Brock. I have a subordinate pilot who collects antiques...and uses them in combat.
...When I said mechanical guns are for men, Brock, I was referring to what is typically used on Tarak, the planet of men. Some girls are partial to them...I am not.
I didn't have any intention of recruiting a man, Brock. It's been enough of a struggle to integrate our three prisoners into the crew, and they aren't careless with explosives.
My question was directed at the women playing, Brock. Our crew works with our male prisoners, but they're not eager for me to bring more on board---especially dangerous ones.
I wasn't considering you as a pilot, Brock. As a man, you could introduce tension in our Dread team---not to mention your reckless weapons handling.
I didn't have any intention of recruiting a man, Brock. It's been enough of a struggle to integrate our three prisoners into the crew, and they aren't careless with explosives.
My question was directed at the women playing, Brock. Our crew works with our male prisoners, but they're not eager for me to bring more on board---especially dangerous ones.
I wasn't considering you as a pilot, Brock. As a man, you could introduce tension in our Dread team---not to mention your reckless weapons handling.
I didn't have any intention of recruiting a man, Brock. It's been enough of a struggle to integrate our three prisoners into the crew, and they aren't careless with explosives.
My question was directed at the women playing, Brock. Our crew works with our male prisoners, but they're not eager for me to bring more on board---especially dangerous ones.
I wasn't considering you as a pilot, Brock. As a man, you could introduce tension in our Dread team---not to mention your reckless weapons handling.
...Lyralei, you said something about your "forest" earlier. Why would it be hard to find? I can fly to it.
...Lyralei, can you elaborate on your "forest"? This planet doesn't have any conditions that would make it difficult to locate from orbit.
...I expected some cultural differences because of our homeworlds, Polly. There must be things all men share. For instance, their...penis.
...I would appreciate any general information on men that you have, Polly. You mentioned their---penises, for instance.
...I've been navigating social differences with our prisoners already, Polly. Something as simple as men's anatomy can be useful. You mentioned their tube-organs---the "penis."
...I can't picture myself dating a girl from another planet, Polly. Mejare is the only colony we've found where women live without men.
...Polly, I asked you about men because you're a girl from another planet. You're used to living around them---Mejare never had contact with cultures that did.
...Amy, if I can offer some advice, you can't force yourself into someone's heart. One of my trainees had the same problem with a man she likes.
...Amy, I have a new pilot who's tried to force a man to return her feelings. Not everyone enjoys being chased.
...We'd be happy to take you in, Lux. You're intelligent, combat-trained, and composed---most of our recruits need to be taught those things.
...I think you'd fit right in on our crew, Lux. It sounds like you can already handle yourself in battle---the only thing you'd have to learn is a Dread's controls.
...I was hoping you'd be interested in my offer, Lux. You seemed like the best candidate on the table, even without your magic.
...I think you'd make an excellent pilot, Lux. From the sound of it, you're already a fine soldier.
...If you need a cause to fight for, Lux, our crew could use a girl like you. You're strong, smart, and combat-ready, magic or not.
...Wikipe-tan, did you say you worked as a radio operator? That would fill a role on our crew, as well--- our communications officer just had a baby.
...If you're worried about your lack of experience, Wikipe-tan, we train our pilots. That said, radio operation is a useful skill for serving on the bridge.
"Pyramids," "temples," "towers"...that's what you mentioned, right, Susie? Most Mejarians would probably recommend the architecture, too---like its crystal spires.
...Mejare prides itself on its architecture, too, Susie. A lot of imperial imagery is the massive towers and temples reaching out into orbit.
...Susie, I didn't see the "tallest tower" you mentioned when I landed here. I guess this period is more primitive---Mejare's tallest buildings reach orbit.
...The Earth of this time must still be developing its architecture, Susie. I would've expected the "CN Tower" to be visible from orbit, like Mejare's imperial courts.
...A satellite is a scanning instrument placed into orbit. They're trivial next to space travel---they don't even self-propel like a Dread.
...Just as this moon orbits Earth, a satellite is any scanning instrument placed into orbit. They just use gravity to move---simple next to a Dread fighter.
Satellites are just orbital scanners for planets. They're the first space technology ever designed---you should see my Dread.
...Satellites are among the most primitive space technology, Nami. They're orbital scanning instruments---my Dread is far more advanced.
I can assure you space technology exists here---my ancestors were from Earth, and Earthlings have been sending attack fleets after us.
...I could prove space technology exists, but I see no reason to share it with an Earthling. You've already sent entire fleets to kill us.
...Maybe a pirate is blameless here, but Earth has been dispatching Harvest units to destroy us. Space technology is all too real.
...After being told I'm descended from spacefaring Earthlings and facing its attack forces, I find it hard to accept that satellites don't exist here.
...Never mind. This is just a stripping game---and this Earth is probably from an earlier time. Early enough that you can just sail around in a bikini...
Well...there's no need to dwell on the subject in a game like this. This probably isn't the Earth of my time, anyway...you wouldn't be wearing a bikini there.
...It's not your fault. This is probably an Earth from before its environment was destroyed---with how healthy you look.
...Never mind. The Earth of this time may just be more primitive---you might be better off for it.
...Ringo. Someone from Earth threatened you not to leave for space? That's exactly the kind of rule the Magno Family opposes back on Mejare.
...Mejare's leadership didn't want us leaving its orbit, either, Ringo. If you joined our crew, you wouldn't have to submit to those threats.
...Aster, you mentioned a "Kath" earlier? If that's one of your wives, you shouldn't volunteer her like that---but at least you're not trying to poach more from us.
...I'm surprised you didn't volunteer yourself, Aster. Unless "Kath" is a wife of yours, and you're looking to cut down instead of recruit.
...Fina, you said you're from "Arcadia"? That might just be an older name for Earth. Could you describe what you've seen there?
"Arcadia"...that might just be what Earthlings used to call this planet, Fina. I'm sure you've seen a lot of its surface from the air--- maybe it matches our records.
...I appreciate your offer, Fina. I'd have to ask my own captain, Magno Vivan, but I suspect a fleet of airships wouldn't do us much good.
...It'd be nice to have allies from Earth, Fina, but it's probably not helpful unless you're capable of space combat.
...You wanted to join us for chemistry research, right, Sucrose? If you can work with engineers or with doctors, we could find room for you on our crew.
...I'm sorry, Sucrose, but we don't have a science team. We do have engineering and medical, if you can apply your research to that.
...I'm not sure I would've recruited a man in the first place, Takatoshi. Our crew has had a hard enough time accepting our three prisoners.
...A man with mech experience might actually help mentor our male pilot, Takatoshi. But I don't think the crew is ready to bring aboard random men from Earth.
...Hilda, did you say you've just casually slept with men? I know girls have flings on my homeworld, but that rod men have...it seems like something to take seriously.
...Hilda, have you really just---hooked up with men before? That thing---the tube they have. Wouldn't you have to trust him to let him push it in?
...I can't shop here, Hilda, but a beach would be relaxing. How crowded are the ones in Derdriu?
...If Derdriu's beaches have any privacy, Hilda, I might like to visit them. The shops aren't any use.
...Our captain did used to be a nun when she was younger, Hilda. Maybe that cathedral you mentioned bears some resemblance to the religion she learned as a girl.
...I might be able to learn a little about our captain from an Earth cathedral, Hilda. She's an old priestess from colonization times. Most Mejarians don't take religion too seriously.
...Hilda, did you say Earth has three capital cities? How fragmented is the population here?
Three different capitals...this must be before the frontier-era. Hilda, are there any other states on Earth?
...I don't need an extensive list of places to visit here, Miku. One is enough. Have you ever performed in some large natural area?
...I guess you're familiar with concert halls, Miku? If you've ever performed at a natural amphitheater, I might like to visit it.
...The men we have onboard are vital to the ship's functioning, Penny, so it might really be best if we placated them. Is it as simple as feeding them well?
...As far as I can tell, Penny, the men have been happy to serve on our crew just by giving them big portions at meals. I was wondering if "placating" them was really so simple.
...I was surprised at how quickly we learned to work with the men on our ship, Penny. Maybe it makes sense if it was never a problem for our ancestors.
...I hated the idea of having men on our crew at first, Penny. But we all started to get along with them before we even knew it. Maybe it's just part of being human.
...Penny, have you had a girlfriend before? I guess if robots are so humanlike here, people might start to get attached to them.
...Maybe I should've figured fully human robots would get romantic attention. You meant to say you've been in relationships, right, Penny?
...Either recommendation is fine, Monika. I could stand to learn about Earth's history or its environment.
...Earth's past and present are both important, Monika. If you know any informative locations, I can make a note to visit.
...Pirates don't have it easy, Critical Darling. I didn't expect to recruit someone who I assume makes a good living.
...I'm sure your band is doing well, Critical Darling. I'm not here to pry girls away from lives they already enjoy.
...You've never been with anyone, Critical Darling? On Mejare, rockstars are always seen with their groupies following behind. Girls dream about it.
...I'm surprised you don't have any experience, Critical Darling. Isn't that part of the appeal of being a rockstar? On Mejare, anyway.
...Any natural area is fine to recommend, Critical Darling. Earth is famous where I'm from for how varied its environment was.
...Have you ever performed in some large open area, Critical Darling? Any of Earth's natural landmarks would be good to visit, just to see what inspired terraforming.
...You'd be surprised how close some of our mechs have come to living things, Bobobo. Whatever you meant by "being" one.
...Our ships have shown a lot of their own feelings ever since we took men onboard, Bobobo. Somehow it doesn't surprise me a man "turns into" a mech.
...I guess you twist your nosehair into stilts, Bobobo? You seem more like an android the longer this game goes.
...I can believe you're part machine, Bobobo. Maybe that "nosehair" is wiring.

state.text: Ignatz's seed at least might not kill me on contact. But you can both keep it to yourselves!
Wha---I'm not here for any man's seed. Or hairy humanoid creature's, for that matter!
You---keep me away from any fluids you have. Why don't you exchange seed with each other?

case.state: ...I understand not having found someone, Fluttershy. If you don't mind, I'd like to know what you're looking for in a man.
...Fluttershy, what would make a man the "right person" to you? I have a hard time imagining one as a partner.
...You must have been isolated if you don't know what dating is, Fina. It's frightening how pockets of people can be cut off from all contact.
...You really were cut off from others, weren't you, Fina? Dating is common to a lot of societies. But it's easy for isolated people to have warped perspectives...
...I've stayed out of relationships by telling people the same sort of thing, Gwen. Even if we're all in danger, it's not appropriate for a leader to date her pilots.
...I've used my own position to excuse myself from romance, Gwen. It could compromise missions for an officer to play favorites.
...I can't prove to you that we're innocent, Gwen, but we don't attack civilians. There's a reason we all fell into piracy.
...We might technically be criminals, Gwen, but it's not for personal gain. We were all innocents once, too.
...New York is a big city, right, Gwen? I don't like the noise and the crowds of people. It's just a nuisance.
...I'm sure New York is a nice place, Gwen, but big cities are too crowded for me.
...I didn't like my chances of recruiting royalty, Petra. Still, it's asking a lot of a young girl to have her mend foreign relations.
...Piloting probably doesn't compare to diplomacy. Is that really what your home expects of you, Petra?
...Brigid is full of plant life, isn't it, Petra? I might actually enjoy it there, though I'd rather not be introduced to everyone.
...I don't need the full guest's tour of your home, Petra. But if it's as natural as you say, I might like to spend some time there...
...You mean your ears, Sucrose? We've never met one, no. But colonists might represent only a small portion of Earth humans.
...No colonists have had ears like yours, Sucrose. But we don't know what sample of Earthlings left to found all those colonies.
...I'd written you off long before you started giving smart answers, Myriam. You can't pilot a Dread through a cutout.
...I wasn't considering the girl hiding under a box for a piloting job, Myriam.
...We have a protocol for girls who don't follow orders, Myriam. I'd recommend throwing her out the airlock.
...Pilots who can't take orders usually get reassigned to reg, Myriam. And if you can't handle lifting crates, we'd stop feeding you.
...Reimu, what experience do you have as a "target"? Our Dreads are famous for their agility.
...Our Dreads are large, Reimu, but they're some of fastest ships in our system. What exactly has been firing at you here?
...The only men I know are soldiers, Reimu. But they may not like girls who they see as lazy.
...The men I know seem to respect hard work, Reimu. They are soldiers, but if you spend most of your time drinking, that might be it.
...I'm sorry, Reimu, but we don't even have Mejarian money. The captain doesn't seem to trust it.
...We barely have Mejarian money, Reimu. Our captain is a priestess---I think she doesn't want us getting greedy.
...We'd be happy to accept a girl with your combat skills, Kumatora. A year ago, we were just surviving, but we've since learned of a threat to our homeworlds.
...As a matter of fact, Kumatora, our planets are facing destruction. If you're willing to help, it sounds like you've got experience fighting and working in a team.
...I guess the men in your party weren't your type, Kumatora? They sound kind of like the men I've traveled with.
...I could describe some of our prisoners as a "kid" and a "bum," Kumatora. They managed to come through in the end---maybe in spite of themselves.
...We've learned that lesson a few times over, Kumatora. The only way humans are all bad is if you don't think of them as human at all.
...Good and bad ones, huh, Kumatora? As long as you see your enemy as "human" in the first place.
...My mother spoke about love the same way, Kumatora. You can't understand unless you feel it for yourself.
...My Fama told me she loved my Oma like that, Kumatora. And that I'd understand once I met someone important, too.
...Mhm. You're "firm and round," too, Nami. I can tell you get your own exercise.
Mhm. I can compliment yours back, Nami. You're not coasting by on your figure.
...Don't take this the wrong way, Kumatora, but I'd rather not be your village's guest. Dealing with that sort of attention is just a nuisance.
...I'm sure "Tazmily" is a nice place, Kumatora, but no, thank you. Big crowds are just a pain, especially when they're focused on me.
...Kumatora, there are ghosts in your castle? Are you sure they're not visions created by some power source there?
...Can everyone see the "ghosts" in Osohe Castle, Kumatora? Our crew has some experience with supernatural visions.
...I have a trainee who's always been clumsy, Kyou. She's still managed to help by putting in her best effort.
...Not all of our pilots master the controls right away, Kyou. I have an apprentice pilot who probably wouldn't be much better on a bike.
..."We Sports," you said, Trainer? I was looking for natural landmarks. Are some of them played outdoors?
...I get enough exercise without "We Sports," Trainer. Is there some large natural area where they're played that I could visit?
...Let me clear up the "confusion," Sakura: I'm not an idol.
...Don't apologize, Sakura. But you're mistaken---I'm a real pilot.
I meant their teeth, Sakura---we learned that's where the germs are most concentrated. Not that they ever taught us about their "penises."
Until recently, I didn't even know men had those penis-things, Sakura. I really did mean their fangs---or what I thought were fangs.
...I'd like to hear a poem about nature, Hu Tao. As long as it's not souls returning to the earth.
...I don't want to hear funeral poems, Hu Tao. Earth has a lot of open landscapes, if you can think of something like that.
...Most men tower over us, Rouge. The way you talk about seduction...
Rouge, if I seduced a man myself...he could toss me across the room.

You mentioned "Promepolis," Heris?
...I lived in the city for a while. Having all those people around is just a nuisance.
...I don't like big crowds, Heris. Promepolis wouldn't be best for me.
...I'd definitely recommend you for maintenance over the Dread team, Heris. We could always use more hands, especially with your expertise.
...By the way, I agree with you, Heris. You'd belong in engineering. The girls there are just as young and could use a mentor.
...Being torn apart sounds exactly like what I know Earth for, Cagliostro.
...Our Earths might just be the same, Cagliostro. Tearing us apart is exactly what it wants.
...I'm sure you could apply your alchemy skills to engineering, Cagliostro. Most girls are trained on the job.
...If you're a fast learner, Cagliostro, then your alchemy study could come in handy as one of our engineers.
...The men I know have strong pride, Cagliostro. You may be asking too much of them.
...I don't know much about men, Cagliostro, but I don't think they like to submit.
I turned twenty recently. Some girls on the crew say I look older, mostly in the eyes.
I just had my twentieth birthday. Most girls on our crew are a little younger, and they say I seem a lot older. At least in personality.
That's right, Leon. It's dangerous to enter a planet's atmosphere in one without the right loadout.
Yes, Leon. They'd take a lot of custom parts to function near a planet's surface.
...Men seem to build mechs to handle all terrain. Is that why you've been struggling, Leon?
We had trouble with the men's mechs ourselves, Leon. Even our male pilot struggled his first time on land. Is their versatility the problem?

Leon...?
...It's enough distinction to mention the things you like. How you treat women.

Leon?
...I guess it's what separates people in general. How you treat them, and what you do with your time.

Leon?
...Sparring and exercise. Maybe you consider that part of your job, since it's training. But it helps me relax.

Leon?
...When I have the time, I like to go and train at our gym. I can let out some energy on top of staying fit.
We knew they were there, Leon. They were just some enemy race. I see a lot more of what makes us the same now.
We knew about men, Leon. At least, you were humanoid germs. I've learned a lot more about the "humanoid."
The same way I've treated you, Leon. I guess you could call it an arm's length, but you can still see a lot of someone there.
You're not any different from our prisoners, Leon. Maybe this feels cold, but it's just matter-of-fact.
...I just didn't know what to call it, Leon. I'd rather learn that. As for "pussy," I guess that's not any different here.
What's the real name, Leon? "Penis"? And I've probably heard "pussy" more than you have.
We've taken in girls who are nervous, Nanoko. But you might be better off in engineering.
Don't you like tinkering with machines, Nanoko? Engineering might be a better fit for you.
...Did anything look interesting when you came here, Noire? It was weird seeing a whole planet "terraformed."
How did Earth's landscape look to you, Noire? There were so many different environments, it was hard to survey it.
If your friend's willing to join us, Noire, I'd like to meet her. Being coordinated should translate to a Dread well enough.
Noire, your friend shouldn't have trouble with a Dread's controls if she can move well on her own. Can she meet us?
Cheryl, you were talking about the woods before. A forest sounds nice. Mejare doesn't have much land that can support that.

Mejare's not terraformed enough for forests. I'd like to see those woods you mentioned, Cheryl.
...People call me creepy, after all.
...Are you talking about a god, Cheryl? Or maybe fate? Our captain's a lot more religious than most of us. I just think we decide our own destinies.

Cheryl?
...Our captain has things like tarot cards and prayer beads. Even a shrine. But personally...all I really think is that fate is something we have control over.
Your homeworld sounds a lot like Earth's environment, Mr. Dunban. What are the sights there?
What about your planet, Mr. Dunban? It must be heavily terraformed by the sound of things.
I like warm meals with lean meats, Kumatora. Chicken soup is always good. It's filling, but not fattening.
...Anything hot and fueling, Kumatora. But it can't have too many calories. Something like...fish stew.
...You may not like what sticks, Kumatora. Our reg chief went from "Gascogne" to "Miss Gasco"---and she always corrects it.
...Careful what you wish for, Kumatora. Our reg chief always gets annoyed when we call her "Miss Gasco."
...You could say crewmates are closer than friends, Kumatora. Or maybe I'm just overthinking what a friend has to be...
...Maybe not friends, Kumatora, but---crewmates are like family. I guess that's a special enough relationship...

Kumatora?
It's...weird. A lot of crewmates aren't really friends. But---if you risk your lives for each other, maybe that's something more.

I've never played an instrument, Kumatora.
...But I was a vocalist.
...It's not an instrument, Kumatora, but I used to sing.

There's not a lot of animals on Mejare, Kumatora. Most girls keep birds as pets.
...So I'd say a bluebird.
I guess...bluebirds, Kumatora. Birds are some of the only animals we see back home.
Kumatora...I was on my own by the time I was fourteen. So---I had to learn on my own.
Kumatora---by the time I was old enough for that sort of thing, my parents were gone. So other girls showed me...
I---had to figure that out for myself, Kumatora. My parents were busy, and then, when I was fourteen...they were gone.
"PSI" conjuring up hot springs might actually be linked. But really...I just wish I was strong. Maybe---not needing any sleep.
If the Paksis is related to PSI at all, then PSI is related to hot springs. But to answer your question...I wish my body was stronger. Like, I could keep going forever.
...That's a weird question from someone with superpowers, Kumatora. But by that definition, I have them, too---the power that fuels a Vandread.

Your PSI is a superpower, Kumatora.
...Which means I sort of have one, too. A Vandread's fusion goes beyond all reason.
...Money and health tend to go together, Kumatora. What makes you ask?
...The main thing about having money is not having to worry about your well-being. Are you asking from experience, Kumatora?
That's a---weird question, Kumatora. Especially your choice of mushroom...given what I've heard about those tubes men have.
...Kumatora, that's---very specific. Don't those tubes of men---don't they look like mushrooms?
...That sounds like something you've thought about a lot, Kumatora. Our lives only have meaning because of what we do with them.
...Has that choice troubled you, Kumatora? If you're sealed away forever, that's the same as being dead.
..."Stalker"? You keep smiling at ~player.ifMale(him|her)~.
..."Stalker" is not a word you just toss at someone.
Most girls on Mejare keep birds, Arle. There's not a lot of space for much else in a residence craft.
Birds are the most common pet back home, Arle. It's a fleet nation, so the other animals can't really roam free.
...I like time in our jacuzzi. I can do that myself.
...We have a hot tub, Senko. It helps me relax.
...I'd hate to have to make my own coffee.
...Our coffeemaker.
...When I was a girl, I hated being scolded, Senko. It sort of feels helpless.
I guess you mean being hurt, Senko, but scolding always frustrated me. If they hit me, at least I'd feel like I paid for it.

So you're not any kind of Earthling, Senko?
...I wasn't sure if I should have a tail.
...You're not from this planet, either, Senko? I was worried there were more kinds of humans we didn't know about.
...I mostly like being alone.
I don't do things for others very much, Senko. I don't expect it in return.
...Eight hundred? You might still be alive in my time.
...How long is your lifespan? If it goes for millennia, then you might still exist in frontier times---!
Our captain does keep some shrines, Senko. Maybe that's the reason we've survived.
There aren't many shrines on Mejare, Senko, but our captain has some. Some things have certainly felt like divine help.

state.text: You...sound a lot like my mother. What made her happiest was making a home for me and my Oma.

case.state: ...My mother said things like that. That she wanted to give our family a safe place to come home to.

That's your---spot, I guess?
...Mine's higher up.

Y-your tail?
...For me, it's my breasts.
...Have you been trying to study it? Leavings things to "magic" means they might never develop.
Our ship's fusion core has performed things that seem like "magic." I want to believe there's explanations...
...It sends the wrong message to have your weapon drawn.
...I could point my ring at you, to give you an idea.
...When I was a girl, Galatea, I performed songs to advertise my parents' development projects. I was too young to really understand critics.
I used to be an idol, Galatea, for my family's work. I was all over billboards and tabloids...I'm sure critics made fun of me, but I was really young.
...Do you want to be known only for your strength, Leonie? If I were hiring a mercenary, I'd want someone fair and efficient.
...If you name yourself after your strength, Leonie, you might get into more fights than it's worth. Maybe try something more about justice.
...I know you mean physical things, Arueshalae, but I feel like I've lost parts of myself over time.
...Do you only mean physically, Arueshalae?

I was once nearly killed, Arueshalae, and I dreamed I got the chance to speak to my mother again.
...If it was a dream.
That's easy. A few of my pilots and I all shared the same bad dream a while ago---some red light that killed us and destroyed our ship.
"Change"...I always get stuck in a cycle of wanting bigger breasts and remembering how much of a pain they'd be.
...Not in a good way, Fina. It was me and the gang I used to run with. And we'd hassle girls like that, make them do things...that's how I joined.
Our quartermaster likes it, Fluttershy. She uses cards to break in rookies who aren't behaving themselves.

This is the planet my ancestors came from, Fluttershy. And they used to live together with men here.
...I guess some of them were men.
...This planet, Gwen. At least in my time. They've sent out fleets of intelligent drones to harvest our organs.
...When I was little, I performed onstage as an idol, Gwen. It helped advertised my parents' terraforming projects.
...When you join a pirate group, Gwen, it sort of becomes your whole identity. You can't just go back to being a civilian.
...That'd feel over the top, Gwen. Like you're trying to form a connection that isn't there...
...Flying helps me feel like I'm in control of things, Heris. Exercise is kind of like that, too. That there's always room to improve.
I never liked trying my luck, Mr. Raynor. I saw girls on the street who did this a lot, and ended up selling themselves or nearly losing fingers. I just fought it out.
...A few scramble orders have gone out while I was in the shower, Joey. Sometimes there wasn't time to throw anything on.
...I feel like that's for other people to say, Joey. But if I had to guess, they might say wearing my headpiece.
...Anything that'd make me strong, Joey. Like the kinds of heroes that can take a bullet and keep standing. And don't need anyone's help...
...A lot of girls don't remember me from when they were young, Joey, but I used to be an idol. Sometimes I sing on our choir.
...Snacks are a bad habit, Joey. I only eat at mealtime.
...I don't have a whole lot of experience, Joey. It's hard to say. Maybe...someone who can take care of themselves.
Mejare is a fleet nation, Lucina, but I lived on the planet's surface for a while. It was terraformed to look like here, just with lots of craters.
...For a while, Nami, we thought any male ship was dangerous. We wouldn't board without spraying antiseptic and wearing spacesuits.

Nami?
...I like how my butt's developed. I had to do most of that myself.
...My good side's my backside, Nami. That's because it's all muscle.

Miss Robin?
...Mejare is an "empire" with a bruised ego. It's spent generations on fleet ships---even the men have terraformed Tarak.
...You're better off as a virgin than trying to force it with the wrong person, Nanoko.
...I don't really think about that sort of thing, Rouge. Pearls are a nice shape, without being too distracting.
...Has your friend tried painting, Rouge? I've seen the men on our ship create art like that---even write poems.
I mostly like to exercise, Rouge. Men seem to like making art, if your friend hasn't tried that.

I don't see why anyone would have a problem with that, Shantae.
...I'm kind of the same way. I can't just sit still for long.
The best thing a wish could do is make peace between Tarak and Mejare...as well as Earth. But it would never be that easy.
...I've never really fallen in love with anyone, Takatoshi. Maybe it's because I haven't known myself well enough.
That's awfully vague, Mr. Tobias. There was the time I fought a Harvester machine inside a comet, at Christmastime.
...I don't have any Earth money, Wikipe-tan. Our captain says it's bad business to deal with money in the first place.

I heard about that rule, Y'shtola, yes.
...To be honest, it's one of the reasons I came. If it's true, I'm bound to learn something.
...I can't really think of anything to buy, Yusuke. There's basic supplies we need, but you shouldn't go out of your way for us.
...I give myself tasks to stay focused, Estelle. I never really thought about the opposite.
Most girls I know just fixate on breasts, Elphaba. For me...wrapping around someone's back, maybe. Feeling them shift with you...
...I think everyone looks better with a little tone, Elphaba. Male or female. It shows they take care of themselves.

Arle?
...We were thrown into space, but that's let us see other colonies. Mejare was cut off from them for a long time.
...It took us some time, Arle, but we've lasted the better part of a year exactly like that. And there's been an enemy on our tail the whole time.
We haven't found any mermaid colonies, Arle. If we did, it'd probably be the result of some horrible Earth experiment...
...No one's really sure where our fusion core came from, Mr. Colress. Some people think it's from another universe---it's taken us across ours.
...How much do you take care of your own health, Miss Mercy? You look good, but working out always makes me feel better.
...A lot of the girls I used to know just sort of---groped each other, Miss Mercy. It wasn't for me. It felt pointless.
...I don't like crowds, Miss Mercy. Especially if the attention is on me. One other person is enough.
...I don't have the best experience with that, Miss Mercy. I used to just let them do whatever they wanted...it didn't really feel like I was a part of it.
...From what I can tell, men are very proud, Tsukasa. They don't want to admit their feelings. You might have to show yours.
We don't have this kind of scenery back on Mejare, Panty. It's all fleet ships. I'll see what it's like to swim against the waves.
...That'd be a luxury, Ibuki---to afford a band for an evening. We have a whole event staff for finding ways to entertain everyone.
...I sang as an idol when I was younger, Ibuki, if that counts. My voice has changed a lot since then.

I don't usually join in when the crew has pizza, Dwight.
...Maybe one slice if it's got full tomatoes.
...I don't have anything like that, Dwight. That's why I can't stand waiting around. Nothing makes me feel better except doing something.
...You can walk proud with that, Lyralei. What I like is that butts can be earned. Boobs are just luck, and you lose them if you work too hard.
I helped my Oma plant a lot of trees down on Mejare's surface, Lyralei. This planet's nature is incredible.
...Shaving's harder in this time, isn't it? There must not be any lasers or gel. I like a clean look, Lyralei, but I understand.
A lot of girls on Mejare shave, Lyralei. The fashion is tight, skimpy clothes, and hair poking out would look stupid.
...I've tried yoga, Lyralei, but I hate just holding a position like that. I'd rather be moving.
...Can't you tell if you have a soul or not, Lyralei?
...There aren't many plants on Mejare in the first place, Lyralei. We only brought ones good for humans.
...Birds are the only pet a lot of us have had back home, Lyralei. So I'd say a bluebird.
...Like I said, May, I'm from another planet. It was settled by Earth people, but it took years to get there.
...Isn't there a fast blue one where you live, May? It flies around like a Dread. I'd probably like it.
...I don't miss being judged onstage, so a smaller event sounds good to me, May. But you know yourself better.
You can dance if you want to, May. It'll be some extra practice watching a moving target.
...I came here, didn't I, Kaz? I still want to look good. And I'd like to think I do.
...I used to think like that, Kaz. But I've decided that whatever happens, I'll always do whatever I can about it.
...Exercising, mostly. And then following it with a bath. If your body feels good, Kaz, it helps your mind.
...I think that's something everyone goes through with their parents, Kaz. Just---realizing they're not perfect.
...I think making yourself stronger is always worth the effort, Syrenne.
From the girls I've been with, Syrenne, they just wanted a body to touch. So if you're OK with being that, they mean it.
...When a hot spring popped up on our ship, Syrenne, the first thing the crew did is all jump in at once. You don't have to ask.
My crewmate told me about it, Neptune. Apparently the Paksis is linked to certain points in spacetime---so we took a chance.
You can't really shower by yourself on a ship, Neptune. There's over a hundred girls aboard. Some sheltered rookies do get nervous their first time.

Suzuya?
...B. They say girls with B have a harder time fitting in with people.

Eichi?
...By the time I was old enough to shop at malls, I'd soured on the idea. If the crowd's not too big, I'd like to see the building, at least.
Piloting is pretty fast-paced, Mitama, so you may not have been a good fit.
...Even if you have combat experience, Mitama, pilots have to jump at scramble orders. There's no time to finish your writing first.
Our ship's core seems to be linked to this era somehow, Mitama. It created a wormhole for us to travel through. Is the "Dragon's Gate" like that?
...I think this time and place may have some significance, Mitama. Our Paksis core was able to transport us here. Your "gate" sounds similar.
...I feel more alert than ever, Mitama. I'm surprised you're drifting off after that...
You're sleeping, Mitama? Cumming took the wind out of me for a moment, but now? I feel pumped.
...Is there nowhere you've been that you actually liked, Revy?
...It's not easy to move around on the surface, I guess. You really hate all the places you've visited, Revy?
...I only know a few men, Revy, but they've treated me like a comrade---or even a partner.
...You make it sound like men don't see us as people, Revy. They've gone out of their way to save my life.
...What were you trying to say, Revy? Men can't love or respect us?
...You'd be quite the asset on a boarding party, Revy. But that's the thing---they're not one-woman jobs.
...I'm sure you like working alone, Revy---as skilled as you might be. We need a lot more coordination.
...I figured you wouldn't want to make the jump from four members to over a hundred, Revy. You can't capture a ship all by yourself.
...Maria, did you mean that cloudy planet closer to the Sun? Maybe this isn't far from the frontier era, after all.
..."Venus" is one of the planets here, right, Maria? It's about Earth's size. I didn't think colonization was close to happening in this time...

condition.said: Happy birthday! I may not have one myself,

case.state: ...If you weren't born, Kora, were you cloned in some facility?
...Were you made in a factory, Kora? I've heard that men on Tarak reproduce like that...
...How many of those places you mentioned have you seen in person, Nagisa?
