...Do you mean my parents, Tomoko? That's...not an option for me. I see you're just being confrontational, like many girls your age.
..."Ask my moms." I wish I didn't understand what that meant. I guess I can't wrest any information from teenage angst.
...You remind me of some of my rookie pilots---young girls who see politeness as weakness. I can't ask my "moms."
You ought to have more confidence in yourself, Tomoko. I'm sure you're intelligent enough to beat me in a simple card game.
...It's such a sad display of cowardice to beg your opponents to go easy on you. Why not rise above me instead?
...Do you expect to get through life making such requests, Tomoko? That everyone should handicap themselves to make your life easier?
...Maybe if you believed in yourself, you would win this game outright and not have to make embarrassing pleas to strangers.
...I see. Why don't you tell me about "Japan," then?
...Maybe I need to adjust to your sense of humor. What are "Japan's" key features, then?
...If you were just joking, then you must be able to describe Japan properly. Go ahead.
"Japan"...well, if you live there, then tell me about it. Is it a large region of Earth? What is its culture and history?
...A likely story from a confrontational young girl. Would you have claimed it was a joke if I'd treated it as such?
...It's a common tactic of young girls backtrack on their remarks upon being criticized for them. I hope that's not what you're doing.
...From my first impressions of you, Tomoko, this seems more like backpedaling.
...A joke, or an attempt to pass off a poorly-received comment as humor?
...Mary, if you don't plan to take my questions seriously, then don't answer them.
...I see. You're more concerned with making a fool of me than having a conversation, which is common for girls your age in places like this.
...I'm not interested in the jokes of a snickering teenager, Mary. Either explain yourself properly, or don't address me.
For God's sake...I get enough difficult young girls on our squadron. I'm not going to beg for a proper explanation, Mary.
...Which means?
..."Sugma"? Well, explain it, then.
...I'd prefer you start with the words you used earlier, Mary, but go ahead. Explain that one.
...By your grin, I assume it means something immature. Well?
...Are you talking to me, Tomoko? If you're referring to being introverted, I understand that very well.
...Tomoko, are you still talking about being introverted? I was shy when I was younger, too, but you can't just feel sorry for yourself all day.
...Tomoko, stop complaining about your introversion. I had to get over mine, as well, and it's no one else's responsibility.
...Stop bringing up your introversion if you're just going to complain, Tomoko. You can't expect others to accommodate you.
...What did you just call me, Tomoko? "Koo-hai"? I still don't understand "otoh-may."
..."Koo-hai"? One confusing Earth word replaced with another...talking to this girl is exhausting.
...Explain what "otoh-may" is before throwing new words at me, Tomoko. "Koo-hai"?
...What does "koo-hai" mean? Actually, start with the "otoh-may" word you used earlier.
...A "cognitohazard." If Earth had weaponized the very idea of a phrase, it would've unleashed that upon our crew by now.
...I'll believe the existence of "cognitohazards" when I see them. Surely Earth would've attacked us with one before sending Harvest fleets.
...A girl in possession of "cognitohazards" would be in the upper ranks of Earth's military, targeting our ship, not playing strip poker.
...I should be grateful Earth's fleets have no weaponry as absurd as "cognitohazards." Harvest cubes can be shot down.
...It's no issue, Amy. As I said, I'd be happy to answer any of your questions. Just...individually.
...Thank you, Amy. I don't begrudge your curiosity...as long as you pace yourself.
...It's fine, Amy. I'm accustomed to young girls giving overexcited reports---and to weathering the storm, so to speak.
...I don't mind indulging your curiosity, Amy. You're very interesting to me, as well---so we should take our time.
With---a few boys? You say that so casually---!
A few---boys? I---didn't think you'd be so quick to describe your sexual experience...
A few---w-wait, aren't boys...male children? You're young, too, but---!
A-Amy? I---was only implying that you may have learned about men, not had---sex with them! Like it's nothing...
So your advice is...to do strength training.
...I see. So you just wanted to tell me about her fetishes, and that strength training will build strength.

So...you're saying I should exercise.
...Your friend must be strong if she can let monsters assault her for her own masochism.
...I was about to say that our closest analog to monsters would be letting men beat me up. But your advice is to do basic strength training.
...Your "bits"? That's such childish wording...I can't believe men left you unscathed. How early do men and women start dating on this planet?
...What kind of childlike view of sex is that? You sound so naive about it, but you've dated men from an early age...?
...Being the pirates we are, we don't have many books on our ship. But I have enjoyed studying the books on fighter ships I was given when I became a pilot.
I used to read more when I was a girl...that's not an option for a pirate. But our ship does have books on Dread fighters that I enjoy.
Slow down, Amy. Are you saying that Earth women sometimes splice their eggs and have daughters, as Mejarians do? And that practice is looked down upon?
Sports...when I dropped out of school, I managed to survive by streetfighting...
That's the same as asking us what our talents are, isn't it? Our captain claims I learned how to pilot Dread fighters faster than any girl she's met.
I never thought I had much talent for anything as a girl...but in a flying competition, I could win. I've been told I'm the Magno Family's fastest-learning pilot.
I discovered my aptitude for piloting when I joined our pirate crew. In some sort of flight competition, I'd have a good shot.
...I used to streetfight, but I have no formal training there. In a flying competition, our crew agrees I'm our most talented pilot.
...I just arrived on this planet, so I'm not aware of any films here. Mejarian film is usually propaganda celebrating the empire's glory.
Mejare was only colonized about a century ago, so our history is limited. And its version of Earth's history has men scrubbed from it...
Historical figures...after learning that Mejare changed many historical figures to women in its version of history, I'm not sure who to respect.
Ancient Earth ruins would be quite interesting...and I could fly us both to them in no time. You'd just have to direct me.
I would say Earth's first development of interstellar space travel. It was what led to the colonization of the galaxy, and thus my homeworld.
Mejare has more of a colonization story than a creation one...saying how we were led away from Earth, and men's oppression, by the angel Gynos.
...Are there giant frogs on Earth that attack the populace? You mentioned that so offhandedly...
...I can see how explosion magic might lead to damage. But if your villagers can create magical golems, why not study that, as well?
...What is your definition of "monster"? Earth's intentions with the Harvest are quite monstrous, and I've helped destroy its motherships.
...The most monstrous ships our crew has faced are the Harvest's motherships---many times the size of the Nirvana. But what do you call a monster?
Our quartermaster, Gascogne, likes to use poker to socialize with crew members. As a result, I've played this game a lot...just without the stripping.
...Are you saying stripping naked will be humiliating? I find losing to a man to be far more so.
...Losing to a man would be quite humiliating indeed, Guzma. I don't plan to show you my body.
...Are you saying being stripped naked like this is humiliating? I find losing to a man to be far more so.
...Losing to a man would be quite humiliating indeed, Guzma. I don't plan on doing so.
...If a Dread fighter can count as a weapon, then many of our crew considers me our best pilot, the captain included.
...Would you include piloting in that question, Brock? I've been told that no girl on our crew learned to pilot a Dread fighter faster than I did.
...Discounting my Dread ship, I've been complimented on my aim with a laser ring. It is a woman's weapon of choice.
Are you only including men's weapons? I've been praised for my accuracy with a laser ring, but that's a woman's gun...
...That sounds like the offer of a pervert who wouldn't mind degrading himself for a woman if he lost.
...And what would we get out of that deal that would be worth your perversion?
That's quite a specific question, Yuelia...I've never felt worthy of the praise our captain and quartermaster give me, even when missions are successful.
My Fama took me to see films and plays when I was younger. There were sweet stories, as well as more violent ones...like "Ovule, Slayer of Men."
Some might describe me as quite the talented pilot for my age. Our ship's eleven-year-old nurse, Paiway, is a fast learner, as well.
...My subordinate pilots have a bigger habit of creating misunderstandings. One of the men has accidentally stumbled in on girls changing.
There isn't any room for animals on a pirate ship. Even when I was a civilian, pets weren't common...probably because there are male ones.
...I don't begrudge civilian girls for accessorizing, but it only hinders a pirate's readiness for combat. My headpiece is at least secure and unintrusive.
Hm. That's a perfect description of our newest pilot---a young man named Hibiki. It's incredible how his recklessness never fails him.
...I admit I can struggle with teaching less talented pilots how to handle a dogfight. A good teacher has a love for people more than the skill itself.
I haven't been fishing---my parents were wealthy, so we had easy access to food. But they did take me to the plains to run around as a girl...
I expected men to be mindless beasts, like I was taught they were as a girl. Imagine my surprise when I found myself fighting trained soldiers.
Our quartermaster tends to stick pilots who can't get along with others into our regisystem, moving crates. It's purposely a job beneath them.
...Our captain has called me "hardheaded" for displaying that exact behavior. A lot of my pilots tend to be strong-willed like that.
...The stress of constant battles can take its toll on pirates, especially girls who joined eager to prove themselves. Morale is a volatile thing.
...I don't have any family. Not except for our crew...just as my parents made mistakes, my pilots do, as well, but I still value them.
...My crew is my family. We have our share of troublemakers, but nothing that has destroyed our camaraderie.
...That's how many of our upper-ranking pilots would describe me. The newer girls are too afraid to see how reserved I am.
...That's very personal, Yuelia. I've listened to myself over a loved one before, but I was young and foolish then...I guess that's how you learn about yourself.
I try to avoid sweets. They're empty calories and can cause mood swings---pilots need both fitness and a clear mind.
...I tend not to see meals as a source of pleasure. Fish, rice, and vegetables constitute most of my food for the nutritional value.
No one on our ship has much opportunity to wear tailored clothes. Besides, having to fit into a pre-made bodysuit helps keep me in shape.
...I myself try to be more caring around a girl we took in from Pluto---she's an outsider. She's opened up around me a bit, as well.
...Many girls who ended up as pirates would rightfully claim to be unfortunate. As a crew, though, we've had our share of improbable successes.
...I've had to coach a few pilots whose confidence fell apart when it came time for actual raids rather than simulations. Talent doesn't equal courage.
We have some men prisoner aboard our ship, Yuelia. Circumstances have required us to make them part of the crew, much to our dismay.
It wasn't by choice that a man become part of our Dread team, Yuelia. I resented him at first, but his mech provides several tactical advantages.
I was told all sorts of lies. Mejare's government has a vested interest in keeping us at war with men.
...I'm sure "ECHOs" are useful, but I'm quite satisfied with my current work tools. And my headpiece, for that matter.
You can't remember? ...I'd like to forget my first time, but I could never imagine doing so...
...It sounds more like there is a stigma here against same-sex cell combination. You and your family would be welcome on Mejare.
Based on the ships I've seen, Earth is capable of anything Mejare is, including egg-splicing. I guess using men and women's cells is just ingrained here.
...Earlier, you were trying to convince me to use an ECHO. Yet you only have yours by coincidence? Make up your mind.
...I understand. I could never afford the tools I use, either---our crew has accumulated supplies through raids.
...Don't think I'm criticizing your scavenging for tools, Gaige. Our crew does the same thing, raiding military outposts.
Raids are nothing to be excited about, Gaige. Much of our technological advantage is lost on foot, and the chances of death are actually higher.
...By "raids," I mean raids on foot. Those missions are much more dangerous, especially for a pilot crew.
...It's one thing to endanger yourself, Gaige. I have a team of pilots that I need to keep alive each mission.
..."To Hell with danger." It's easy for a lone raider to say that, but not one who's responsible for the lives of a dozen girls.
...In the "days of war"? War is still very much alive, Brock. "Antiques" refer to the primitive mechanical weaponry of the past, like yours.
...If you have a colleague who specializes in energy weaponry, you would do well to respect them, yes. It represents modern technology.
...It's not "overkill" to respond to a space attack fleet with fighter crafts of one's own, Brock. Maybe Earth has hidden that technology, too...
Men's bodies are quite bulky themselves, so your preference for angular shapes isn't surprising. Women are slender and build ships to match that...
Men are stronger and bulkier than women, so it only makes sense that your weapon and craft design would follow suit. Dreads are much smaller than Vanguards.
...A pickaxe? That isn't even a weapon---a man using an unwieldy mining tool for its raw strength is quite appropriate, as well.
...My home planet would consider men too dangerous to be kept alive. I know better now than to treat them like that.
...I hope you don't decide who's worthy of slaughter from the words of others. Mejare would put all men in that category.
...There isn't much to the story, Cynthia. Mejare sees women's history on Earth as a primordial afterthought.
...Mejare is more concerned with painting men as savage animals than presenting accurate history, Cynthia. I would look elsewhere.
...Mejare is not as free a society as it claims, Cynthia. It was founded upon separating from men, and its accounts of history reflect that.
...I'm sure interstellar travel is not afforded to every citizen on Earth, Cynthia. Your government does not want unmonitored contact with colonies.
...The world reborn...I don't like the sound of that. Maybe some sort of site for the Harvest's organ preservation.
Over a thousand years...Mejare is only a century-old civilization. "Japan" is a region of Earth, right? What sets it apart from the others?
..."Japan's" capital. I've read that Earth was once divided into many smaller regions...if that's true, can you tell me more about Japan itself?
1,075 years...as "Japan's" capital. It's hard to believe a single small region of Earth has more history than all of Mejare...can you tell me more?
...The "portal between worlds"? That's a fanciful name for a nature area...or are you actually serious about "your world" versus Earth?
...It wouldn't be like your archaeological studies. Mejare's history as a civilization is short---some elders have been alive for its entire existence.
Mejare's history is brief enough that some first-generation colonists are still alive. I'm not sure if you prefer searching for clues to ancient times.
...From what I understand, Earth's history is very old. There must be countless examples of revisionism to vilify an enemy...
...Is it human nature to define an "enemy" and seek its destruction? Mejare with men, and Earth with its colonists...I've come to respect the former.
...If isolating an "enemy" is part of human nature, then surely forming bonds must be another part. All men were once my enemy...
Even trade is a luxury many planets lack. Mejare and Tarak, for instance, had lost all contact with other colonies.
I'd like to see Earth's colonies have even that small level of contact...maybe Mejare and Tarak could find peace.
...You'll have to forgive me. We've encountered people who hold sacrificial rites for the sake of Earth being "reborn."
...Our crew has learned to regard a world's "tradition" with skepticism. Earth has convinced them to self-sacrifice for its renewal...
...If you have no need of it, then a textbook would prove fascinating. I've certainly pored over the anatomy textbook we discovered...
I don't mean to take your school supplies from you...but if it's no trouble, then a history text would make a nice side to our book on sexual reproduction.
...What do you expect me to see you as when you take that as a personal insult? Don't define yourself on a race of sworn enemies.
...If you're going to play the victim, then I have nothing more to say to you. Hating men used to be my duty as a Mejarian until I met them for myself.
...If you see an attack on your beliefs as on attack on you, then nothing I say will make a difference. Peace only comes when you try to understand your enemy.
...Who your culture chooses to brand an enemy and slaughter is not your identity, Aella. I once saw any word in men's favor as an attack on my womanhood.
You aren't listening. Don't you realize I'm saying I once had enemies who turned out to be reasonable? We're repeating ourselves.
...Should I recount how I once thought men were impossible to reason with, as well? This is going nowhere.
...You'd be surprised who is capable of being reasoned with. I can only hope my fellow Mejarians prove more easily persuaded.
For God's sake...we're talking in circles. If I thought I couldn't reason with my enemies, I would now be without some of my closest allies.
I hope you're doing your part for the present as you study the past, then. Earth has undoubtedly vilified its colonists in recent history.
I wouldn't be surprised if Earth has recently altered accounts of space colonization to paint itself as the home of "true" humans, Cynthia.
I'm hoping our crew can set a precedent for men and women coexisting, then. Our mutual destruction is assured otherwise.
...Well, Mejarians believe men are diseased, and Tarakkians believe women eat them. We'll both be killed if we can't achieve peace.
It doesn't surprise me. I'm inclined to agree with my captain on this matter---"legend" and "tradition" are convenient excuses for the indecisive.
These are people who sacrifice themselves for a false promise, all in the name of "tradition." It's sad to watch someone refuse to take hold of their own fate.
That's my point, Erufuda. You would keep your weight down if you engaged with any particular exercise beyond the surface level.
That's because you keep changing your routine, Erufuda. Your body can't find any rhythm to what you're doing, and you can't increase the intensity properly.
...I never criticized Jura's butt, Erufuda. Regardless, softness can be achieved by relaxing muscles. It's not an excuse to be overweight.
It's a misconception to equate fat with softness. Muscle is only hard when tensed. In any case, Jura's butt is not my concern.
There are many girls who hold the same misconceptions about building muscle, Erufuda. It doesn't harden your body unless you flex them.
...It's nothing, Jolyne. Just a family memento...has a relative given you anything?
...It was a gift from family, Jolyne. That's all...do you have something similar?
...Are you saying you're a target for some hostile organization, PA-15? Well, you may have disarmed yourself, but I have not.
You only have yourself to blame if you're attacked after unloading your weapon, PA-15. I still have mine, if providing assistance is feasible.
"Sangvis"? ...I happen to be armed myself, in case this enemy of yours attacks indiscriminately.
"Sangvis"? You have an enemy, and you've disarmed yourself? Now I'm regretting having done the same...
...I didn't realize you were the target of hostiles, PA-15. I should retrieve my laser ring before this situation worsens.
...PA-15, are you expecting an enemy attack? I shouldn't have disarmed myself---but at least my laser ring doesn't require ammunition.
...Thank you, Lucy. It's the crowds and the alcohol I don't like---I'd gladly sit down with you one-on-one, drinking coffee.
...I appreciate that, Lucy. If you're willing to talk individually, I'm sure I could learn a lot from you. I'll just order coffee...
That's not unbelievable, Lucy. I'm descended from Earth colonists---the genetics for blue hair had to come from somewhere.

condition.saying: Kingdom of Fiore has a queen

case.state: You're friends with royalty, Lucy? ...Technically speaking, I may be, as well. Though he wasn't aware of it at first...
...No, Orendi, I haven't. I've seen what becomes of a race who augments themselves beyond recognition.
Unnecessary augmentation would compromise my humanity, Orendi. I've seen it play out among others---they're left unable to reproduce, or even live peacefully.
That's a fruitless pursuit of power, Orendi. I've witnessed a planet fall into madness because its inhabitants traded their humanity away.
...I just was a girl when my family dealt with the media, Pyrrha. It wasn't really my responsibility.
...I can't provide much advice for media appearances as an adult, Pyrrha. I was just the daughter of a famous couple. I had to wear a dress and smile.
...I only know how to deal with publicity as a child, Pyrrha. I smiled for the camera...any photos of me now are in a raid suit, behind a mask.
...It wasn't me they were covering, Pyrrha. It was my parents. They were scientists contracted to develop living systems.
...The press were covering my parents' work in urban development and energy conservation, Pyrrha. I was just a cute face to put on posters.
One bad decision will lead to more in an attempt to justify the first, Orendi. It occurs even with less serious issues than cybernetics.
Each indulgence makes it harder to control, Orendi. You don't need to observe cyber augmentation to see that.
..."Insta-health"? I've never heard of these things. But there is no treatment for a girl's death.
...Are you saying you have self-service first aid stations, Gaige? That's nice, but death is a real and irreversible threat.
...A pirate can't be picky with her food, Erufuda. But when we have them, I enjoy fish and wheat toast.
...Our food options are too limited to say I "can't live without" something in particular, Erufuda. But fish are a lean source of protein, and wheat toast for carbs.

...Shouko?
...I see. So this is some sort of condition...I should be the one apologizing, then.

...Shouko?
...So, you have a communication disorder, I take it. I'm sorry for being rude earlier.
I was speaking to my second-in-command, Cynthia. She's elsewhere in the building, and I want us to be aware of each others' safety.
My deputy ensign pilot is at another table, Cynthia. Her safety is my responsibility, so I'm maintaining a comm line with her.
...What is it you protect your subjects from? Is that related to "macro management"?
...I'm not sure what you mean by "macro management." Is that setting policy, or is it related to what you protect your people from?
That's right. As you open up to others, you start to change without even realizing it. I recently met a colleague I hadn't seen in a while, and she couldn't believe it when I laughed.
...I think I've become better for it, Laevatein, and so could you. I surprised one of my fellow officers the other day just by giggling.
It was her idea to come here, Cynthia. I agreed, both to ensure her safety and because it was an opportunity to learn about our ancestors' homeland.
...She caught wind of this place and asked me to come along with her, Cynthia. She knows I'll protect her without gossiping later---and for me, I can learn about Earth.
It's not my goal to humiliate them, Erufuda. I try to be terse---their personal laziness endangers their crewmates.
Dressing-downs aren't meant to shame girls, Erufuda. All I need to say is that they're being unfair to their teammates by not taking their own health seriously.
...I don't hound them about it, Erufuda. I give advice when they ask for it. In turn, I trust them to tell me when they have concerns.
...I meant that my pilots can ask me for diet advice, Erufuda, not that I force it upon them. I trust them to make clear any issues they have with my leadership.
I don't personally measure them, Erufuda, but we have regular weigh-ins and fitness tests. No one wants to be the "chubby girl."
I don't organize them, Erufuda, but we have shipwide weigh-ins. Being measured in front of the others naturally leads to girls judging each other.
Our crew was thrown across the galaxy in an instant thanks to a wormhole---is that what you mean? You've created a stable one?
...There's a cross-dimensional portal where you live, in a stable state? That's incredible technology--- wormholes are short-lived!
That was my personal communicator, Miss Jessie. I came here with one of my ensign pilots, and we need to stay in contact in case danger arises.
I'm having one of my ensign pilots report to me, Miss Jessie. She's at a different table, and I need to monitor her safety.
We have a history of conflict with Earth, Miss Jessie. While this doesn't appear to be the Earth we know, we can't rule out potential threats.
Earth is a known aggressor against our ship and our homeworld, Miss Jessie. The chance of danger may be slight, but it isn't worth the risk.
It's not this game I'm wary of, Miss Jessie---it's Earth. In our time, it's become hostile to colonists like us, and that may still be true here.
Much of our crew is the same way, Laevatein. We became sick of that hypocrisy when it led to power failure in their homes.
I understand the feeling, Laevatein. Our pirate group was formed because girls were sick of the double-talk from authority, especially when it left many of us homeless.
It wasn't a sister I lost, but...I understand how you feel, Laevatein. Most of the Magno Family has lost loved ones.
Laevatein...I can relate to losing a loved one, at least. My parents. A lot of our crew has gone through something like that.
...It's funny you say that, Chazz. An accident with our energy core recently gave us the ability to fuse our Dread fighters with one of the men's Vanguard mechs. We call them Vandreads.
...Actually, Chazz, our Dreads can combine with a male Vanguard mech to produce the much more powerful "Vandreads." We've already seen that Earth also possesses this technology.
Fusing ships together is indeed technology we never considered, Chazz---until recently. Our combined Vandread mechs have been our crew's most powerful weapons.
Fusing Dreads and Vanguards into powerful Vandreads is exactly what's allowed us to survive, Chazz. Earth has a Paksis like we do---"XYZ Machines" might be your term for the same technology.
...I'm sure you're proud of them, Chazz. There isn't any need for hostilities with the Earth of this time. It seems like it's an in earlier age, anyway.
Neither of us has even seen the other's mechs, Chazz. The Earth of this time doesn't even seem capable of space combat.
You shouldn't underestimate your opponents, Chazz. In fact, this Earth seems more primitive than the one we're currently battling. It might be best for you to avoid conflict.
It's possible to combine women's DNA via machine, Chazz. Whatever "wieners" are, they're not necessary.
..."Wieners"? Women's DNA can make children, Chazz. We just need to fuse egg cells artificially.
...Yes, it is, Deimos. Mejare's firearms tend to be compact energy weapons.
I understand that the kinetic weapons men use are usually larger than ours, Deimos. It fires energy beams.
Even two women can disagree on how to raise a child. My Oma sounds a lot like your father, Adrien---I didn't always find her easy to understand.
...Adrien, you sound like you had a bad relationship with your father. My Oma and I didn't understand each other much, either. Even with another woman around.
...I appreciate that. Even on my homeworld, I'm...not so good with this sort of thing.
...Thank you. Even with other girls, my sexual experience is...limited.
...Men don't have any shame, do they, Adrien? You're gossiping about me while you let that "semen" drip down your chest.
...Do men have no interest in cleaning themselves, Adrien? You could wipe that semen fluid off yourself before chatting about me.
I'm not the one preparing my food, Erufuda. We have a cooking team who enjoy seasoning and decorating dishes for us.
I probably wouldn't bother seasoning it myself, Erufuda, but our cooks do. They take pride in making our food appealing.
They're have some flair, Erufuda---it's a point of pride for the cooking team. Like the reg staff, they want to provide the best for the Nirvana's pilots.
...I'm not sure if you're just making fun of me at this point. I know mass is conserved in the universe, but beyond that...I'm not a scientist, let alone a portal one.
The same weight...? This is already hard to believe, Erufuda. I'm no scientist--- maybe our chief engineer Parfet could relate that to conservation of mass somehow.
...You're Gwen, right? Thank you. I was born on Mejare, one of Earth's foreign colonies.

..."Gwen," right?
...My homeworld is planet Mejare. It was settled during the old frontier era. I guess you were trying to make me feel welcome here.

I appreciate the compliments, Gwen, but they're not necessary.
...I'm not from this planet. Earth settlers founded my homeworld a few generations ago.
...You don't need to flatter me, Gwen. I come from the colony world Mejare, in a far-off sector. My ancestors lived here.
...Whispering to your friends. That's typical for a schoolgirl, at least.
...Maybe you are a normal student, if the first thing you do is huddle with friends.
...Your "Book of Friends"? Friendship's not something you just write down...you might never see me again. But I can do it.

What's up, Shouko?
...If you really think we've become friends that fast, then sure. But I can't stay here.
...If you want to show off better, twist around and look us in the eye.
...It's hard to make eye contact when your best side is the back, but it goes a long way.
...Nothing about my body feels wrong now, it's just---something else.
What's going on---? It's not even a physical feeling...
Voices in my head---voices that aren't the Paksis. I can't make out what they're saying...
T-this---isn't like what I've felt before. The words were always clearer...
Ugh...n-normally I might see visions of people. This time, it's---their absence.
I-I can't explain it, but these aren't normal visions. There, people appear---not vanish.
Some voices are familiar, but---distorted? Like it's not really them...
