...You speak as if having "superlative prowess" is normal. You shouldn't look down on others for their biology.
...Is that how those on Tamaran assess others, on the possession of "superlative prowess"? I hope Earth hasn't taught you that.
...In human culture, it is considered rude to judge others based on factors outside of their control, such as "superlative prowess."
...I should've known a floating alien girl would look down upon those without superpowers. Humanity thrives on overcoming those odds.
...There isn't much to see, Starfire.
...It's standard flight armor, Starfire. Nothing worth inspection.
...You were interested in my armor?
...I wouldn't expect an alien with "superlative prowess" to be fascinated by human armor.
...At once. To do otherwise would be cowardly.
...Is that a common strategy in the games you've played, Starfire? It sounds underhanded to me.
...It's one item of clothing, isn't it? I didn't depressurize my armor and try to count that.
Mmh...that should be obvious. Piecemeal removal is completely arbitrary.
Didn't you hear what I said? I am a human. A few centuries on another planet wouldn't change that.
...Are you implying that a few centuries away from Earth would change human anatomy, Miss Jessie? Evolution is much slower than that.
...Maybe if Mejare had a harsh climate, a few centuries apart would make us different from "modern humans," but the planet is terraformed.
Earth would have you believe Mejare and other colonists have devolved from "current humans," Miss Jessie, but I'm just like you.
"Extra"? Mejare prides itself on having extra beauty, and nothing more. I hope I can represent it well in that respect.
I can't claim to be an expert, Miss Jessie. Maybe you'll see a muscle in my rear that you lack---but Mejare's pride is in beautiful, human women.
Mejare's claim to fame is feminine beauty, Miss Jessie, not strange female anatomy. But maybe we have marks on our backsides that you don't.
I think you'll find Mejarian bodies to be quite normal, Miss Jessie, but hopefully very shapely. That is my homeworld's pride.
...I'm sorry? I don't understand what you're asking. Why would pirates have a particular accent?
...Could you repeat that, Fidget? Are you implying all pirates have the same accent?
..."Arr, Jim-lad"? Is that some sort of Earth stereotype about pirate women?
...What are you saying, Fidget? That I speak in too educated a fashion compared to most pirates?
...I'm not our ship's captain. And I have an eye decoration, as you can see...not that I understand what you mean.
...Our captain is an old woman, Fidget. With both of her eyes...I don't follow what you're saying.
...You're mistaken, Fidget. I'm a junior officer, not the captain...and I don't wear this headpiece because I'm a pirate.
...I lead our Dread team, not the whole ship. As for the eyepatch comment, I don't understand where you got that idea.
..."Parrot"? Is this a setup to an Earth joke?
...If this is setting up a joke, Fidget, maybe an Earth girl might have more context for it.
...I don't have a parrot. Nor a boat. Are you trying to make me laugh?
...My "parrot on the boat." That must be some sort of joking phrase on this planet.
Our "pirate captain" is an elderly woman named Magno Vivan, Fidget. And scurvy is a disease. The relation escapes me.
...Scurvy is a disease caused by Vitamin C deficiency. I don't see what that has to do with our captain, who I am not.
...I imagine a "scurvy dog" is a dog that's contracted scurvy. For the record, I am not the captain of our ship, nor the commander.
I command the Nirvana's Dread team, Fidget. That only makes me an officer, not captain---and what's that got to do with scurvy?
"Shanties"? ...Our crew actually is fond of singing on special occasions. "To Faraway Times" is a favorite.
...They're not necessarily "pirate" shanties, but singing is the one shipwide activity I enjoy participating in.
...You may be expecting otherwise, Fidget, but I actually do know some songs. The Magno Family enjoys singing during holidays.
...Are you familiar with "Spacy Spicy Love," Fidget? I actually sang a verse for the crew---much to everyone's surprise.
...If by "islands" you mean "military outposts." Largely the ones in low orbit.
We conduct our raids in space, where we frequently hold the advantage and can make quick escapes. Why islands?
...Why would we raid islands? Neither Mejare's nor Tarak's armies have much presence outside major cities.
...There isn't much "booty" to be found on uninhabited islands, Fidget. We target the military.
You...watch Mejare, Yuelia? I thought its empire would keep better track of satellites... unless you've conspired with them.
Mejare's problems are equal parts Earth's fault and our own, Yuelia. Have you set up some kind of undetected satellite?
What do you mean, you watch my homeworld? If you've slipped monitoring equipment into orbit without imperials noticing, I'm impressed.
Is that "watching" with Earth's resources, Yuelia? It's difficult even for us pirates to monitor what's happening on Mejare's surface from orbit.
Hm? Our main crafts are Dread fighters, which are built for speed and accuracy. Recent events have given me experience piloting mechs, as well.
I'm glad you asked, Yuelia. The Magno Family's fleet consists largely of Dread fighters, designed for quick raids and escapes.
I've piloted several crafts, Yuelia, but Dread fighters stand out. I took a liking to their speed and power, and I was among the fastest learners.
Oh, I enjoy piloting discussions. Dreads are my main areas of expertise, and mine is the fastest we have. I'm learning mechs at this time, as well.
...Leadership is overwhelming until you've seen and heard everything young girls can throw at you. I was given the job to be more level-headed.
...You may not believe it, Yuelia, but I used to be much more aggressive. I was thrust into a command role to make me more mature.
Being responsible for a Dread team's worth of girls makes your own problems seem small by comparison. It's calmed me down considerably.
Command matures you quickly, Yuelia. I rose through our ranks quickly because I was brash, but I was made an officer to quell that.
Senior officers will tell you that responsible girls are given leadership roles. It's the opposite---I was made an officer to keep me in line.
Leading others is all about controlling yourself, Yuelia. I kept starting fights and taking needless risks until I was named a junior officer.
...It was just a fashion accessory, Yuelia. My Oma's company designed it...alongside living units.
...My headpiece doesn't do anything, Yuelia. I believe it was a model for a product made by my Oma's firm.
...From what I understand, my headpiece was a model of a new scanner design, Yuelia. My Oma designed products like that.
...I understand it looked like a scanner, Yuelia. My Oma's company made it...it was just a prototype design.
...It was just a family memento, Yuelia. Courtesy of my Oma...don't concern yourself with it.
...My Oma give it to me before she died. There's no need to dwell on it...
...It was a gift from my Oma, Yuelia. That's all...I didn't want to make a big deal of it.
...Yes, it was important to me. A gift from my late Oma...that's all there is to it.
I see every competition as a chance to improve myself, Yuelia. I can't do that if I don't give it my all.
Poker is all about reading your opponents, Yuelia. If I can succeed here, it will help me improve my piloting skills, as well.
Healthy competition forges rivalries, friendships, and self-improvement, Yuelia. I can't improve if I don't take this seriously.
Piloting is just a more serious competition, Yuelia. Here, I can practice predicting my opponents without the same life-or-death stakes.
You can't let the enemy see weakness, Yuelia. Besides, I'm lucky enough to have a normal body...
Part of leadership is keeping a straight face, Yuelia. And compared to many girls, I have nothing to be embarrassed about naked...
It's my job to be calm, Yuelia. Besides...what right do I have to be embarrassed? I don't have any scars.
...It's arrogant of me to act embarrassed, Yuelia. I know younger girls who've suffered burns...nakedness is no issue for me.
Our quartermaster, Gascogne, has put me through many poker games when she sees I need to vent. Here, I'm analyzing others...
...It's strange to be playing poker with peers. I usually find myself in games with our quartermaster as she teases out my frustrations.
...It's nice to be able to question people from Earth, Yuelia. Usually in poker games, our quartermaster is the one questioning me.
Card games are our quartermaster's favorite means of shaking down me and my crewmates. I often need that...but this is a nice change of pace.
...I come from a planet of women, Mary, if that's what you mean. Why does that sound hellish to you?
...My homeworld has its issues, Mary, but you seem to be implying that the lack of men is the reason for that. Why?
..."Hell on Earth" for having no men around, as I understand? I figured Earth girls would be attached to men, but you would go that far?
...I'm sure you're accustomed to men, but it is not "Hell on Earth" without them. If that's indeed what you're referring to...
That's fair. I'm not from this planet, after all...go ahead.
I'm prepared to answer, Amy. I understand Earth's mixed-gender culture is very unlike Mejare's.
I'm used to answering questions, and I expected some given my unusual homeworld. Go ahead, Amy.
My home planet and my outfit both seem to invite questions. I'm listening.
...I'd rather discuss my suit than my personal life. What I'm wearing is a common pirate flightsuit, though Mejarians do love form-fitting clothing.
...There isn't much time when I'm not working, Amy. That's thanks to being a pirate---and pirates wear these suits the most.
...This is more a pilot's suit than anything else, Amy, though some young Mejarian civilians like the feel. They're cheap, so our pirate crew wears them.
...I'll focus on the suit questions. Bodysuits are both practical and efficient, which makes them low-cost uniforms---useful for a pirate crew like ours.
I think you'll find my underwear quite standard, Amy. What would be the sense in overcomplicating it?
"Fancy underwear"? An undergarment's job is to provide support and protection, Amy. What would you add?
...I'd describe "fancy underwear" as lingerie, but you seem to mean that there should be mechanical parts on my bra. I don't see the use.
Even my "space stuff" isn't fancy, Amy. Something as simple as underwear isn't improved with electronics.
...I used to streetfight, either for money or just to survive. Still, I wouldn't think it's made me muscular enough to be called a "brawler."
...I pilot a Dread ship. That places me firmly in long-range...we're taught to not fight men up close if we can help it.
...That depends what a man's definition of a "brawler" is. I fight with my Dread ship, as well as small arms...and formerly my fists.
And you would be mistaken, Brock. Women's weapons are inconspicuous, as opposed to men and their rocket launchers.
..."Max" sounds like a man's name. I can assure you my experience with men is limited. Do you actually wear bodysuits here?
...Who is "Max"? Another man, it sounds like...the only men I know personally are the three prisoners aboard our ship.
..."Max"? A man, I assume---why would a man wear a bodysuit, let alone give me one? Men's bodies are too angular.
...No, I don't know a "Max." I know very few men in general...do men really consider bodysuits a fighting outfit?
...Are you implying our pilots sometimes lose limbs in combat, Gaige? Dread crashes are very dangerous, yes.
...Is Earth still divided into countries, Megumin? I was born on planet Mejare, an Earth colony known for having no men.
...I come from Mejare, an all-female Earth colony. Are you saying Earth isn't united as a planet, Megumin? That would probably lead to a violent culture.
"Evil gods"? As if Earth weren't dangerous enough already...I was hoping to visit some secluded beaches, not a primitive village.
..."Evil gods" aren't what I had in mind, Megumin. Famous landmarks would be much easier and safer to observe than your village.
...Do you mean "execute a prisoner," Fidget? It'd be easiest to just throw them out of the airlock.
..."Walk the plank"? That sounds like a euphemism for executions...we have an airlock for that.
...I used to. But I wasn't a pirate then.
...No. I stopped drinking rum when I became a pirate.
...Our ship has some rum. I haven't drank since I came aboard.
...When I say classical has survived, I mean we have the most records of it. I actually took an interest in punk rock when I was younger.
More classical pieces were preserved when we settled Mejare than anything else. That's all I meant..when I was a teenager, I got into our punk scene.
Mejare still has other musical genres, Revy. My Fama gave me stern looks when I entered a punk rock phase...
I only prefer classical music now to relax. Mejare has underground punk bands I once took interest in, much to my parents' disapproval.
...That's correct, Saki. Is there something you'd like to ask about Mejare's culture?
...I have had relationships. To call any of them "girlfriends" would be quite generous.
...No, Saki, I didn't. If women's bodies operate on a cycle of reproductive viability, it only seemed natural that men's would, as well.
...If men and women are really part of the same species, Saki, I'd expect our bodies to have similar cycles.
...Saki, the period is an integral part of women's reproductive cycles. For men to have no analog to that makes them seem so...alien.
...I am a human, Mary, so no, it's not weird at all.
...I "look identical" to a human because I am a human, Mary. I understand Earth has framed Mejarian colonists as otherwise.
...Mejarians are human women, Mary. At no point did I imply I was an alien.
...Men have settled their own planet, Mary---Tarak. It's in the same system as Mejare, which has led to armed conflict.
...I know little of how women are treated here, Mary, but there exists a colony of men, as well. It's a desert world called Tarak, near Mejare.
..."Kama Sutra"? I'm not the one to ask about Earth literature, Yuelia...but if girls are hesitant to share details, it's probably sexual in nature.
...I'm not familiar with Earth's literary canon, Yuelia, but that book is probably sexually explicit. Why else would girls be hush about its contents?
...I know you aren't serious, Erufuda, but artificial gravity has been commonplace technology for centuries.
...Aside from the obvious answers, women haven't been weightless in space for centuries, Erufuda. Artificial gravity is standard.
...No one is weightless in space, Erufuda. Even my Dread has an artificial gravity system---only the most antiquated ships don't.
...Truthfully, most of my pilots are in fine shape, Erufuda. But I don't want them to get complacent...and I don't want to lose any of them.
...Every bit of excess fat could mean the difference between life and death, Erufuda. My pilots do take good care of themselves... but I worry.
...I think some of my pilots actually appreciate my strictness, Erufuda. Many of them were aimless before joining our crew...
...I know better than most that many young women need structure in their lives, Erufuda--- especially pirates. I want to provide that for my subordinates...
...I'm trying to set an example for my pilots, Erufuda. Complacency is the most dangerous threat we face...and nothing is worse than losing a team member.
Erufuda...half of our recruits are drifters off the Mejarian streets. I want to give them goals to strive for...and a greater purpose.
...I see this game as an opportunity to learn about Earth. I assure you, my crewmates can hardly get a greeting out of me.
...I care little for a man's opinion. But you should know I talk far less when I'm among crewmates.

Shouko?
...Our crew's travel through the galaxy has been beset by Earth's attacks, but yes, we've found places of striking beauty along the way...

Yes, Shouko?
...Well, we've all done our best to appreciate space's beauty in between attacks from Earth's Harvest fleets.

I see you, Shouko.
...It's true, space is full of wonders and mystery. Of course, Earth's fleets have distracted us from that...as have the men.
...I, too, don't concern myself with escalating conflict because of perceived personal slights. I used to, when I was in your position.
I'm not interested in a delinquent's posturing, Saki. Don't project animosity where there is none...like I used to.
...That's understandable, Saki. I'm glad you've found something positive in your life---too many delinquent girls just drink and fight.
I'm not denying our differences, Saki. You should be glad you don't have to fight to survive...it's difficult for delinquent girls to break that cycle.
...Are you implying women strive for beauty solely to please men, Erufuda? Even if that were true, it's no reason to pretend obesity is beautiful.
Coddling girls who make poor fitness decisions is not "inclusive," Erufuda. Men's presence wouldn't change that---I hope.
What do men have to with that, Erufuda? Girls pursue beauty to impress each other. Obesity shows a lack of self-control, nothing more.
...Is something wrong, Galatea?
...Galatea. If you have something to say to me, then do so.
...That's correct, Galatea. There may be men aboard our ship, but Earth has a society in which men and women have coexisted.
...Yes, Galatea, that's right. I was hoping to gain the perspective of a culture that's accustomed to men and women sharing space.
That's right, Galatea. Both men and Earth are technically my enemies, so this should help me learn about both---men and women live together here.
I'm sure you still have some insight to provide me as an Earthling, Galatea. Mejare has lost much knowledge of planet Earth in general.
...Even if your circumstances are unusual, I would welcome your insight on this planet, Galatea. In fact, you may prove to be less biased.
...Space travel is well-established at this point, Cynthia. Our elderly captain might have a similar perspective to your grandmother.
...The first recorded spaceflight is several centuries old at this point, Cynthia. Our captain was a first-generation colonist---maybe your grandmother is around the same age.
...Do you have a close relationship with your grandmother, Cynthia? Our captain is quite elderly, and she speaks of our planet's founding in the same way.
...I'd imagine there are as many women living on extraterrestrial settlements as there are men, Cynthia. Apparently it's commonplace for them to live together.
Most of the settlements our crew has encountered have a roughly equal proportion of men and women, Cynthia. I believe even Tarak and Mejare's populations are close.
I pilot a Dread fighter as the leader of one of the attack fleets on the Nirvana. It is the flagship of a neutral pirate group in the Tarak-Mejare conflict.
I serve the Magno Family pirate outfit as Chief Pilot of our Dread team. That armor I was wearing signifies my status as Wing Commander.
I serve the Nirvana pirate ship as a junior officer and Chief Pilot of its Dread fleet, Cynthia.
I am one of several wing commanders in the Magno Family pirate outfit, Cynthia. We are currently separated from our remaining crew, making me the full-time Chief Dread pilot.
..."Fool you"? I freely admit that I'm part of a pirate outfit, Shantae.
...What other pirates have you encountered, Shantae? I've made no attempt to deceive you about who I work for.
I don't lead the entire ship, Jolyne. I'm Chief Pilot of our Dread fleet. Though I do have a reputation for strictness, even to our upper command.
I'm only a junior officer, Jolyne. I lead our Dread fleet. In fact, our captain is probably more laid-back than I am.
I serve as wing commander, not captain. There are several women who rank above me, Jolyne...though they're often more relaxed.
It's funny you say that, Jolyne. Our captain and quartermaster both feel I can be overly serious at times. I command our Dread fighters.
...We don't seem alike at all, PA-15. Unless you mean how we've both brought weapons.
...Aside from both being armed, I don't see a resemblance between us, PA-15.
...The Magno Family was formed after an energy crisis shut down a living district on Mejare, Cynthia. Many of our recruits are refugees from that incident.
...Until recently, our pirate group hadn't left the Mejarian system, Cynthia. We raided military bases for supplies after an energy crisis left many civilians homeless.
...I joined the Magno Family because I was living on the streets, Cynthia. It was formed for girls in situations like mine after a major civilian disaster.
It's not, Lucy---Earth is the organ harvest. We've had to repel the fleets it's sent to collect ours.
Earth's other colonies are its organ farms, Lucy. Mejare is designated for breasts and uteri, so we've been attacked by Harvester fleets.
...In my time, Myriam, Earth is already doomed. It's attempting to give my homeworld a similar fate.
...I serve as a wing commander, Myriam, but that's irrelevant to this game.
...You're a reporter, aren't you? You would do well to gain a better understanding of space travel than some vague "degree."
Mejare is in a state of open conflict with Tarak, Cynthia. And that conflict is based on us being women. Tarakkians believe women eat their intestines, and so would execute us on sight.
Tarak is all-men by design, Cynthia. If we were to try to land there, we would immediately be captured and executed.
We have a base of operations in low orbit around Mejare, Cynthia. If we were caught there, we would risk prison. So much as approaching Tarak would mean execution.
Tarakkian men would not welcome us as allies just for opposing Mejare's empire, Cynthia. They do not believe women to be human beings.
Yes, I am, Pyrrha. I serve as a wing commander for my squadron.
That's right, Pyrrha. I have a fighter craft of my own and command several other pilots.
Mejare is an extraplanetary Earth colony, Pyrrha. It's quite some distance across the galaxy, so it's understandable that you wouldn't know of it.
Mejare is an Earth colony in a distant sector of this galaxy, Pyrrha. It has a sister planet nearby, called Tarak---which is a colony itself.
I actually came here to compare the two, Pyrrha. What roles do men typically fill in your society?
This is my first time observing a mixed-gender society, Pyrrha. I'd hoped you could shed some light on the subject, such as men's function within it.
...I'm not a biologist, Pyrrha, but evidently genetic disorders are not a concern using our artificial process.
...When two women are ready to have a daughter, Pyrrha, their eggs are artificially spliced together. Maybe disorders were originally common, but the process has been refined for decades.
...Is that the stigma Earthlings associate with women having children together, Pyrrha? Our eggs are spliced together. If disorders were an issue at first, it's been resolved.
...I guess you view a man's involvement as more natural. My education is limited, Pyrrha, but couples on Mejare donate and carry spliced eggs. Whatever disorders you mean have been dealt with.
...I do, Pyrrha. I never associated with my crewmates much outside of my duties, but in the past, there were at least other junior officers I shared those duties with.
Our crew is currently isolated from the rest of the Magno Family, Pyrrha, so those feelings have been stronger recently. I'm the only one of my rank aboard our ship.
...I serve as a part-time wing commander, Pyrrha, but the others who share that rank are cut off at the moment. So any feelings of loneliness have been exacerbated lately.
I serve as a junior officer, Pyrrha, which is an odd middle ground of rank. It doesn't help that the others in my position are currently absent from our ship.
Mejare is an Earth colony settled around a hundred years ago, Neptune. It's known for having an exclusively female population.
Mejare is my home planet, Neptune. It's one of many settlements founded by Earthlings in recent centuries, and only women live there.
My homeworld is a planet known as Mejare, Yunyun. It's a remote Earth colony populated only by women. I recognize that you're being friendly, if you were concerned.
...I know that showing interest in others is friendly, Yunyun. I come from Mejare, an all-female Earth colony in a remote sector of the galaxy.
...Can you describe a "monster" to me, Neptune? Mejare has mild surface conditions due to heavy terraforming, though its exosphere has dangerous debris.
Mejare is a terraformed, temperate blue planet surrounded by twin asteroid belts, Neptune. Can you explain what you mean by "monsters"?
Mejare is a blue planet settled late in the frontier era, Yunyun, roughly a hundred years ago. Only female colonists and their descendants inhabit it today.
Mejare is a temperate Earth colony, Yunyun. It's been home to several generations of female colonists and their descendants, such as me and other members of our crew.
I'm far from perfect myself, Galatea. But that's very flattering.
...You don't need to flatter me, Galatea. I could point out more flaws on my own body than yours---but thank you.
Mejare exists in an isolated system, Mr. Raynor, so we've only recently explored beyond it. Our crew is Mejare's first contact with many other colonies in the sector.

Most of the colonies in Mejare's sector are isolated from each other, Mr. Raynor. That includes Mejare itself---we didn't even know other human settlements existed besides Earth until we left the system.
Most of my experience lies in Dread assaults around Mejare's system, Mr. Raynor. We became explorers by accident---but we have found other human settlements.
...Thank you, Mr. Raynor. Until recently, our crew was more an assault team than an exploration one. But a wormhole accident sent us across the galaxy, which has led to new discoveries.
It's funny you mention that, Erufuda---since the Nirvana was formed in a fusion accident, we had trouble with climate control at first. My suit was sticking to me one minute and chafing me the next.

Climate control is something we often take for granted on modern ships, Erufuda. The Nirvana has an old section, and our power core malfunctioned at first---my flightsuit wasn't ideal for fluctuating temperatures.

Funnily enough, Erufuda, I had to keep a straight face when the Nirvana first formed and we couldn't regulate its temperature. I was nearly sweating through my suit, and then it froze to my body a few minutes later.

Yes, Shouko?
...I resented the men early on---relying on other women was bad enough, and they challenged my authority. But I couldn't ignore the value they brought to our crew.

Shouko?
...Having to rely on men as crew members hurt my pride at first. But I realized I was being foolish...it's strange how quickly we became used to them.
..."Nevada"? It's possible there are other all-male planets like Tarak that we aren't aware of. Has it always been that way, Deimos?
...Are you not from this planet either, Deimos? We haven't encountered a colony called Nevada in our sector. Was it settled solely by men, like Tarak?
...That's correct, Mr. Raynor. Our captain was a first-generation colonist and recalls that men and women were separated when their frontier ships arrived at the two planets.
...As I understand it, Mr. Raynor, Mejare and Tarak were both settled at the same time around a century ago by colonists who separated by sex. Our captain was among the passengers.
...This is the standard flightsuit our pilots wear, Megumin. Its flexibility and simplicity make it useful for combat roles, which I assume Darkness fills for you.
...By "crusader," I assume you mean Darkness is some kind of fighter. Our pilots wear these suits so they won't fumble with their clothes when the ship is under attack.
...No, Chazz, I wouldn't. The Magno Family has not been active on Earth, nor on any private shipping companies. We attack military.
Those attacks were likely from an Earth pirate group, Chazz. The Magno Family only operates on Mejare and Tarak, targeting military ships.
...I'm here to learn about this planet, Chazz. Men and women coexist here, and it's where my ancestors came from.
...Earth is my ancestors' homeworld, Chazz, and I'd like to see how they lived and worked with men. Your family's company is not my concern.
Yes, Chazz, that's correct. There are no men to exclude, so we don't typically think of things in those terms.
That's correct, Chazz, but they wouldn't be called such. To Mejare's society, the only concept of a human is a woman.

condition.saying: What would you say is the biggest thing you've ever stolen?

case.state: Most of our vessels were stolen in steadily bigger heists, Chazz, and the one I currently serve on is quite large. You don't need to know more about our forces.
It's enough for you to know that our most recent ship is impressive, Chazz. We've progressively stolen larger ones.
...No, Chazz, it isn't. This is the planet where humans originated, and it's much different than my own.
...It's not, Chazz. Mejarians are taught to respect the planet our ancestors came from, and I'm glad to be seeing it for myself.
I spend my free time exercising, Deimos, so I can be ready for combat. Cooking is also a common pastime on our ship. Of course, you should be aware that we're pirates and not typical Mejarians.
...As pirates, we're not normal examples of women, Deimos. I keep a workout routine, others cook or maintain their appearances.
There are no men on my home planet, Yuri. Mejare was settled specifically as a female-only colony.
My homeworld is a colony that only took female settlers, Yuri. I didn't know any men personally until a year ago.
...This is a flightsuit, Perona, not a diving suit. It's a standard uniform for space pilots.
...I wear this suit to pilot my Dread fighter, Perona. Our crew operates from orbit rather than on the coast.
...I'm not the person to ask, Galatea. I've done it, but...it depends on the girl you're with. And I hung out with thugs.
If you want my personal experience, Galatea... short, rough, and empty. But I have crewmates who are in healthier relationships.
...It was this or asking our prisoners to strip for me, Miss Jessie. I need to understand men better for as long as they're crew members.
I'm not interested in finding a man to sleep with, Miss Jessie. I barely know their anatomy---and this is an easy opportunity to see it.
...I don't know men's bodies well enough to find them attractive, Miss Jessie. That's why I came here---to learn how men and women coexist on this planet.
We haven't encountered any alien life forms in space, Perona. Humans have largely colonized the galaxy by terraforming dead planets.
Humans haven't found aliens in any colonization efforts so far, Perona. Those colonies were only founded thanks to terraforming technology.
...So far, only humans live in space, Perona. All of our colonies were inhospitable to life until they were terraformed.
It's like I said about the other colonies, Mr. Raynor---we were manipulated into war several generations ago, probably because our planets were close to each other.
The Mejarian-Tarakkian war is a product of propaganda, Mr. Raynor---the same way I said the other colonies have been divided and conquered.
...I'm not very familiar with men, Marinette, no. I had hoped I could learn about them from a game like this.
...If you could share your experiences with men, Marinette, I would appreciate it. I'm sure I could learn about them from you.
...Perona, you want a map of the entire universe? Even one nebula requires sophisticated computers to navigate.
...Perona, how big do you think space is? Humans have only colonized a few sectors of one galaxy, and computer models are needed to map even that.

Hermione...?
I came here to see the original home of humans for myself, and one where men and women lived together. I didn't expect to also find something like "magic."
...I was curious about my ancestors' homeworld, Hermione. Especially since they lived alongside men. Although this magic presents a whole separate issue.
My homeworld has no men living there, Adrien. I didn't see one in person until I was a teenager.
...You're correct, Adrien. I was raised on a planet with only women. The first time I spoke with a man was a year ago.
...I didn't feel the need to say anything else, Adrien. Is there something about men you want to tell me?
...I thought we were finished, Adrien. If you have something else to say about men, I'm listening.
...That's what we hope from our homeworlds, Mr. Raynor. Both Tarak and Mejare. A common threat got us to accept our prisoners, after all.

Mr. Raynor...?
Our hope is that our common enemy will unite the men's and women's homeworlds. That's how our crew took men in.
It's no issue, Yuri. Mejare has had energy shortages that forced evacuation of our living districts. It was preventable, but the government hardly even provided help afterward.
You don't need to apologize, Yuri. Corruption on Mejare forced many citizens out of their homes when energy systems failed. No new housing was built.
...Our crew takes measures to avoid money, Fate. The captain has said she doesn't want us to be tied down or traced by taking jobs.
My "equipment" is standard on my homeworld, Fate. The Magno Family keeps its hands clean of money where possible so we remain hidden.
The Magno Family uses what it can steal from militaries, Fate. Money leaves more of a trail, and there are few illegal outfits to take it.
Our crew operates to survive, Fate, not to turn a profit. We take what "equipment" we need on raids.
You're referring to our quartermaster Gascogne, Fate. She has a reputation for using it to dress down new recruits who are starting fights.
...Our quartermaster Gascogne is known for being a poker shark, Fate. If a new recruit is causing problems, she sits them down for it while they fume.
Fate...? You must mean Gascogne, the head of our regisystem. Poker is how she deals with difficult rookies. Is there anything else?
This is our standard flightsuit, Nami. Most of our pilots wear it, except for the armor---which is for junior officers.
...This is just a flight uniform, Nami. My armor is for wing commanders, but even it is just standard materials.
Mejare is a planet, Nami. It was settled a century ago. But that island you're referring to might be where our ancestors lived on Earth.
It's a planet, Nami. I was told in school that Mejare's original colonists isolated themselves from men, even when they lived on Earth. There might be some truth to that.
...I guess it's true Mejarians usually aren't shy about being nude together, Perona. Around men, we had a policy of full-body suits and masks.
...It's true Mejarians seem less modest than Earth girls, Perona. It might be because there's no men around---we used to wear masks and thermal suits if we knew we were raiding them.
...That won't be necessary, Senko.
...I'm not looking for one, Senko.
...I brought it up in case the staff said something, Polly. I don't want to make a scene.
...Polly, I get enough hounding from my crewmates on my birthday already. I didn't want tonight to be about me.
...I knew I'd end up with a girl who'd try to turn this into a birthday party.
...You're not the kind of girl I'd let have a taste, Polly. Even if you were alive.
I used to know some thugs on Mejare who had that picture of birthdays, Polly. Knocking back booze in a dingy bar.
I'm not going to strip to music, Polly. If you want to celebrate so badly, do it yourself.
I find parties to be nothing but a nuisance, Polly. Especially when I'm the center of attention.
...I'm from "another world" that humans settled, Lux. Although "flesh-eating monsters" is about how the men on Tarak would describe us.
You have the same view of Mejarians that the men on our neighboring planet do, Lux. "Paralyze them and eat their entrails." But we're all human.
I lead our ship's assault team of Dread fighters, Colt. Our navigator is actually a man---the only one our ship's helm responds to.
Our navigator is actually one of the few men we have on board, Colt. I serve as the Nirvana's Chief Pilot.
Our ship is the result of a fusion accident between a male and female vessel, Colt. It's powerful but unreliable---we spent days just getting all the systems online.
...I can best describe the Nirvana as temperamental, Colt. It's the result of an unstable energy core fusing men and women's ships together and feeding off our emotions.
Mm...my suit is our standard flight uniform, Nami. I have to set an example to my pilots by dressing for combat.
I can't wear training gear into combat, Nami. I'm an officer.
...Nami, if I can't bother to wear my flightsuit in case of attacks, I can't expect my pilots to.
...This is a pilot's suit, Fina. Members of our Dread team wear them for ease of movement.
...This is just a flightsuit, Fina. It's the uniform for our crew's Dread team while piloting.
...You're Sucrose, right? What counts as a "terrestrial world" besides Earth? Mejare was settled and terraformed by Earthlings.
...My homeworld was terraformed, Sucrose. Its people are descended from Earth travelers. I would think that's a "terrestrial world."
...That's right, Sucrose. More or less. Do you---have personal experience you'd be willing to share?

My experience with men is limited to working with them on our crew, Sucrose.
...Have you been intimate with one?
Mejare uses machines to conceive, Sucrose. Women form couples and have their eggs spliced so that one of them can carry the child.
Mejare has developed ways to combine two women's DNA, Sucrose. One donates an egg, and one carries the child. All of us were born this way.
...Our crew has spent the last few months in space, Bobobo, yes. Is there something you want to know?
...Yes, Bobobo, our ship has been traveling through deep space for some time now. Why do you ask?
Dreads are technically just fighter crafts for space combat, Takatoshi. They only become mechs when fused with a man's Vanguard.
I only pilot a "mech" in the sense of my Vandread, Takatoshi. It's a fusion between a Vanguard mech and a Dread, which is a more traditional space fighter.
...It doesn't do anything, Hilda. It's just a hair ornament.
...There's no function, Hilda. It's an old gift. Just fashion.
...I get the impression most Earth girls couldn't, Hilda. Life without men is just life to me. Maybe you could explain the role men play in yours.
...I don't know what life with men is like any more than you know what it's like without them, Hilda. What do you find them so essential for?

state.text: ...I had two mothers, Yuri. We all did. An "Oma" mother donates an egg; the "Fama" carries the baby.
...Besides the man, that sounds like Mejare's families, Yuri. Girls have "Oma" and "Fama" mothers, the Fama being the one who carried them.

case.state: The Magno Family was formed by innocent people who were left homeless, Penny. We aren't looking to create more of them. I guess pirates here are in it for money?
Most of my crewmates are innocent people, Penny. We only target military outfits for supplies. Does this planet have a piracy problem?
...Space can be very lonely, Fluttershy. But I do have my crewmates with me. I didn't appreciate that for a long time.
...I'm not actually in space alone, Fluttershy. My crewmates are with me. Even if I do have a habit of secluding myself.
...This is just our crew's flightsuit, Critical Darling. But techno is popular on our ship, and on Mejare itself.
I'm not a musician, Critical Darling, but there are lots of young girls on Mejare who like techno. That includes our crew.
...Space exploration began generations before my time, Y'shtola. We call it the frontier era. Most of even that technology is outdated by now.
...I was born well after space travel was developed, Y'shtola, on a colony founded by spacefarers. I don't know much about how the process began.

state.text: ...Do you mean a computer, Sachi? It's just a hair ornament. My Oma gave it to me.

case.state: ...It's just a family gift, Sachi. There's no electronics inside.
...Mejare has lots of water, Magma Grunt. Our terraforming projects haven't granted access to all of it, but its settlers liked the prospect.
...Yes, it does, Magma Grunt. From what I've learned, Mejare was chosen as the women's homeland largely because of the water supply.
...Are you talking about sexual urges, Magma Grunt? With each other, mostly.
..."Function" as in "have sex," Magma Grunt? Girls usually form couples on Mejare. You do that with men, don't you?
...Are you talking about toys, Sucrose? Having one that big is...sort of perverted.
...An "implement" the size of a man's rod is the kind of thing you'd have to ask a shop to get from the back, Sucrose. At least on Mejare.
...Do you mean sex toys, Sucrose? I've met maybe one girl who had one as big a man's tube. She had that sort of reputation.
...I know about some of their organs, Nami, but I'm sure an Earth girl can explain more. I was hoping this game would help fill some of those gaps.
...That's why I'm here, Nami. More or less. I'm not sure how much there is to know beyond those tube-organs.
...Are you talking about those egg-sacks, Perona? That's the first thing they teach us about raiding men. Don't fight them hand-to-hand, and kick at their groin if they grab you.
...I already knew that, Perona. I've spent a lot of missions fighting men, even if I didn't know why I was supposed to aim for their groins if they got close.

My turn again...what is it, Constanze?
...Maybe, compared to this time period. What makes you say that?
...What are you referring to, Constanze? It might be advanced, if this is before the frontier era.
By my planet's standards, Surcrose, yes. Maybe you think I'm prude for not...going bigger.
It sounds like it's just cultural differences, Sucrose. But you'd definitely get weird looks where I'm from.
...Which is, Bobobo?
...You mean, how we function without men, Bobobo?
...For some reason, I thought you might be the one Earthling to take that in stride, Bobobo.
...I couldn't tell you how they work, Gwen. I'd have to ask our engineers.
...I don't know the science behind Mejare's laser weapons, Gwen. It only matters that I can aim one.
...I'm just a pilot, Gwen. I received some weapons training, but I don't know how the internals work.
...I don't know what a "dude" is.
...What's a "dude"?
..."Dudes"? I don't understand.
...Go ahead, Petra. I know I've been just as curious.
...I expected plenty of questions when I came here, Petra. I've had plenty for others.
...I stay away from that sort of thing, Petra. Besides, there's only one girl who shares my rank.
...Thank you, Petra. But I wouldn't date my pilots. And there's only one other wing commander.
Mejare was only founded because of terraforming, Y'shtola. We live a lot like our ancestors on Earth.
Mejare isn't much of an "alien world," Y'shtola. The frontier era was kicked off by the ability to terraform planets.
...That's right, Fluttershy. Mejare was settled without any male colonists.
...No, they don't, Fluttershy. Mejare is all-female, and we were taught we only had female ancestors.
...That's right, Jason. There's about as many men living on this planet as there are women, right?
...No, Jason, there aren't. Is is strange for you to see men here? I thought the populations were equal.
...Well, it beats lifting crates in reg, Bobobo. I couldn't stand just being some grunt in the bowels of the ship.
...You could say that, Bobobo. I became a pilot because I wanted to stand out on the crew.
...Of course it is, Monika. We have to raid military ships just for supplies.
...I serve on a pirate crew, Monika. Survival is never a guarantee.

...Shouko?
The reason we have men aboard is because our ship got fused with an old section of the men's. We make them sleep and use the bathrooms there.
...Mm. Privacy isn't much different, Shouko. Our ship was fused with the men's. Their quarters, bathrooms--- everything is on that side.
We used to operate in our system, Fina, but we've been marooned elsewhere for a while now.
...A year ago, that would've been true, Fina. We've been trapped in deep space for months, far off from Mejare.
We used to be local, Fina. Mostly raiding Tarak to keep our homeworld off our backs. An accident threw us across the galaxy around a year ago.
...It's been a while since we've really operated as "pirates," Fina. There's a magnetic storm near Mejare that always kept us close, until a wormhole stranded us in another nebula.
...Agh. Gravity hasn't been an issue since the first spaceships, Critical Darling. It's built into every craft we have.
...Artificial gravity has been standard for decades, Critical Darling. Even my Dread has g-force dampeners.
I lead our Dread team, Reimu. This armor shows my rank as wing commander, and is fairly standard.
Dread team leader, Reimu. This is just junior officer's armor. Imperial soldiers have much better materials.
...If you mean I look strange, Kumatora, it's probably because I'm not from here. I'm a pilot from planet Mejare.
...Do you mean how I'm dressed, Kumatora? This is my pilot's uniform. It's common on my homeworld.
...You don't look like you care for them, either, Kumatora. You've got the same haircut.
...I guess you could put it that way, Kumatora. You've put your hair the same way.
...Your hair's cut the same way, Kumatora. You might be talking more about yourself.
...There's a lot I could talk about, Fina. Mostly other human settlements, and what we've discovered about our own history.
...We've learned a lot about ourselves from seeing other colonies, Fina. Especially how men and women live together there.
...As a matter of fact, our ship's helper robot might be the first of his kind with feelings. What's your interest, Noire?
...Our crew has a sentient robot onboard, Noire. But it's only from a fusion accident. Is that Gamindustri's test for advancement?
...What's "the dragon," Y'shtola? You've sounded like you've never left this planet at all.
...You mean you've heard of space travel, Y'shtola? You didn't give that impression, whatever the "dragon" is.
...I've had crewmates who died. What's your point, Hu Tao?
...Piracy is dangerous, Hu Tao. That shouldn't be a surprise.
I don't know what you might find interesting, Hu Tao, but our captain used to be a priestess. She has a shrine for crew members who've died.
Do you mean our crew, Hu Tao? Our captain has photos of each of us, and they're added to a shrine if we die. It's something from her days as a priestess.
...I respect my crewmates, Fina. And they respect me. I keep to myself otherwise.
...My crewmates care about me, Fina, even if it took me a while to accept that. I don't have any partners, if that's what you mean.
...My homeworld is Mejare, Miss Samus. It's a colony planet from the Frontier Era. From what I can tell, it's remote compared to your Federation Space.
...I was born on an outer-world colony called Mejare, Miss Samus. It's isolated even from most other settlements.
Mejare's settlers didn't change their diet, Yuno. The men did. If you want "space food," try their pills.
...Men must be less picky. The ones on Tarak eat synthetic pills. Our food is the same as it is here, Yuno.
How do you think Earth's colonies were settled, Yuno? They were terraformed to match Earth.
...I'm not an alien, Yuno. If I can live on a terraformed colony, obviously I can live on Earth.
...Very funny, Yuno. That armor wasn't to pad my chest.

What, Yuno?
...Don't make fun of me. I know how the armor looks.
...What's a "contraceptive," Yuno? Are you just taunting me again?
...Are "contraceptives" your word for push-up bras, Yuno?
...That's right, Leon. Dread corps. Do you actually know anything about that?
...I'm an officer for our Dread assault team, Leon. Are you just making conversation?
...Earth is the planet my ancestors came from, Leon. But I'm not trying to ruin the mood.
I don't mean to be too serious, Leon, but I am here to learn about where colonists all came from.
...Don't play games with me, Leon. What's this about?
...What are you saying, Leon? Just speak for yourself.
...What's that supposed to mean, L'Arachel?
...What manner is that, L'Arachel?
I wasn't trying to hide anything, L'Arachel. You said as much yourself.
You could see what I looked like from the start, L'Arachel. I'm not ashamed.
I'm---not the best with people, Kumatora, so I stay focused on our missions. If I stay calm, it keeps everyone else calm.
Everyone has their job on missions, Kumatora. A lot of leading my team is just keeping a cool head, so no one panics.
I don't usually think about people that way. What do you like, Leon?
That's a pretty simple way of thinking, Leon. What about you, or any man?
I wouldn't be here if I still thought men and women weren't mostly the same, Kumatora. That's why I want to know what an Earth girl thinks separates us.

I know, Kumatora. Men are also human beings. I'd never be this close otherwise.
...What is different, in your eyes?
...Do you mean for our ships, Heris? The main core is Paksis crystal---it's what made space travel possible in the first place.
The fuel for our ships is Paksis crystal, Heris. Everything from terraforming to warp speed has always been powered by it.
...I used to do those things, Reimu. But I hated it. I wanted some kind of purpose.
...Reimu, a few years ago, I hung out with girls who did that sort of thing. It just made me feel aimless.
...What would you have me do, Hilda? I'm playing along and talking with everyone.
...I spend most evenings scouting ahead alone, Hilda. Socializing isn't enough for you?
...I don't talk much in the first place, Hilda. People get nosy and start asking for more. What do you want?
...I work for pirates, Aaravi. Our captain is a civilian.
...Magno's Family are pirates, Aaravi. Magno herself is a priestess.
...Most of them are more social than me, Heris. They get excited over holidays and like to gossip.
...They can be flighty as people, Heris, but they know when to do their jobs. I just keep to myself.
...I don't know, Petra. We've all been handling new feelings. It was enough just to learn they were the same species.
...I'm not sure how I feel about them, Petra. A lot of us aren't. Even the fact they were human was a lot to take in.
Most girls on Mejare don't really like "athletic" builds, Petra. They're worried working out will shrink their breasts.
...They're not really jealous, Petra. A few have told me to exercise less so my bust will fill in.
...Mejarians are human, Trixie. Are "Mindfluckers" another species you fight?
I'm not a---"Mindflucker," Trixie. Do goblins have some kind of conflict with them?
There's plenty of couples on Mejare, Heris. I guess that's unusual here---between girls.
...If you mean couples, Heris, most girls on Mejare end up marrying and starting families. Have you never thought about that?
...Are you calling me a whore? This is my flightsuit, Turandot.
...What? I'm not a whore, Turandot, I'm a pilot. This is our uniform.
...It does, Anatoly. Right nearby. Tarak is Mejare's sister planet.
...That would be Tarak, Anatoly. It's the only other colony in Mejare's system.
...Women don't walk around naked, Hilda. But some girls do like seeing how far they can push it.
Girls show skin, Hilda, but there's a line between almost and totally naked. I guess you could say we like toeing it.

...Ahri?
...I don't know all the details, but you're not far off. The Paksis has a will of its own, and it's attached itself to me and some crewmates.

You can really sense that?
...You're right, Ahri. I and a few crewmates were swallowed up by the Paksis. It's had strange effects on us ever since.
...I'm fine, Noelle. Unless you'd like to join our crew, or provide some rations.
...We're shorthanded, Noelle, but you probably don't want to leave. We could always use extra food supplies.
You don't need to do something irresponsible to unwind, Erufuda. Our jacuzzi helps relax my muscles after training.
Erufuda, you can relax without a vice. I like some time in our jacuzzi for that.

Erufuda?
...It's when you're too exhausted to continue. That sounds simple, but I went too far all the time.
...Actually, Erufuda, I had a bad habit of doing that. I was always searching for strength I knew I didn't have.
I like squats the best, Erufuda. Maybe too much. I could spend more time on my upper half.

What's up, Erufuda?
...Probably squats. There's been times I cut into my upper-body routine for more of them.
...There is something relaxing about it, Erufuda. When I look out the windows, or scout ahead, it's a chance to take it in.
...I guess it's cool, Erufuda. For me, it's more...peaceful. Staring out into space is a nice way to gather your thoughts.
One centimeter doesn't add any fat, Erufuda. You obviously know that.
..."Erufuda," right? We're nearly the same height. You're just being stupid.
I don't know if that's true, Erufuda. But you could train twice as much and still put on weight if you're not smart about it.
...You don't seem totally lazy, Erufuda. I think you're just unfocused, and you eat too much for it to matter.
...What do you want me to say, Erufuda? I already told you how bad it's gotten. If you want to change that, drop the fries and stick to a plan.
I have been honest, Erufuda. You're out of shape, and you need to take weight loss seriously.
They have, Erufuda...mostly around the chest. It was a point of pride.
Erufuda...some girls have picked flightsuits that don't fit their measurements. But not around the waistline.
...I've shot down ships, Erufuda. On the ground, it's harder to tell. But I can pick out a few moments there, too.
...It's part of being a pilot, Erufuda. And a pirate. There are a few times on a raid that I know I shot someone.
...Is that angle the back, Erufuda? I get more compliments for that.
...What angle is that, Erufuda? I get more rookies calling my butt pretty than my face.
...If you want a flat stomach, Erufuda, then stop playing games and train properly.
...And your waist is still spilling out the sides. Erufuda, this kind of thing is why you can't keep weight off.
...If you're really a warrior, Erufuda, then you should get in shape for your own sake. Not to impress others.
...You're a fighter, Erufuda. Your pride and your combat skills should be enough motivation.

Erufuda?
...No.
...What kind of question is that? I don't want to play with your belly chub, Erufuda.
...I don't do a lot of weight training, Erufuda. You're a fighter, so maybe we could start by sparring.
...Let's start smaller. If you want to help me strength train, Erufuda, I'd like to see your combat skills.
Not if they fit in the first place, Erufuda. They stretch pretty well.

Erufuda?
...They're pretty flexible around the shoulders and groin. You just need the right size.
...I just feel that talk is cheap, Leon. If you liked me, you'd end up showing it.
I don't get many compliments, Leon. But they're still not valuable. I'd rather see how people feel with their actions.
...Miss Robin? I figure actions speak louder than words. But since you study Earth's history---how much is there to study?
I'm just trying to see things for myself, Miss Robin. If you're a historian, then how far back does Earth's history go?
I learned about men growing up, Miss Robin. They were large humanoids covered in germs, and they lived on another planet. That was about it.
Mejarians don't think about men much, Miss Robin. They were just some diseased, humanoid species the Border Guard had to deal with.
...I'm not really sure what it is, Cagliostro. That's why I want to find out.
...I don't have a good answer, Cagliostro. There's feelings that are hard to put into words. So I want to experience them.
...What do you want, Turandot?
...We don't need a deal, Turandot. Do you have another question?
Our ship's been under attack, Takatoshi. They're automated fleets called "Harvesters."
We've been fending off fleets of drone ships for a while now, Takatoshi. We call them the "Harvest."
..."Lesbians"? Mejare is all women, Nanoko, if that's what you mean.
...Is that what you call women on Earth, Nanoko? Mejare is all female.

Gloria?
...Whatever "energy crisis" Earth has, Mejare hasn't done much better.
Mejare's biggest problem is wasting energy. I don't think we've learned much from your time, Gloria.
It was never a fashion trend, Gloria. I've never seen another girl wearing one.
It's not fashionable, Gloria. The captain told me to dress more like an individual.
...What?
...Is that a joke? I'm a pirate, Dorothy.
...Are you talking to me? Dorothy, I'm on a pirate crew.
...Is that what you call it, Dorothy? I guess you see them every day.
I didn't even know they were called dicks, Dorothy. You know a lot about them, right?

Miss Robin?
...I've---never been with a girl I really liked. Just dumb thugs.
...That's hard to say, Miss Robin. I only really know what I don't like---loud and obnoxious, with nothing to show for it.
...What? Trixie, we can bathe on a ship just fine. And we want to---we even have a whole spa.
...We bathe every day, Trixie. There's showers and hot tubs. What kind of ship wouldn't have plumbing?
...Trixie, there's no "time off" for pirates. None of us have "friends" or some other place to go.
...Trixie, we're pirates. That's because we have nowhere else to go, or anyone else to be with.

...W-what? Hilda---is that what dildos are supposed to be?
...They're not too common, anyway.

H-Hilda, I---are you saying dildos are just toys of men's---penises?
...I guess that's why they've got a stigma.
The---"balls"? Is there some other organ I don't know, Dorothy?
...What are "balls"? I barely knew about the rod, Dorothy.
...That's right, Hayase. Mostly his---penis, I think it's called.
...I figure most organs are the same, Hayase. It's the reproductive ones I'm not sure about.
Anything higher would put me out of a Dread, Mr. Dunban. I don't think I could stand just giving orders on the ship.
...No. I'd hate to let others do the fighting, Mr. Dunban. I'm already a wing commander.
...I don't know what you're talking about, Kumatora. Something---psychic?
...What do you mean, Kumatora? "Energy" like PSI?
...So can we, Kumatora. It has moments where it feels lonely, or afraid---or even sick.
...It definitely has a will of its own, Kumatora. We can all sense it, too---it communicates.
...You mean, the tube, Hayase? Men get anxious about their size?
...Hayase, are you saying men feel insecure about how big their rods are?
We do get pretty close, Miss Robin. Maybe I wasn't topless in that suit, but---there was my butt.
It's not like we don't show off, Miss Robin. You wouldn't call that suit modest, would you?
...I'm an officer for the Magno's Family outfit. I can answer whatever questions you have, "Aqua Grunt."
...You might be a "grunt," but I'm a wing commander. I can represent Magno's Family if there's something you want to know.
...You can sense things, right, Cheryl? It's probably the Paksis.
...I don't think it's really me, Cheryl. It's Paksis energy you're feeling.
...That's how I've always been, Cheryl. I can focus on getting work done. It's just---it's not a skill.
You're probably better with people, Cheryl. I can focus on training, or flying, but with something like words---it doesn't come out right.
...You mean, smaller breasts, Hayase?
Is that another way of saying small-busted, Hayase?
...What's your point, Hayase? That's the game we're playing.
Isn't everyone playing to see this sort of thing, Hayase? What difference does it make?

Like a---male girlfriend, Cheryl?
...That's hard to say. I'm not even too sure what I like in a girl.
...I don't really know, Cheryl. Even if you asked me about a girlfriend, really...
Most Mejarians never meet men at all, Cheryl. I didn't see one in person until my first raid.
All the men are on Tarak, Cheryl. Only our crew and the Border Guard ever encounter them.
Huh? U-uh...Cheryl!
...Cheryl? W-what do you mean? Don't---!
We don't really build mechs, Roll. They're men's crafts, and they're small compared to a Dread.

Roll?
