I've been ready. It's better that I participate.
...Is it finally my turn?
...Bare chest for a bare face.
...I know it's me again. Do you know what's coming?
...Let the enemy get one good shot in, and look what happens...
...You don't let up, do you?
I knew one mistake would lead to another...
...I'm blushing, aren't I?
...I didn't need all that time to think of what to strip next.
...You broke my streak. And now...maybe my pride.
That can't be my last string of good luck...
I don't know about you, but I prefer leading the pack.
...That bought some time, at least.
I'll need a lot more luck to really pull ahead...
...Cosmic punishment for misleading you?
In poker, it's hard to know if you've even made a mistake.
..."Forgive yourself for your mistakes."
Losing like this isn't sustainable...
...That was quick. Fine, then...
The worst attacks are the ones where you can't even get your bearings.
Tch. I like the suit without the armor...
...In a dogfight, one mistake is death.
If the Paksis really is here, it's probably feeding off all the aural energy...
Damn. I was doing well.

You waited, and this is the big one.
...Sort of.
...I'm starting to sweat under this thing, anyway.
...Just as I finished my updates.
...What do you think's coming off?
...I lost a lot of hands when Miss Gasco got me worked up, too.
...What's worse? The losing streak, or the size difference?
This game is so watered-down...
...I really can't hide from it.
...Do you feel like I deserve this?
...Makes my reinforcements pretty pointless, doesn't it?
...I guess I deserved that.
...Alright. I know it's my turn.
The best I can say is that I'm keeping pace.
I was getting ready to lose this time...
That lucky streak created a lot of buildup for a B-cup.
I was doing well enough for a while...
...You're staring, ~player~. I know I lost.
...I'm doing the best I can, I guess.
...That was good mileage out of my reinforcements, at least.
...It didn't need to happen so fast, but at this point, I probably wanted to go all the way.
...Do you feel like you're getting lucky?
What a pain...
So much for my "reinforcements."
...Barely any time to adjust.
...I would've folded if I could.
...I knew Earthlings would never make it that easy.
That was coming sooner or later. And---it's probably good.
...That was enough time to adjust.

My turn.
...Are you excited?
...It's me. Let that streak be a warning. I'm not out of this until the very last shot.
Nirvana, this is Meia. I've held out as long as I can...now entering the final run.
Damn...well, I knew this would happen. I'll start small...
...Fine. I know I need to feel consequences to appreciate them.
...This had to happen eventually. Both losing a hand, and...well.
...Let's get this over with.
...I guess I should start small. Small by most standards...
...My turn. And...well, it won't seem like much.
...I know what's first.
...I've given some thought to what to strip first...
...I know. It's me.
I figured. But you know, I don't have a lot to lose.
...My turn.
...My turn again.
...Now for the real hard part.
...My whole order of doing this is pretty set.
...It's best to get this over with before you all get your hopes up.
I figured. Next'll be...my armor.
Me again. I don't have much of a choice now but to show you the truth.
It's me. This'll be the hardest loss...for you.
...I'll go again.
...That's my third. Even keeping pace is a big help, though.
...You can tell what's next, can't you?
This time I won't have any hard feelings. But the rest of you...
...I didn't spend much time as an ensign pilot. I don't like being stuck in the middle of the pack.
...Me again. Maybe you were looking forward to this.
...OK. Just a second...
...My suit's sticking. Maybe it was the right time, anyway.
...It'd help if I had any street clothes. A jacket, shirt, pants...shoes.
...The thing is, poker doesn't reward being so reckless. Except when it does.
...Well, I won't really be showing anything new.
I guess any amount of time this bought me was enough.
...There goes half my "reinforcements."
Upstaged by people taking needless risks...somehow it's more charming when it's the man in my squadron doing it.
...Haanh. Fine.
It's me. And it's time for the final hurdle.
...OK. I'm ready.

{pyoro}Meia, your defenses are nearly gone! Advising a tactical retreat!{!reset}
This is the whole point, Pyoro.
Normally, when I'm the center of attention, I have an agenda ready.
...It's probably for the best.
...My turn, for the last time.
We're all pretty even. I haven't forgotten---Earth is the enemy.
...OK. Nothing more for me to hide behind.
It's me. No more "reinforcements," either...

It's said that each of us is put on a stage in life, proving our existence for a judging crowd.
...I'm ready.
...Tarak has its minefield, and Mejare its asteroid belts. My last line of defense...is these.
...I'd never be happy, would I? If I didn't take everything off.
Tch...like I wasn't wearing the least to begin with.
...I'd say I didn't get the chance to scout, but it's already clear I have the least breathing room.
...I hoped I'd go a while. I can't afford too many lost rounds.
...After one whole round of recon, I've concluded you're all very modest.
Damn. Not even a round in...
...That didn't take long, and it's clear I needed it to.
You all wear too much...
...I get the sense that Earth people would be scandalized if I walked the streets like this.
I started with a streak, but you're all still ahead, anyway.
I know my suit isn't much, but Earthlings dress pretty heavily...is it because men and women live together?
That was a nice run to start with, but it doesn't seem to have helped much...
...Earth has cold winters, right? I don't know why else you'd be so covered...
...I was hoping for a good start. It looks like I'll need a good game in general.
Ugh...I won't learn anything if I can't keep pace.
...This is what poker does. It riles you up while leaving everything to chance...
...I can blame this on luck, but the crew owes a lot of our success to luck, too.
I should've worn more clothing, but...there wasn't much to bring.
I won't have much opportunity to study the group if everyone is busy studying me...
...No room to catch up.
Too much bad luck too quickly, and this mission might be a failure...
...Do you all wear so much here because of the seasons?
I'm still in a bad position...
...Personally, I wouldn't wear extra clothes unless they meant something.
...You can tell what's next, can't you?
...It's been some time since I lost, not that it helped much.
I'd need one of our raid suits to improve my situation...
I really don't wear more clothes than this---ever.
I should've taken an extra shift to~background.time~ instead.
...I think I know why our quartermaster likes to put pilots through poker games. It's so she can see how we deal with helpless situations.
...My stripping wasn't meant to be the main event to~background.time~.
The one time I join an away team...
...What do you think happens this time?
Maybe this game is a Harvest plot to sort clothes from organs.
...Street gangs on Mejare aren't above forcing girls to strip for fun.
I don't like being the center of attention...
...After all that, I'm still the lightest-dressed here. Even if it doesn't seem like it.
...That streak only did so much for me.
It's not hard for Earthlings' pants and shoes to outlast a Mejarian.
Just when I was mounting a comeback.
...If you feel secure, you really ought to be winning harder.
...You figure you're keeping the pressure on?
It's hard to observe when you keep being observed...
...Now I really feel like a foreigner.
The girls in my old gang would be laughing and jeering right about now...
...This is the kind of thing I'd order a retreat for.
The last thing I wanted was to be the center of attention tonight...
Maybe I should've just sped into Tarak's orbital minefield...
...So much for that.
I'm hardly in a better position now than before. And I'm---out of position...
Just let me---no, my bra is next...
You do what you can, and then some, and it still might not be enough...
Earth people are covered head to toe...
I gained a little ground, but...who knows how this'll end.
Still not comfortable...in any sense.
...These did a lot for me, and still not nearly enough.
...What? There's nothing extra this time.
...Shot down in flames.
...Come in just a flightsuit, and add bad draws on top of it...
...Miss Gasco always seems to draw a full house when she needs one.
...The others say I'm good at hiding my feelings.
I do pretty well in games with betting and folding...

...Nirvana, do you copy?
...Repeated damage. This mission appears untenable...
This---isn't over yet.
...Not impressed by by emergency clothes, I take it.
...The captain told me once that you can make no mistakes and still lose.
I can't believe I came to the homeworld of the Harvest and agreed to put my organs on display.
...I guess no reinforcements will help.
...If we played again, there's not much I'd do differently.
...Time to see what Earth people think of me.
...I think I've gotten better about accepting my mistakes.
If you think stripping excites me...maybe it would if I were winning.
If this were a dogfight, Miss Gasco would be retrieving us all...
I might as well try to fight with a stripped-down Dread.

{pyoro}Pyoro~! Things are getting serious now! What have you learned about Earthlings, Meia?{!reset}
...They're lucky.
...I'm up against a lot more clothing than I'm used to.
...I can't afford too many of these.
...The only real strategy is wear a lot of clothes, I see.
...Could you see the cards on my face? Or just my hips...
...It's me. It looks like I'll have to win a few rounds to everybody's one.
...Earth people seem pretty overdressed.
My turn. I might end up naked first...
...Wouldn't it make sense to all have to wear the same amount of clothes?
Tch.
My disadvantage...isn't just in the clothes.
...That headpiece was a lesson. This game is another---wear more clothes to strip poker.
Maybe I should just be glad I even understand the cards here...
...You have a lot more control in a cockpit.
If only I had all those elaborate dresses from when I was a girl...
...In times like this, one tactic is to sacrifice armor for evasion.
I'm behind. And now, it's...
...Even in a bad situation, a leader takes charge.
Maybe I should've asked my crewmates for some decorations.
Even accounting for luck, I should be doing better than this...
...I knew things might end up like this, but I don't have to be happy about it.
In the bars I used to play in, card games would devolve into fights if one girl lost too quickly...
...How many of these losses could I have avoided?
Mejare's fashion is not meant for this.
...What? I'm not surprised I'm losing.
I don't wear enough for this game...
I'd hoped to stay competitive...
Even with extra support, I can't gain any ground...
...This really is bad luck.
...I'd better learn a lot as the rest of you catch up.
Maybe we should've skipped straight to ambush and capture.
I sure used to have more clothes to wear...
Winning would give me a good memory of Earth for once.
...These may not end up going far enough.
...All things considered, I'm luckier in a cockpit.
...What's there to reflect on? No raising, no folding. Just one card I should've swapped instead...
I could've practiced more with Miss Gasco, or maybe just borrowed her coat...
...When we strip a station bare, there's usually some kind of security.
I should've come wearing the captain's robes...
Nirvana, this is Meia. Reinforcements were ineffective.
Planet Tarak's last line of defense is a minefield. Mine is a thong.

{pyoro}Pyoro~! Another emergency resupply?{!reset}
No...we'll have to leave it to chance.
There has to have been a way I could've played better...besides wearing more.
...What can I say? We don't wear very much. But this isn't over yet.
...If I have to win naked, I will.
...Well, I didn't think this would be easy.
...If I'm actually going to win this, I have my work cut out for me...
It's a shame Cupids are known for their stoicism. Otherwise this costume would fit you much better, Jura...
Kicking off boots, undoing the garter belt...my suit has shoes built right in.
Maybe this'll convince you I'm more woman than monster.
Gascogne won't be happy if I misplace any pieces of this...and there's more than I'm used to.
No, I didn't grow out any pubic hair for the occasion, either...it'd be foolish for just one day.
I can be with my crewmates later to~background.time~. Besides, this is still more modest than some of their clothes.
I'm sure the crew's organizing their Valentine's party, and picking out even skimpier clothes. I'll join up with them later.
...I know that. It's just...
...I get what you're saying. But...
This place never seemed too strict about the rules.
They don't seem to care around here as long as we're naked in the end.
...I hope so. But even then...I'd still like to be a pilot.
We just have to make the best future we can. But in that future...I can't think of another job for myself.
...There's a kind of nostalgia when you step in.
...The second you lower yourself, it's like you're home.
...Mine's always been a mess.
I can't even style mine. It's always stuck out the same way...
...A frontal assault, before swinging around...
We'll start with my bad side, and then do the good one...
I guess that's not the answer you wanted.
...You sound disappointed.
...I believe it.
That was my impression of you two.
I don't feel like I've left an impression yet...
If this counts as taking charge, then...
...This is the world she focuses on.
...She saves that for the human element.

It's fine.
...You should check in on the others.

Don't worry. Focus on the game.
...And the away team.
...So those times really leave an impression.
...And that image is hard to forget?
...Jura just did it at a bad time. She never had a problem to get over...
...Jura was a one-off. When I joined, I had a habit...
That's pretty vague...
..."Prestige"...
Have you tried it yourself?
...Has it worked for you?
It's no big deal...just help make sure it doesn't get lost.
...If I left it on, people would just ask more questions.
...But she never had to deal with you, right?
I don't think you ever had your turn with her.
...How's this?
...This'll have to do.
Well, there's no sense getting excited about them...
If I had yours, maybe it'd be worth a little showmanship...
That's true. We both seem to be better with other girls.
...But among girls, we both have our adoring fans.
...I'd need a new outfit, for one thing.
...I couldn't walk around in this suit anymore.
...Zizou, she dragged me to strip poker game. Jura already doesn't respect me.
That's implying she ever respected me. Remember what kind of game this is.
If Jura had any respect for me, she wouldn't have made me strip naked in public.
She already dragged me here. Jura and respect are like men and women...they don't mix.
...It sounds as if you take in stride whatever Emi demands of you. I hope you feel satisfied with that.
...Maybe you should ask Emi to let you make decisions for once. Unless you're truly happy following her around.
...I see. So Emi tends to take the initiative, and you follow. For some girls, that works...if you're happy.
...I guess that makes Emi the leader, and you the follower. Not every girl can be a leader... but that's your choice.
...You're not the only girl to find me tiresome at first. Or frightening.
...New recruits have a similar first impression of me.
...Rookie pilots often see me in that light. Or they're frightened by "the weird thing on Meia's face."
...I was teased in that sort of way when I first took the position, but only fresh trainees do it now.
...It's not heavy at all, actually. What good would armor be if it weighed me down?
Heavy? It's bulky, but all armor is lightweight. I've read that ancient Earth armor was heavy...poor materials, I assume.
Most of my armor is lightweight padding, Penny. It's only so effective for a pilot...hence why I don't make Jura wear it.
Why would armor be heavy? It's just pressurized. Metal armor is the stuff of history books... even this is hardly effective.
Maybe Earth armor is heavy, but Mejarians build for lightness. Or don't bother at all...it's not much help for a pilot.
...I'm not the Nirvana's captain.
...Our captain is Magno Vivan. I'm the squadron commander...
...I lead our Dread pilots. That doesn't make me the captain...
Don't make a scene...and I'm not the captain, Daria.
...Haru's not bothering me, Jura. Don't go yelling at girls on my behalf...
Leave her alone, Jura. It's not Haru...I'm just making the practical decision.
My headpiece is the least important here, so I'm starting with it. Don't overthink things...and don't start blaming nearby schoolgirls.
Haru has nothing to do with my decision-making...don't start antagonizing her. Where's a safe place to put this?
..."Get it back"? This bar has no right to my belongings. Jura, can you take care of this?
...I'd rather have Jura hold onto it than surrender it to the bar, as you suggest should happen.
I won't be "getting it back," because no one should take it. Maybe you should hold onto it, Jura...
...Penny, you're far too trusting if you'd give anything to the owners here. Jura, could you hold onto this?
She's just overreacting...it was a gift from my Oma.
Jura's just a bit concerned for me...my Oma gave this to me, and I usually keep it on.
Pay her no mind, Ryuji...my Oma gave this to me, that's all.
This was a gift from my Oma. Jura doesn't see me take it off very much...
I'm not...looking for romance. Especially not from a strange woman on another planet.
An interstellar relationship is even more than I bargain for than usual. Drop it.
Jura...don't play matchmaker with me as your test subject. She's from a different planet regardless.
Unless you plan on recruiting her, Jura, we'll never see her again anyway...not that I want a relationship.
I see absolutely no reason to be friendly with this girl...she's done nothing to alleviate my fears.
The very first thing she did was threaten me. Why should I give her a chance?
Sei clearly enjoys escalating situations. She had her chance to prove me wrong and wasted it.
Maybe I'd be more respectful if she were the bigger woman. Instead, she tried to start a fight...
You're very friendly, Yang. Blondes always seem to be...wouldn't you agree, Jura?
You seem like you'd get along with Jura just fine...both amiable, as blondes always seem to be.
Between you and Jura, I have to wonder if blonde hair has genes for friendliness...
Blonde hair and energy seem to be intertwined. Jura was proof enough...and now Yang supports that.
Your occupation is reason enough to stay defensive.
Among crewmates, I might relax...but around a soldier, no chance.
A drunken, belligerent soldier is nearby...I'll let you decide if I relax.
My defensiveness is up to how you conduct yourself, Sei...and whether you swear off your loyalties.
It isn't armor that makes a girl defensive...it's the company she keeps.
...Jura, I'm sorry for ever calling you vulgar. Hearing this girl speak is making me feel dirty.
On and on with your sex-talk...at least Jura has some class about it.
Cameltoe? I need a shower after this game...even Jura's never made me feel that way.
I should've expected a disgusting drunk making passes at me tonight. I never realized how subtle you were, Jura.
"Tight long johns." That's a new one...go ahead and explain, Jura. You love fashion more than I do...
..."Bodysuit," Aella. Or flightsuit...Jura loves talking about clothes, so I'll let her explain.
...You mean my flightsuit? They're certainly popular, but... well, Jura is the expert on these matters.
..."Long johns"? Interesting name for a flightsuit...but I'll let Jura discuss fashion. She'd actually wear different outfits if she had any.
We're not a wealthy enough crew to have private bathrooms, so yes, she has.
We have a communal bathroom, Penny. It's not so awkward when everyone is the same sex.
A ship's crew is like family, Penny. We don't get much bathing privacy---even in the gym, I'm down to my underwear.
We all share bathing accommodations, Penny, as well as anatomy. Jura's seen me naked---and worse.
Earth women are more reserved about their bodies, even to each other, right? Men's presence must do that---we share a bathroom and spa.
Our commander, B.C., came up with it. I couldn't tell you if she's a Buddhist...I'm not sure what that is.
B.C., our commander, named the ship. B.C. is many things...but what a Buddhist is eludes me.
What exactly is a Buddhist? Our commander, B.C., came up with the name...for the record, I suggested the Sonnet.
Our commander came up with it. I don't know what a Buddhist is, but we all submitted names...Jura said "the Luxury Night."
...I'm glad you have a good relationship with her. Unfortunately, Earth's current inhabitants see them as resource farms rather than heritage sites.
...Earth's government sees it fit to strip colonies bare and eradicate them, including their inhabitants. I'm glad not all its citizens agree with that.
...It's encouraging that some Earthlings see value in the extraterrestrial colonies. Your leaders do not, beyond organ harvesting.
Maybe sexuality on Earth is more flexible than I realized. Inhabitants of other colonies always seem appalled when they learn Mejare has no men.
Whenever we encounter colonists from other worlds, they're taken aback by our all-female crew, like men's absence is unnatural. I guess I expected the same reaction here.
..."Straight" and "gay" people? I guess Earth would need extra vocabulary with the presence of another gender.
...Well, we haven't encountered sexes beyond men and women in our travels. It might exist, but if it did, I'd expect Earthlings to know all about it.
I guess that's possible. Though we haven't discovered colonies with a third sex anywhere---men seem to fill every aspect of reproduction that Mejarians use machines for.

This is the first time we've explored outside the Mejarian system, and the first time we've seen men as human beings, so a third sex is possible. But if even Earthlings don't know about it, then it's unlikely.
I'm glad I've kept myself clean for this...is something the matter, Pyrrha? You look concerned...
Fortunately, I'm coming off a fresh shave...is something wrong, Pyrrha?
I've been working on building those connections. Aren't you part of a combat team yourself?
Recent events have caused me to rethink my attitude, so I've been trying to reach out to others. What's your relationship with your teammates?
I've realized that it isn't healthy to try to isolate myself from them, even if I'm their superior. Are you the same way with your teammates?
It took time for me to come around...you're part of a "huntress" team, right? I've found that others are usually happy to open up to you if you start.

state.text: There's nothing enjoyable about crime. Not street crime, anyway...well, it was leading the squadron that made me "get my shit together," Sei.
...Well, leading the squadron is leagues above streetfighting... yes, Sei. Leadership tends to make you "get your shit together."
Streetfighting is not the brand of crime I'd like to return to. Piloting is better...actually, Sei, I was given command so I'd calm down.
You make a life of crime sound fun...I used to streetfight before I became a pirate. ...I fought on the crew, too, Sei. Leadership calmed me down...
If accepting gifts from your Oma is girly, so be it...that's not exactly an insult on Mejare.
I would call a dress girly before a "Sec-Monocle," if that's indeed the name...I wear it because my Oma gave it to me.
I'm capable of being feminine, Sei. But I don't wear it for fashion---my Oma gave it to me.
You're quick to jump to conclusions, Sei...it was a gift from my Oma. Mejare has much girlier accessories.
...You like massages, too, Sei? Well...I'll let Streaming-chan deal with that.
Yes. Massage Sei instead...and stop asking me questions.
...I actually enjoy the stress relief massages provide. Especially my lower back...but I'll leave you both to it.
Sei seems a lot more willing than I am, Streaming-chan. Massage her...I'll just ask our spa attendants.
...Er...well, how about you provide some general details? Their...size, longevity... preferences.
...Well, I did come here to learn about men. Once their tube stands up...how big is it? When does the seed come out?
...I guess you could teach me about men. What are their...tubes like? Do they fit easily?
...I have a few questions about men. How easy is it to handle those tubes of theirs? ...And what do they like in girls?
Any similarities I bear to an Earth celebrity are probably coincidental. ...Something "happened" to her?
..."Rei Ayanami." My ancestors were from Earth...maybe a relative? Hopefully not, if something "happened" to her.
I don't know who that is---or even what an "Eva" is. ...But I'm sorry if she met some awful fate.
...As you might expect, I'm unfamiliar with Earth women, including "Rei Ayanami." ...Sei's concern doesn't bode well.
...With a man? Here? Don't be ridiculous...that goes for you, too, Sei.
What? I wouldn't do that here with a woman, much less a man. ...Did you hear what I said, Sei?
...Maybe I dress like a whore to an Earth girl, but I'm not from Earth. I don't pursue strangers...male or female, Sei.
What makes you think I'm willing to prostitute myself for your audience? ...That goes for you, too, Sei.
...I like large, open, empty spaces. ..."Cozy" is a word I rarely use.
The only small space I feel comfortable in is my Dread. ...And I wouldn't call it "cozy."
...I like open spaces. And I dislike crowds for filling them...no, Sei, it's not cozy at all.
The Nirvana can be cramped, with so many of us packed onto an old ship. I don't like it...and it certainly isn't "cozy."
Since they look like men's tubes, Mejare's government cracks down on toys...well, Sei, you're just used to having them.
The government prefers toys be kept small and simple. ...Otherwise, we'd be like Earth women and love men's tubes.
The Mejare Empire fears us growing attached to the shape of men's tubes...well, we hardly know what we're missing, Sei.
We're trained from a young age to avoid toys...they resemble men too much. ...If you're used to having them, Sei, then I guess it would be boring.
...You were right, Sei. What an awful girl...
...Dwelling on death makes it impossible to live. Sei, this girl is insufferable...
...Sei, this girl makes you look much more tolerable.
The captain keeps a shrine of crew members who've passed. ...But that won't be enough for her, will it, Sei?

case.state: Oh, you two...are together. I was curious how men and women treat each other as couples...teasing is typical on my homeworld, too.
...Wait, Adrien is---your partner, then. You're just teasing him...female couples on Mejare do that, too.

...It's my responsibility.
...And I doubt you'd go easier on them in my place, Jura.
I hear you've taken pretty authoritative command in my absence, Jura. Maybe we're not so different... anyway, it's an important job, Reimu.
...It's true. Maybe there's something about being opposites that lets us understand each other.
...You're the most social on the crew, and I'm the least. Maybe there's something comforting in that contrast.
I could see how a man pantsing you feels more threatening than the locker-room game it is between girls. Normally, I'd have no underwear for him to grab.
I see. None of our prisoners have tried to rip our underwear off, thankfully. Tonight is a rare time I'm actually wearing some.
That sounds like the bizarre strategies the man in my squadron comes up with. We're pirates---we'll accept any plan that works.
"Underhanded tactics" might be inherent to men's battle strategies, based on my male pilot. Our pirate crew welcomes that if we succeed.
Are these tactics effective? We left our honor behind when we became pirates---the male pilot on my team has won battles for us in creative ways.

condition.saying: nowhere near as interested in men as she is

case.state: ...No, I don't. Trying to deceive you would only mean we'd learn less.
...This visit is our one chance to learn about Earth. Lying about what we want would waste it.

condition.saying: Your blonde companion can come along too

case.state: Jura and I are both in the assault team, not command. You would have to make that request of our captain.
Dread pilots don't accept missions for the crew. Our captain makes those decisions.
Neither of us have the authority to order the crew on a mission. We're the pilots sent to carry them out.
I'm not looking to have children, either. The mechanics of even doing that with a man are...not clear to me.
...I appreciate that a man might be similar to me, but I'm not interested in having children with him, either. However that would work.
...I knew what you meant. Keeping one's hair short is definitely less common on Mejare...but more common among pirates.
I know, Marinette. My hair looks nothing like the female Corrin's...or indeed like most girls'.
I know, Marinette. I used to think about hairstyles much more...and I know that keeping it short is not very womanly.
...I wasn't confused. The female Corrin wears her hair long...which is a more feminine trait. Pirates are less likely to do that.
...If you're afraid of not being liked, you might not realize when you are.
...If they really do like you, then they want to see you like yourself.

Sanako?
...It does kind of remind me of my old idol dresses.

...I see. I wasn't aware Mejare's moons were inhabited. It makes sense---the Magno Family has settled in the nearby asteroids.
...Have you made your home on a Mejarian moon or asteroid? There's no other way to "see" it without satellites.
...No "fancy machines." Monitoring a planet is a trivial engineering task. What are you trying to say, Yuelia?
...I wouldn't call a satellite "fancy." What do you use, then? Or do you live that close?
...My Dread is a fancy machine, Yuelia. A basic orbital satellite is not...how are you watching, then?
...Only a primitive people would call satellites "fancy." And yet you can "watch" Mejare? Either you live nearby, or you're trying to confuse me.
...Erm. I'm sorry if I was overexcited just now, Yuelia. I command a Dread team on a pirate ship.
...Excuse me. I shouldn't act overeager like that...I've gotten my piloting experience working for a pirate crew.
...Ahem. I'm sorry about that, Yuelia. I should be more composed. I'm not actually formally trained---I'm part of a pirate group.
...I'm sorry. That was a bit much on my part. I wish I could've gone to school for piloting---I actually work for pirates as a squadron commander.
...Ahem. Well, it's been the focus of my life for quite some time now. I work for pirates, so there is little time for other pursuits.
...Excuse me for that. If I were a pilot for Mejare's empire, I might have time for other hobbies, but I'm a pirate---it's my passion by necessity.
...I'm sorry. I was overenthusiastic there. I do enjoy piloting, but I'm a pirate---I couldn't pursue much else if I wanted to.
...Erm. I shouldn't oversell my situation. It was a meaningful role I could take with the pirates I fell into, and piracy allows for little else.
That's...a nice outlook to have, Yuelia. Thank you...I'm accustomed to seeing function first and foremost on our ship.
...I guess you're right. Maybe I'm too used to practicality thanks to piloting.
...In a sense, yes, that's still doing something. I've tried to avoid being too sentimental... broken equipment is dead weight for pirates.
A life of piracy will cause you to judge machines on their function. But you're right...a memento is meaningful.
...It's the least I can do. I have some other things as well---a music box, and a sample from their laboratories. But those don't frighten recruits as much.
...They didn't leave behind much else. New recruits usually stare at it for a while...I don't show them the other heirlooms I have.
Most girls join our crew with few possessions. I myself only had that headpiece and a few other things...it tends to intimidate rookies.
...It's the only memento I wear around and show others. It helps identify me as "the scary girl with the thing on her face."
"Mother"? Oh, right...like a Fama. That sounds nice...I'm glad you have something to remember her by.
...A "mother" is the woman who carried you, right? With a male parent...I'm glad you could bond with her.
...Right. You have "mothers" and "fathers" here instead of Omas and Famas. In any case, I'm glad you cherish that.
"Mother"...like a Fama, if I remember correctly. I wish I'd spent more time making things with my parents...
Competing isn't meant to be fun. I'm overcoming an obstacle---forced exposure on an unfamiliar planet.
I don't see the fun in competitions like this. I do see a springboard for self-improvement, win or lose.
Fun is found in pastimes, not competitions. A picnic, for example...or any time shared with loved ones.
When I picture a fun time, I think of relaxing in a spa---something with no winners, losers, or failure. A game is meant to expose your weaknesses.
...There's no danger for an Earth girl. Our crew is a known target of this planet.
No danger to you, maybe. My job demands constant vigilance, especially on an aggressor like Earth.
...Yuelia, part of my role as officer is to patrol and scout ahead for danger. And Earth has attempted to kill us before.
As long as I'm here on Earth, danger is always present. I do enough scouting for their attack fleets when we're lightyears away.
I don't like how luck-based this form of poker is. There's no betting to make things interesting...but I can still try to read each of you.
It's true that the primary strategy here seems to be "wear more clothing." Still, I can reflect upon whether I judged my opponents correctly.
Even in a dogfight, there is an element of luck. It's far too high here, I agree...but I can still make predictions based on body language.
I agree, Yuelia... especially since there's no betting. But even if reading my opponents isn't much help here, I can still practice doing so.
There are more pressing matters than my naked body, and I must remain positive around them, too, for the sake of my pilots.
...Well, part of my job is maintaining a positive outlook in the face of an enemy fleet---or at least making sure others do so.
"Collected" may be a better word. If I can't keep my composure when naked, I can't keep my pilots calm on a mission.
The other crew members see me naked all the time. Besides, nudity is no issue next to a raid in terms of morale.
...The image of confidence is one of a leader's most important qualities.
...A leader has to project confidence, even if she isn't sure what to do.
...Confidence is more a tool than a state of mind. It is meant to keep your subordinates calm.
...I'm quite practiced at appearing that way. Confidence is to reassure others, not yourself.
...One at a time, Amy. Those are all complicated questions.
...I appreciate your curiosity, but none of those are simple topics. Please focus.
...Slow down. Each of those would require some explanation.
...Which of those are you most curious about? We can start there.
...The more decisions a girl makes, the more her appearance reflects them. Life imitates art, I guess.
It's not so strange an idea. Our choices in life will go to inform our appearances, much like a character in a book.
...My hair color may be a coincidence, but past decisions will determine how a girl dresses and carries herself. It makes sense.
Fiction comes from observing real-life women. Poise, posture, dress...none of those things come separate from our personalities and pasts.
Maybe Earth's resources were more scarce than I'd realized. What are you lacking? Do you not have cotton or synthetic fibers?
What are your complaints with your underwear, Amy? Even simple cotton bras and panties should suffice for a civilian.
All I wear underneath is supportive training gear. Maybe basic underwear is a luxury on Earth...what does yours not provide, Amy?
I've never had a desire for more "advanced" underwear. Mine is supportive, and other kinds are to be attractive...what are you looking for?
..."Dykes"? You've now used two words I haven't understood...
...Which is it, "dykes" or "lesbos"? I'm not familiar with either...
...First "lesbos," now "dykes." Young girls lack perspective on what others understand...
...I thought your issue was with "lesbos," Mary. Now you've switched to "dykes."
...So, you'd only wear skintight clothing as an underlayer. I'd heard Earth girls were more conservative...is it because of men's presence?
...Is it part of Earth culture to not expose your figure, even in spandex? Maybe to avoid tempting men...
...So you would wear skintight shorts, but never by themselves. Is Earth girls' extra layering a defense measure against men?
...I guess with how aggressive men can be, Earth girls hide their bodies. Your shorts would suffice on Mejare without any layers over them.
...If you could explain what "ECHO" technology is used for, I would appreciate it.
...I haven't heard of "ECHO" technology. Are they wearable scanning devices?
...This isn't the technology you're thinking of...we don't have anything called an "ECHO." What is it?
My parents put a stop to me doing anything too dangerous...while they were around. I fended for myself on the streets after that.
...Once I came home with some bruises, my parents put a tighter leash on me. Once they were gone, I learned how to fight just fine.
...It started as typical teenage interest, but my parents quashed it when I started fighting. Then they weren't around for that...and I kept fighting.
...On top of the danger, it ruined the cutesy image of me my parents had marketed themselves on. But once I was alone, it was me and my fists.
...That doesn't surprise me. In my experience, Earth views many of its colonies as "unnatural."
...Mejare and Tarak represent the ultimate breakdown in communication between men and women. Still, there's more to relationships than sharing a sex.
I guess I have no place to talk when it comes to understanding men, nor does any Mejarian. But if they're really human like you and me, then it must be possible.
I knew men don't have uteri---our male doctor was apparently baffled when he first scanned one. But I figured those egglike sperm-holders had cycles...
I knew men don't carry their children, but they have those dangling sphere-organs that hold sperm. I assumed it'd function like a uterus wall...
...Men have those round ball-like organs hanging near their rods, don't they? If they hold sperm, I assumed they'd behave like the organs that hold our eggs...
See, it's off already...I think the armor you're used to may be archaic.
No, I can get it off with no issue...maybe you could show me some of yours.
It's made of a rather light shock-absorbent material, actually...maybe you wear the metal armor I've read about.
I've read that women on Earth used to don metal armor. That sounds more like the impractical plating you're describing...
...Mejare as a colony is only about 100 years old. Even if that were enough time to speciate, the planet is terraformed---there's no pressure to do so.
A few generations on a terraformed planet like Mejare is neither enough time nor the proper environment to cause us to evolve into a different species.
...You have the right idea, yes. Incidentally, it's good to see that you're still alive...I wasn't sure you'd be.
...Yes, Mejarian sex is rather intimate. I'm glad to see you've continued your piracy without any injuries...
...I've recently learned that to be the case, thanks to our male prisoners...
...That's true. There are men I've come to respect...the prisoners aboard our ship.
...I was certainly taught men were all the same, and less than human at that. I know that's not true, thanks to the men we captured...
...Is that so? Who are these colleagues of yours, and how do they hide it?
...I know men aren't all the same. I was taught that you were, but when I first saw one in person, part of me knew you were human...
...I used to maintain that men were savage animals, like everyone on my homeworld. Still, seeing one in person on my first raid...he had a human face.
...I'm aware now that men are as human as women are. Deep down, I think any Mejarian who sees a man in person realizes that...
...I imagine a man carrying a rocket launcher would avoid fighting at close range.
...You seem perfectly fit for a man, Brock. Though I guess wielding explosives would encourage you to fight at a distance...
...I'm still not sure why I would want to a be a brawler. Are you saying you fight for a living?
Much like how we're not to fire missiles at close range...are you a pirate, as well? Why are you in firefights?
...I'm sure you have last resorts at close range. But I'm part of a pirate group...why are you always fighting?
...You're correct. A missile's power comes with the danger of using it up close...I'm sure you're familiar.
...Yes. Dread pilots face a similar issue with our bombs if the enemy is too close...it's good you understand that.
...There must be some respected status among men known as a "brawler." I'm not familiar...
...You sound very complimentary, but I'm not familiar with why being a "brawler" is so valued in a man's eyes.
...I'm not accustomed to male culture. I understand you enjoy tests of physical strength...is that why you respect me as a "brawler"?
...I didn't claim to be proud of my streetfights. Is "Brawling" some kind of rite of passage in male culture?
...I know it's lowbrow. I had to face that when I started fights with crew members...is "Brawling" some specific men's activity I don't know about?
...I've heard that men enjoy fighting each other for sport. You sound excited that I might "brawl"...but it's not something a woman values.
...I guess this is where men and women differ. A man might be proud of his time streetfighting, but it's quite degrading in a woman's eyes...
...I guess Max can be a girl's name, as well. A woman wearing a bodysuit makes more sense...though I'm now trying to picture a man in one.
...It's good to hear you have female colleagues...it's good to know that they're the ones in bodysuits. Though I'm curious if a man could pull one off.
My mistake. At least you get along with women on this planet...you donning a skintight suit would probably amuse her.
Hm. I might like to meet this girl you know, then...we share a fashion sense. She'd probably laugh if you stuffed yourself into a suit like hers...
...Maybe I should've realized that. I need to remind myself that men and women live together here...
...My apologies. I'm not used to men who have female colleagues... even on a planet full of them.
...A man, I assume. I guess men and women's names may have become frozen on my homeworld, but continued to evolve on Earth...
A female Max, and a male Sandy...I shouldn't expect names to be gendered the same on Earth. Is "Meia" a female name here?
...I wouldn't know how to seduce a man. And if I did, my goal would not be to stuff you into my flightsuit...
...It would be a challenge for me to seduce a man when I don't know what you like. And I'm not interested in seeing you stretch my suit out.
I guess one could tailor a suit to fit a man's body. It'd need broader shoulders, wider sleeves and legs...a smaller butt.
I see...Max is a girl's name on Earth. Lasers and tight suits are standard aesthetics for a Mejarian...but what does she use to run?
I see. Mejarian girls, too, value lasers and tight clothing...and speed. But in flight, not running.
Is that so? My Dread is respected as the fastest in our fleet. What technology is this that she uses to run so quickly?
On the ground, maybe. No one outpaces my ship. Technology to run fast is new to me---how does it work?
...You may have a skewed impression of what a healthy blood sugar is. Self-starvation does not lead to muscle gain.
...I don't tell them to starve themselves---not that it would make them fit regardless. Don't frame your eating habits as typical.
...I suppose, if your goal is to delude yourself and those attempting to help you.
...The doctor would probably notice that she weighs less, as well. If you're not interested in really losing weight, why bother seeing her?
...If you're not seeing results, then maybe you could describe your current exercise routine.
...What do you for your exercise regimen? If it isn't structured, then no wonder it isn't working.
Many of our fresh recruits would agree with you. I ensure they follow my orders, and the reality of dogfighting does the rest.
We tend to recruit girls who have problems with authority. They also think I'm condescending until their first raid.
To disgruntled young women off the streets, sternness can indeed seem like condescension. It takes a raid for them to understand.
...So you are still fighting. Meanwhile, my pilots look to me for a cool head in battle...even as my breasts come out.
...So even as a singer, the need for violence remains. A Dread team leader's role is precisely to not be excited during battle...
...Yes. To delay doing so would draw attention to them.
...That is my intention, yes. To start with my smallest item...
...Yes. It makes the most sense to do so...at least with no context.
...Yes, size generally determines what girls will strip first. Even if it's unusual...
...Men, you mean? Yes, I'd agree---the men I know have a habit of involving themselves in my business.
...Men are? I can vouch for that---our doctor tries to give me advice, our helmsman tries to chat, and our mech pilot combines with my Dread.
...I don't care for nosy people. If you mean men, then I agree---the man in my squadron goes as far as intruding into my cockpit when we combine ships.
...Men are nosy? Well, forming a Vandread with a man means I'm stuck in my cockpit with him, so I'm inclined to agree...
Men are a nosy, intrusive people. I know three of them, and they're all nosy... imagine how I feel knowing each has saved my life.
I'm afraid that's not true at the moment...Earth is convinced they are the only "true" humans, and they see other human settlements as resource farms.
I also hope that one day human settlements across the galaxy will be preserved. Unfortunately, Earth is currently ransacking them to preserve itself.
...If it comforts you, Mejare's all-female society is hardly a utopia. Still, men's presence seems much more jarring.
I'm sure you could become accustomed to it---it is nice to share anatomy with everyone around you.
I have an equally hard time picturing life when half the population is larger than me, with dangling appendages between their legs...
Men's absence leads to a much simpler understanding of what it means to be a human, if you ask me. I'm sure you can relate to other women better.
Even if you're used to men being around, surely you must understand other women more easily. You'd grow accustomed to Mejare.
...Well, you're not my subordinate. Nor would I get much information by barking orders at you.
I'd like to think I'm above the standard of abusive prison guards. I'm here to socialize, after all.
"Boring" is a very mild insult. New recruits have gone much further, and their insults risk undermining my authority.
I can't take much away from a girl I barely know calling me "boring." New pilots do that, too. It starts to sound familiar.
Part of being an officer is learning to weather the insults of young girls who are trying to get a rise out of me.
I'm not sure how you could miss them, frankly. Unless you somehow acquired a propaganda source from Tarak's founders.
It's possible Tarak's founding men left behind historical accounts that remove all traces of women. I don't know how else we could be omitted from colonial records.
It's not my intention to raid this place. I'm here to learn about my ancestral planet and its inhabitants.
I'm not here as a pirate, nor would I act as one alone. I'm seeking information on Earth and its man-woman customs.
I'm here as a tourist. I don't mean you any harm---and on that subject, I would recommend you carry a weapon for self-defense, not an attack dog.
If I were here to attack you, I'd be in my Dread as part of our fleet, not playing cards alone. This is a cultural visit.
I don't have many other clothes in the first place, Myriam. Nor did I suspect this system could be so easily gamed by wearing more.
...You may find it hard to believe, Myriam, but this flightsuit is the most elaborate clothing I have. I also expected more emphasis on poker skill.
...Are you saying I look out of shape, Myriam? I do my best to maintain my figure.
...I exercise because I have to fit in my suit, Myriam. Are you saying I look squeezed into it?
Mejare's culture is built upon the celebration of excess. We do have far more resources than the men's planet, Tarak---but that means the elites see fit to waste them.
Mejarians waste resources on a massive scale just to one-up each other. The planet is beautiful as a result, but not everyone gets to enjoy it.
My homeworld values outer beauty above all. A few civilian districts are nothing if it means the imperial class can continue to gild their gardens.
I'm afraid Earth is our enemy, as well. They consider themselves to be the true human race and see extraplanetary colonists as expendable.
Earth might provide a suitable living space if they weren't also seeking our execution. In their case, it's for our being colonists rather than women.
That's not possible. Earth is Mejare's enemy, too---in fact, it's the enemy of every colony, Tarak included.
Earth is just as hostile to us as Tarak is, if not more so. Its aim to subjugate every colony---they were the reason we were forced to cooperate with our male prisoners.
We haven't encountered any other female colonies ourselves. Maybe it was settled before egg-splicing was perfected, so men were kept around to reproduce.
Maybe Mejare isn't the only human settlement dominated by women. If Gamindustri has a small proportion of men, it may be a primitive version of Mejare before women could reproduce on their own.
I don't know enough about other planets to say that. But life on Mejare can be ruthlessly competitive, and those at the bottom of the social ladder have to band together. That includes me.
It takes a stronger connection than body parts to form friendships, man or woman. Our crew is tight-knit, but that's because we're all outlaws.
...No, I don't think so. Not all of the planet is habitable, but pre-colonization scans would have picked up on large, aggressive life forms.
Unless there's monsters on the less industrialized continents, then I don't think so. Even then, we would have detected their presence by now via satellite.
...I don't know for sure, but this doesn't appear to be the Earth of my time. The Earth our crew knows is ecologically devastated.
Earth is Mejare's ancestral homeworld, but this appears to be a version of it that predates the frontier era. For one thing, its atmosphere is intact.
Earth is nearly uninhabitable in my time, and its moon has spun out of orbit. From what I can tell, this is a time before it developed space travel---and its hostility.
I serve the Magno Family pirate outfit of planet Mejare. Though we've recently become closer to vigilantes, as a hostile attack force from Earth has been targeting our homeworld.
Our enemy as of late has been Earth, as its Harvester fleets are attacking our homeworld of Mejare. But we're pirates, so Mejare itself had been our enemy up to this point.
I suspect that this isn't the Earth of my time---for instance, its moon is still in orbit. That may be why you aren't familiar with its colonies.
That might be another reason you don't know of Mejare. There are several factors that lead me to believe that this is a pre-colonial Earth---such as its moon.
That sounds similar to the Omas and Famas of Mejarian couples. Girls who are more outgoing and driven tend to become Omas, while Famas are demure and carry children.
...So, women were once meant to care for children, while men did riskier work. That's not unlike the Fama and Oma women of Mejarian couples, respectively.
...Maybe I took too much offense to that. You'd have to ask a doctor---I never received higher education.
It sounds like the kind of thing one would learn in advanced genetics classes. I dropped out of school as a teenager, when I was relocated.
I didn't finish enough school to learn biology at that level. A doctor from Mejare might be able to tell you more.
When we were at our hideout near Mejare, I used to have more breaks. But I'm the only chief pilot on our ship at the moment, so no one else can fulfill my duties completely.
No, I don't. Our ship is stranded away from our hideout on Mejare, and I'm the only pilot of my rank present. So any breaks I used to get are gone.

condition.saying: Just a little quid pro quo

case.state: It's dangerous to believe otherwise. People who are convinced they're perfect are capable of horrifying things.
Not everyone find flaws in themselves. All it takes is an idea of perfection for someone to be convinced that nothing else has a right to exist.
It wasn't totally by choice...there's a large magnetic storm cutting Mejare off from its neighbors. But our nearest neighbor is Tarak, which is inhabited---by men.
Other colonies refer to Mejare as "beyond the Great Magnetic Storm," which has probably done the most to isolate it. We do have one neighbor---Tarak, the male planet.
It's not completely isolated---Mejare has a sister planet called Tarak, where men live. But a magnetic storm makes traveling beyond that dangerous.
We were horrified to discover it, as well. Every planet deals with them differently---some worship them as gods of sacrifice, while others try to survive in a poisoned environment.
...It's sickening. As the Dread team leader, I don't go down on the ground much, but I've heard--- ecological destruction, ritualistic sacrifice, resistances crushed.
Its founders split off from the male colonists on their ship, and we artificially splice egg cells to have children. I asked you a question in return.
Women's DNA can be combined via machine, and male colonists settled on Mejare's sister planet Tarak when they were founded. Answer my question before you ask more.
...That won't be necessary. From what I could see from orbit, Earth has many natural beaches.
...You don't need to do that. I saw a lot of coastline between the clouds when I approached Earth.
...So, you would prefer women's company. I'm not used to hearing men say that.
...So, most men there would rather have women present. Is that right?
We've found that, as well. Male or female, our enemy treats us the same. It's hard to ignore each other's humanity in a situation like that.
...That's right. It was because of our common enemy that we didn't just throw them out the airlock. But because of that, we've found how human we both are.
They each have strengths, which is why we kept them around. The ship only responds to our helmsman, and another is our only doctor. One joined my team as a mech pilot.
Yes---navigation, medical expertise, and mech piloting. We were already shorthanded---the men were all we had to fill those roles.
Other colonists we've met also think it's unusual to not have men around. They might attribute Mejare's social problems to that.
Mejare has its social issues---the existence of pirates is evidence of that. Most colonists seem to think men are necessary for a society to function.

condition.saying: big, ugly men with machine guns

case.state: That sounds like a fitting description for Tarakkians. But I doubt they have any contact with Earth, either.
"Big, ugly men with machine guns" describes Tarakkian soldiers very well. Still, they're unlikely to be who you mean.

condition.saying: stealing from them aren't mutually exclusive

case.state: That's true, but our crew has enough enemies as it is. Attacking random civilians won't help us.
You're right to be suspicious, but we don't attack civilians. We're also not seeking any more enemies at the moment.
It seems like there's few places where men and women aren't together on Earth. So much so that schools for girls have a strange reputation.
...So, girls and boys usually go to school together. You seem to coexist almost everywhere.
I only command our Dread team. Who or what we attack is not my decision.
I'm a junior officer---you would have to propose that to our captain. She usually avoids hiring us out.
...Is that how Earthlings see themselves, even in this era? Gods?
...Earthlings from my time have come to see themselves as gods. That tradition must run deep.
...Thank you. I guess you expected drinking and gambling, but many of us are formerly upper-class.
Most of us come from wealthy backgrounds. They're trying to recreate their old home lives.
...I'm not sure. I wouldn't want either of us to depend on the other.
...I haven't given that much thought. I can take care of myself...I'd want to be with someone who can do that, too.
It was a biological experiment. The Earth of my time plans to harvest our reproductive organs.
It was part of a conspiracy with Earth to create a planet where the uterus could be harvested from the population.
Even with your supernatural powers, I doubt you can even survive in a vacuum. This Earth must be primitive if that's your idea of space travel.
Do you have no concept of space travel in this time period? You would need a ship, even if you have the power to fly.
Space itself is very beautiful. Our ship has an open terrace for stargazing---I come visit there when it's quiet.
If you've seen Earth from space, it's very beautiful. All planets are, as are the stars and comets.
It's easy to hate an enemy you've never met. I learned men were "diseased," and according to them, we paralyze them and eat their entrails.
"Men carry diseases. Stay away." That's all I learned as a girl. Apparently, they learned women sap their energy and suck out their organs.
I agree that they're flattering. It doesn't bother me---if I can't hide my figure, then I have to maintain it.
I see that tightness as motivation to exercise. I can't hide how I look from others.
Typically, one woman will donate an egg to be spliced with one of the other's, who carries the baby. You sound like you're dependent on men to have children.
An Oma and Fama combine the DNA from their egg cells to have children. I know men have those sperm cells, but you make them sound like they're indispensable.
You're the first to flirt with me. Our prisoners are men from Tarak, a planet with no women.
The men I have met are just as unfamiliar with women, so you've been the most forward.
I've observed some differences. Height and body proportions... reproductive organs, obviously. But you must mean in personality.
...Are you talking about our behavior? Just from this game, I can point out lots of differences in our bodies.
This time period seems primitive, but there probably exist maps of the constellations. That will show all of space that you can see from Earth.
This era must be before space travel developed. I remember learning that Earthlings started by mapping the stars, so try looking for those.

Of course our "worlds" are different. I grew up on an all-female Earth colony.
...Are you talking about magic?
...I come from an Earth colony called Mejare. Our worlds are naturally different. What are you implying...?
...I heard there were protests. Women felt that the land was their Mejarian birthright. I was young, but I could tell they weren't getting it back.
I was just a girl. I sat in the shelter during the fallout. Whatever protests happened, nothing came of them.
Mejarian soldiers are well-accommodated, so it's a matter of capturing the right ship. That provides "excitement" in itself...
If you mean our standard of living, it's as good as the ships we can capture. A lot of money goes into the Mejarian Border Guard.
According to her, it's because you can't win at cards without controlling your emotions. She's also strong enough to keep us from storming off.
None of us can overpower her, and you can't win poker by showing how you feel. Your only recourse is to sit still and calm down.
You can introduce yourself if you give me a reason to take you prisoner.
If a man finds himself anywhere near her, he's probably our prisoner. A man like you would definitely be in handcuffs.
We're not looking for more male recruits. And the regisystem is not on the way to the brig.
No. We've learned our lesson about bringing men of your sort aboard.
It's sparked a change in all of us. Even now---stripping naked near a man. That'd have sounded like a death wish to me not long ago---from infection.
...Maybe it's men saving my life that's made me comfortable enough to be naked near one. A year ago, I'd have compared that to jumping into medical waste.
Our crew already had reason to doubt what we'd been told. Most Mejarians have never seen a man at all, and we've had to herd captive soldiers.
If any Mejarians could be convinced, it'd be us---we'd actually seen men in person just from raiding Tarak. I remember thinking how one had a face like mine.
Mejarians would never touch a man, let alone have their seed injected inside them. Even we used to wear lined suits around them for fear of falling ill.
There are no men, period. No one would want to go near them---we're taught men are diseased.
Mejarians believe that men are covered in dangerous germs. No one would want them as slaves, even to reproduce.
No, we don't keep slaves. If you asked a young Mejarian girl to draw a picture of a man, she'd make a human-shaped cloud of germs.
The Magno Family's stated enemies are the governments of Mejare and Tarak. We attack their border guards for resources---never civilians.
Our planets' leaders have robbed their own people of their homes. The Magno Family raids their military outposts.
The Magno Family was formed because Mejare left us homeless. We take advantage of its war with Tarak to target both planets' border patrols.
