...I'm not sure that's right. Is "the Colony" a whole settlement? We're not part of Mejare anymore.
...I know. I guess it all just reminds me of old times too much. With my parents...
I don't have a problem with you, either. It's...I think it's old memories cropping up.
Maybe the enemy territory woke up her fighting spirit.
She's a fighter, and Earth is hostile. She probably couldn't help herself.
...I check the grounds, and you check the food. Together we'll gather all the intel we need.
I guess the refreshments are part of our recon, too.
Jura, if we were able to come here, then so is the enemy. Don't make excuses.
If you don't want to keep an eye out, Jura, then don't volunteer for a scouting party. You can still enjoy yourself while keeping watch.

I'm not embarrassed by Misty, either.
...But she doesn't need to follow me everywhere.
...Misty can be a little much sometimes.

I can't answer your question how you want, Darkness.
...I've never been with a girl I liked.
I've been with girls, but...it wasn't about what I liked. Or who.
If sparring counts, we've wrestled. Our team goes through all sorts of combat training.
You're thinking of a real fight, Jura. We've all done some sparring with each other.
Tight is fine...but I'd rather play to my strengths.
I like tight clothes. But I like ones that emphasis my...good side.
...That's true. I've had a lot on my mind. Haven't you?
...The thoughts keeping me up aren't too different from yours.
...I did. The question is if this is all the Paksis's doing---or something else entirely.
...The exact same. The Paksis drew us here...or maybe something drew it here.
Your guess is as good as mine...
...Don't ask me.
Having different approaches is good for the team.
Our team tries to incorporate everyone's strengths.
...I never delegate command. You never request it.
I should let you gain experience...and you should ask me to.
But it's not like the red one we know. And it feels---distant, like it's watching the planet from afar.
The original one, before it split. But it'd be a lot stronger if it were really here...
That sounds about right. Just don't keep us waiting too long.
If you tease too much, they'll get bored. Even you're not perfect.
...It's just---I try to avoid this sort of thing. It's different from watching you change.
...Tch. The showers are one thing, but a game like this---I just feel kind of removed from it.
...Isn't that the kind of dynamic you have with Barnette?
...I'd have to make room for Barnette first.

~player~?
...When I said I spend time nude with my crewmates, I meant the girls.
...Do you really trust him that much? I wouldn't try to get to know our male crew members naked.

~player~...?
If you know her well enough, then sure. You can build a lot of trust naked.
You're already friends with her, right? There's something nice about having nothing to hide and still trusting them.
...Erufuda, you are in no position to tell someone that exercise is unnecessary. Stay out of this.
...Erufuda, you are not qualified to offer any fitness advice to either me or my pilots. This is a private matter.
This is between me and a subordinate, Erufuda. And you are the last girl Jura should listen to for exercise advice.
..."World order"? Maintaining that means different things to different people.
...Things like "darkness" and "world order" are pretty vague.
...Would you never do this with your teammates, Yae?
Are you saying you're not as close with your own group, Yae?
...If you think there's something wrong with us, you sure seem to like it.
...They're tireless enough to serve you. Like me, or her, or Barnette.
I assume she just means getting out for a change.
...I'd take that to mean socializing.
...I guess it isn't fair of me to try and do everything myself. I can tutor you if you'd like, Jura.
...Do you want me to teach you how to lead the team, Jura? It's time I would've just spent patrolling---you're usually with Barnette.
It's a warning, not a rumor. If you ever feel unwell, Sayori, try to remove yourself from this girl.
...I don't know about your state of mind, Sayori, but I already feel on edge around her. That's my warning, if you ever do.
...No, I was too young for that. I didn't work at all until I joined our crew---the captain even said I was spoiled.
...Working for our crew has been my only job. A lot of us grew up being handed everything.
...I see what you mean. When I lived on Mejare's surface, there was only land.
...Right. There's nothing like it back home---Mejare doesn't have any oceans.
This is extreme if you want to be less shy. Bars always have people who try to take advantage of others.
...Why don't you tell us what you are, then. Instead of what you're not.

We can't afford to be reckless here.
...Aren't you going to explain yourself?
...I see. I'm afraid my piracy is limited to the material. Maybe you could help explain the methods, Ryuji.
...Is that so? We tend to steal...food, fuel, and weapons. Care to explain how you do this, Ryuji?
...You really don't seem the type. Ryuji, you seem excited. Care to explain how this is done?
...That doesn't sound like it would help people. Maybe you could elaborate...with the assistance of your male classmate here.
Not as good as she should be. If I had my way, she'd toss it and practice with a laser ring instead.
Not enough to make up for always lugging it around on missions. A laser ring is all she should need.
She herself will admit she doesn't practice enough, Penny. Of course, practice with a laser ring would be better.
She's decent enough with a laser ring, and that's all she would ever need as a weapon. The rapier is superfluous.
...I maintain the professional opinion that her rapier is suboptimal next to a standard laser ring.
Pirates don't exactly get the height of privacy...and I should've figured you'd gang up on me.
I swear Jura shows me respect when we're actually piloting...this is her chance to enlist help teasing me.
...Right. I should've known you'd both start pestering me...I'll be planning flight practices.
Yes, Sei, I've seen Jura naked...she's indeed very beautiful. Have fun irritating me with her.
Jura is a colleague, not a friend. Pirates don't get to choose who they work with...which is a good skill regardless.
We're more coworkers than friends...and we don't get a choice in coworkers. We ended up working with men, after all.
"BFF"? Oh...friends. We met and work together out of circumstance more than anything...
I'm not terribly fond of Jura's approach to work, so friend is a stretch. She's tolerable as a colleague.
It seems that's the peril of working in the military. Pirates aren't so quick to cast their comrades aside.
Well, unlike the military, we don't consider our members expendable. Personal teasing isn't worth a reprimand.
Pirates are united by being outcasts. I couldn't discharge Jura like in the military---she has nowhere to go.
Then you understand our distaste for the military, Miss Misato. Respect is earned among pirates, and lives aren't just numbers.
...Just as I presume her every move, Jura thinks I'm secretly a pervert because she's obviously one.
Don't pay attention to her, Sei. She doesn't understand how not everyone is as sex-obsessed as she is.
This is how Jura rationalizes my work ethic. She presumes I'm as lustful as she is and merely trying to hide it.
...Don't let my suit fool you. This is standard Mejarian fashion...Jura just wants to pretend I can't be more disciplined than she is.
As if I'd let a soldier see me sweat. Any plans Jura had failed when you came along.
Maybe on a lighter table, I'd feel embarrassed. Against military personnel, I only know competition.
Embarrassed? Not with a soldier skulking around. Jura's teasing is none of my concern now.
With a military woman haunting this table, Jura's matchmaking is the least of my concerns. I'm watching you.
For once, I agree. Wearing small things is clearly part of the game...so she's free to choose them.
I take no issue with what Jura's doing. Pirates need to be resourceful...and my second-in-command should be sharp.
It sounds as if you're jealous of Jura's forethought, Sei. You started with plenty on yourself...

state.text: Using what we have to win is not dragging out the game. This is the kind of resourcefulness I expect from my subordinates.

case.state: Why did you bring a sword in the first place?
That's not really clothing, Lyn.
This is just a game...on your home planet, I assume. Why are you armed?
You don't practice enough with your rapier, Jura. It just weighs you down.
...Speaking of swords, your laser ring would've been a better weapon to bring than your rapier, Jura.
I---don't bring up Kahlua. We barely know these people.
You---don't tell her our life stories, Jura. Kahlua has nothing to do with this.
If you knew I liked spending time with Kahlua, why didn't you just leave me with her again?
Any charm I had has been crushed by being dragged here...and leave Kahlua out of this.
I and the other pirates I work with clash with Mejare's military on a regular basis. ...Do you do something similar, Jolyne?
It's hard to be a pirate and not grow a distaste for soldiers. ...Oh, are you a pirate, too, Jolyne?
I pilot for a pirate crew. Hating imperial soldiers comes with the job. ...Did you face prison time for something like that, Jolyne?
I'm part of a pirate crew that raids Mejare's military. You would, too, if you lived there... do you have a similar story, Jolyne?
You smell like alcohol. I thought it was Jura at first, but no, it's you.
Do you drink a lot? You smell like it.
You smell like alcohol...you really shouldn't drink. It's bad for you.
...A goddess? Nayru, you look more sleepy than godly. What's she talking about?
...Are you sure she's a goddess, Navi? Nayru, I'd like you to corroborate this.
Goddess? She helped create your planet? Nayru, what's the meaning of this?
You're not serious? I was told she's an Oracle, but a goddess? Nayru, is this true?
...Pay attention, Rin. Soldiers will always resort to violence if you question their loyalties.
Leave the schoolgirl out of this. The last thing she needs is an authority figure feigning sympathy.
This is a soldier's early effort to indoctrinate you, Rin. She doesn't care about the fringes of society.
...Do you see, Rin? Soldiers have no regard for the humanity of a criminal, and they won't for a disabled girl, either.
...So even here, there's boundaries. I guess I pictured both genders climbing in a bath together without a second thought.
...So you wouldn't share a hot spring, for instance. I guess there's some instinct for separation.
...It is embarrassing, but that's why I want to face it. You have to take your fears head-on.
I wish I could say it didn't embarrass me. But getting scared off by that would be even worse.

I guess you haven't perfected the technology yet. Mejare only exists because of how easy Paksis crystal makes terraforming.
...Did "Coerthas" have some kind of disaster?
So it's still that experimental in this time... even our pirate crew could scrounge up the resources to terraform a small area. What happened in "Coerthas"?
...How should I know? No one has this aura about them by accident.
If that's true, then keep it that way. I'd love for my instincts to be wrong for once.
Mejare may have settlers from Brigid, too. What do you celebrate?
I think Mejare's first colonists came from all over Earth. Maybe there's something we've borrowed from Brigid.
You don't need to strip to be mature. I've spent time in places like this. We used to heckle the shy ones.
We're even called Magno's Family. It's not about others---I just want to prove myself.
A crew is a lot like family. I'm not trying to upstage them, I just---want to prove I exist.
That's just what parents do. I was always causing mine trouble, getting in fights or yelling at them. But they still loved me.
...That's part of being a parent. They love you through all your mistakes, or your arguments, or even getting hurt. You can't have been worse than I was.
Maybe I could return the favor in a flight sim.
If nothing else, I bet I'm a better swimmer than you are a pilot.
...I hope your reason's not the holiday.
...If that's somehow more romantic...
...I don't understand. It---changed somehow?
...It---was a Fennekin, but now it isn't?
...That's my point.
Exactly. It's...too safe.
Is that what the war is about? Energy shortages?
...Was fuel the cause of the fighting?
..."Condition"?

What's the "condition"?
...If you don't mind.
...No interest?
...Do you prefer it that way?
...But no less.
...So we're even, then.
So you've been keeping well? Our crew is still in deep space---I think they've been tempted by a few tropical planets recently.
We have encountered some sunny planets recently, which are tough to ignore after so long in space. I hope you enjoyed your semester.
Do you know what it takes to make a pilot nauseous? You can play dumb if you want, but I'm not fooled.
Don't patronize me. There's a reason you've got this aura about you, whatever it is.
...What's a combo? ...What's a bug?
...And this revolutionized things, somehow?
These things run on computers, right? If there was a bug, why didn't they fix it?
An observation, not an insult. It's just unusual for me...clothes aren't readily available for a pirate.
...I wasn't insulting you. The clothes I have are stolen, so this is unusual for me.
You have to understand...none of us owns very much, being pirates. We all wear the same thing every day.
Varying your outfits is not a privilege pirates have. It just stuck out to me, that's all.
...Thank you. I guess that's true for me, as well---I'd never have left the Mejarian system if I hadn't joined our pirate crew.
...We've just met, but thank you. You're right---being forced out into space has let me see more of it than I'd ever dreamed.
I think my parents would've liked me to join a prestigious academy like that. It sounds like it would take discipline I didn't find until later.
I'm sure it was hard work. My parents had their eyes on some imperial academies for me, but they were worried I was too temperamental.
Our Paksis is kind. In fact, it's afraid of Earth's. Maybe it's afraid of a lot of things that happen here.
There might be more than one evil energy lurking on this planet. Our own Paksis is---caring.
I'm a pirate. It pays for outlaws to look out for each other.
It's hard to survive outside the law on your own. That's why I'm part of a pirate group.
Can't it? You seem to be doing a good job.
I'm telling you, I don't know what "Super Mario" is. Slow down.
I've made it twenty years without knowing about it, so I think it's not all that important.
...Why are you doing this to me? I was just being polite...
What's wrong? It's just a belt. Are you alright?
If you're so shy, maybe you shouldn't be playing this...I don't want to see a girl all broken up.
...Don't ask me how you're going to get all the way down to nude.
I'll just hope you manage to win. Stripping looks physically painful for you.
...Florina?
...Is she disqualified, then?
Well, that didn't last long.
Well, that's one down.
Looks like men have a use after all...thinning the herd.
The point of my suit is functionality. It doesn't encumber me.
Are you saying you wear that for fun?
My suit is standard-issue. I don't get to complain about comfort.
What exactly is Jerusalem? A man's name?
I understand spiders' importance. I still don't like them.
I've lived in apartments infested with spiders. You'll have to forgive my distaste for them.
I don't like my armor so much as I need it.
Tomatoes? That would fly over a Tarakkian's head. They only eat synthetic pellets.
If not for my responsibilities, actually, I'd probably wear a sundress.
...You were designed? You're a robot? I would expect a gynoid to adapt to piloting quickly, yes.
...Wait. You're robotic? I thought you were merely being professional---no wonder you'd adapt.
You're---a gynoid? You had me completely fooled---Earth has masterful robotics. I'd like to see how one handles a Dread...
..."Designed"? You're not seriously a machine? Unbelievable...a robot piloting a Dread would be capable of fantastic maneuvers.
"Designed"? You're...some sort of gynoid? Even still, you look and sound human enough to make your own decisions.
...You mean to tell me you're a robot? Just when I was happy to meet another girl who took herself seriously...
"Designed"? "T-Dolls"? So you're not a human girl---and Earth's robotics are far more advanced than I realized.
...What are you saying? You're a robotic woman? You're speaking like you have no free will!
Of the many complaints my pilots present me with, their laser rings failing has never been one of them. What primitives have you been fighting?
Fragility? Laser rings don't jam. Whatever energy-primitives you've been fighting pale next to planet Mejare.
...You realize I say kinetic weapons are for men is because they're all planet Tarak has the resources for? I think you've been fighting limited-technology peoples.
...Mejare is winning its war with Tarak, the planet of men, because Tarak doesn't have the supplies to get its energy weapons right. I think that applies to your enemies.
I know for a fact Earth has access to energy weapons that eclipse even Mejare's. What backwards planet do you live on where they haven't been perfected?
I have a crewmate who collects kinetic guns as antiques, but it doesn't define her. I hope you don't mean that literally.
...I'm not sure how serious you're being. Commitment to a profession is one thing, but to weapons themselves?
...Your weapons define who you are? Even as a pilot, I wouldn't define myself by my Dread---what makes you say that?
...You say you're defined by your weapons like it's a point of pride. You shouldn't limit yourself like that---but I'm curious why you do.
...Silence, destructive power, and to not degrade oneself with a man's weapon.
You sound like my crewmate Barnette, endlessly praising kinetic weapons. They're for men, and not nearly as refined---or destructive.
Just like Barnette---girls who grow attached to mechanical firearms will never hear a word against them. No kinetic weapon ever destroyed a planet.
"Simple, cheap, and reliable" are words I'd use to describe my bodysuit. Energy weapons can tear through entire vessels.
Maybe you might have a point if you're tied down in ground combat for days. I deal in space battles, and no kinetic weapon can vaporize a mech.
...I never asked for the advice I needed, either. No one ever does.
...Girls will never get the advice they need unless it's forced upon them.
...The advice that got me off the streets was told to me. Harsh realities always are.
...If you only listen to advice you ask for, you'll never be anything but a dropout.
...Thanks. But it's common on Mejare.
Blue hair is run-of-the-mill on Mejare. There's prettier faces underneath than mine.
...Matches my eyes? If you say so...girls usually call my eyes cold.
...Thank you. Yours is nice, too.
It covers everything, but it hides nothing.
Don't be ashamed. It's a perfectly sensible choice.
Bodysuits are comfortable and efficient, but they leave nothing to the imagination.
Your whole figure is on display, Marinette. Of course, on Mejare, no one minds.
Rude? You're awfully defensive after some honest comments.
...At least you love your home planet. Quiz me on Mejare. I won't pull any punches.
...So is a "country" some kind of special planet I should know about?
If you keep insisting on addressing her in public, then it is my business. Half my job is defusing relationship issues among my pilots.
My subordinates get into petty dating issues all the time...this tiff with ~player~ sounds a lot like that.
You've made it all of our business. My pilots often have relationship issues...honesty is the best solution.
My pilots tend to date each other...I know what's going on here. I suggest you confront ~player~ about your feelings here and now.
If you keep insisting on addressing him in public, then it is my business. Half my job is defusing relationship issues among my pilots.
My subordinates get into petty dating issues all the time...this tiff with ~player~ sounds a lot like that.
You've made it all of our business. My pilots often have relationship issues...honesty is the best solution.
My pilots tend to date each other...I know what's going on here. I suggest you confront ~player~ about your feelings here and now.
...Those guns are for men. Mechanical ones. On my planet, we use laser rings instead.
What I meant, Revy, was that men use those kinetic guns. Women should use laser rings, like on planet Mejare.
I was arguing for my planet's laser rings, Revy, not avoiding firearms altogether. Men are obsessed with noisy mechanical guns.
What? Of course women should be armed---but with my planet's laser rings, not the loud kinetic guns that men use.
...You actually have a job? And you're a pirate, at that...how many of you are there?
Huh. An Earth woman, but a pirate... How many members does Lagoon Company have?
...You're a pirate, then? That's...a pleasant surprise. How big is this Lagoon Company?
...That's not the answer I was expecting, but I'm glad to hear it. If you're part of a pirate band...well, how large is it?
Leadership is a mentality. Try learning how negotiate...that way you could make a trade deal with Mejare and lose that heavy holster.
If you expect leadership from yourself, you'll start doing it. Negotiation is a good first step...
Even you're starting to feel the weight of that holster. Negotiation is a good leadership skill...try defusing company arguments.

state.text: Even with no one to lead, you can build up your skills. Try negotiating yourself out of your next fight...just to save on bullets.

case.state: ...You didn't notice? Well, that proves my point, doesn't it? Look closer at my hand.
I'm surprised you'd admit that. We know who would've won a shootout, then---here, look more closely.

state.text: If you don't see my ring, then you now see my point. My hand is my holster---no need to swing that weight around.

case.state: Not exactly the sharp eyes of a markswoman. But that's the point---they're inconspicuous.
You...forgot. It sounds as if you don't interact with normal humans very often.
...So you aren't used to appearing as a human before others. How often do you meet normal humans?
...Are you saying you're forgetful, or you spend most of your time away from normal people? Otherwise it'd be habit to transform.
...I see. Is this game your attempt to socialize with normal humans? You wouldn't forget to transform if you were used to this.
...You're a "goddess"? You must be, if you're so removed from humanity that you'd think a transforming insect is less alarming.
...I can believe you're a "goddess" if you can transform into an insect. Why you thought that'd be easier to accept is beyond me.
...A "goddess" with a perfectly human form. We'd be none the wiser had you simply started like this.
...A butterfly goddess, disguised as a human girl, who thought her transformation would not be alarming. Earth is more than I bargained for.
..."Mom"? Like a Fama, I assume...I lead a pilot team of girls your age. I just want to make sure you're alright.
...I'm not sure what "mom" means, but if you're so sure of yourself, I'll leave you alone. I have my own pilots to worry about.
"Mom"...that sounds a lot like "Fama." In any case, I'm just used to being responsible for girls your age.
..."Mom"? I was just showing concern, Tomoko. I was in your position once, and I mentor other girls who've been, as well.
Why would I make you feel great when I'm concerned for your safety? If you have a home, you should be there.
Praising you was not my intention, Tomoko. I'm saying you should reconsider the choices that led you here.
I would "make a girl feel great" if she were using her missiles efficiently. You need to head someplace safe.
I want you to re-evaluate yourself, Tomoko. Why aren't you getting proper rest? Self-care is important.
...I had a chip on my shoulder at your age, too. Hanging out in seedy bars, trying to make a name for myself.
Trying to start fights just from simple advice...you really do remind me of myself from a few years ago.
...I used to assume the worst of everyone who reached out to me, as well. You should kick that habit sooner than I did.
...I wouldn't show concern to a girl with larger breasts? You're just picking fights...a lot like I used to do.
...I guess an Earth super soldier would be quite defensive about her weapons' secrets. Your friend is behind you...
Combat...I took to piloting out of necessity, but I ended up enjoying it very much. I only had my crewmates to train me...
I'm a fighter pilot...that's not too far off from combat. I received that training informally, though, from crewmates.
A school just for combat...you don't seem like military. I received all my pilot training from my shipmates.
A combat academy...I'm a pilot. I wonder if I'd be better had I gone to a school instead of just receiving training from shipmates...
...So, you lead some kind of religious faction on "Gamindustri." It's unusual for planets to not have a unified society...do the other nations have their own "goddesses"?
...I see. Mejare's society is unified, like most planets...are the nations of "Gamindustri" divided over religion? Are you the only goddess?
That's true, but every extra inch of your body requires your heart to work that much harder.
Maybe I misspoke. If there's less of your legs to travel along, then your heart can use that power elsewhere.
It's not so much that your legs are amputated as that they're shorter. Taller pilots's hearts have to work harder to circulate blood.
I agree. The way you talk about it makes it sound like it was an accident rather than something you were born with. Is that right?
I'm glad you see it the same way. I'm sorry if this is too personal, but your situation wasn't congenital, was it?
Were you born with normal legs, then? You agree that it shouldn't have deterred you.
I understand that that's not the kind of decision you can make as soon as it's offered. Still, it's surprising restraint on the part of Earth's military to have never offered it before.
Has the prospect really never come up for you, even in school? I would have figured Earth's military might send recruiters out for that sort of thing.
I'd hoped you'd at least considered it before, maybe as part of Earth's forces. I can show you the ropes if you're interested.
"Protect the land from destruction"? What's happening to it? Maybe the ecological devastation I've heard about on Earth is already underway.
Your land is being destroyed? Colonies have suffered terraforming accidents, but this is Earth. Then again, I've heard about this planet suffering damage to its surface...
Some girls look down upon exercising as ruining the female form rather than enhancing it. That attitude might be unique to my homeworld.
A fit body isn't always seen as the feminine ideal, at least on Mejare. I don't agree, and maybe Earth doesn't, either.
That's a mature attitude for a schoolgirl. I didn't start to learn that until I took a leadership position, and even then, I was worried about not being liked.
I wish I'd learned that earlier myself. I grew up constantly worrying what others thought of me, and it continued even into my squadron leadership.
...Yes, you should probably temper your energy in the halls. That reminds me of an apprentice pilot of mine---she's always full of energy herself, crashing into the man she likes.
One of our trainees is a young girl who's always running around herself. In fact, she tends to tumble onto the "Mr. Alien" she has so much affection for.
"Arceus"...is that related to the Arcana? Our captain used to be a priestess, and she still has a set of tarot cards.
"Arceus"...? I've never heard of that...is it your term for the Arcana, as in tarot cards? Our captain was once a priestess---maybe we still have ties to Earth's religion.

state.text: I'm surprised you recognized it---Earth must have laser weapons, too. In that case, I'm sure you can recognize my position.
There's a difference between a personal sidearm and a civilian waving around a murder weapon. The fact you even know it's a weapon means I can be clear about defending myself.
...I see you're familiar with laser weapons. My first duty is ensuring the safety of myself and my team, including such threats as unhinged civilians. This is your warning.
Tch! "Work." I won't hesitate to subdue you if you start to act on your threats.
...Your "work"? If this place's security isn't willing to remove dangerous thugs, I'll do it myself. I suggest you stay put and be quiet.
I have a "problem" with your weapon and your attitude, not your mask. You're wasting your time by playing dumb.
The mask isn't the issue, and you know it. I'm not going to keep humoring you if you keep threatening us.

case.state: ...Is that why you're eating them? Of all things, French fries...does your world really have no seasoned food?
...French fries. What an odd food to get addicted to...most girls would prefer sweets. I imagine you don't have those in your world, either?
That explains why you're shamelessly eating them. Still, are they really the height of human cuisine to you? What did you eat in your world?
So your stoicism is not just a personal choice, but part of your culture. I used to perceive men the same way, like all Mejarians.
Muspell...so emotion is frowned upon by your people as a whole. My homeworld sees men as beasts whose only feelings are rooted in fighting.
...I'm sorry. Did something happen to your sister? I was an only child...
Your sister...? I never had any sisters---I'm sorry if I brought up something uncomfortable.
...A robot built from stone? Or with merely a stone casing...for a robot, you have very human mannerisms.
...Why would a robot be built with a marble exterior? In any case, I'd prefer that over the golem I suspected---and you seem quite human to me.
...I actually believe you. If this "mana" energy is related to our Paksis core, it would explain why piloting my Vandread with our male pilot tires us out.
...As much as that sounds like an excuse, I've encountered something like that. Controlling my combined Vandread mech with our male pilot leaves us both exhausted.
...It exhausts you? Earth's Paksis core was responsible for the powers we saw---as well as ours, letting our male and female ships combine! And when we pilot them, we start to feel drained...
...I call them prisoners, but they've become valued crewmates. I imagine the men on Gamindustri have shown their worth, as well.
...They've become our allies out of circumstance. I never thought I'd value a man's help...were you the same way once?
Horror...I don't need to seek that out in books. The way you write about men and women being together here...what's that like?
...I never read much in the first place. Maybe it's better to ask if there are stories specifically about men and women.
"Devil Fruit"? That sounds like a nickname for a drug. How many other people have "eaten" it?
...Tell me more about Devil Fruit, then. Where did you get it, and how common is it for people to have tried it?
...Servants? You're not the first Earthling we've met to demand servitude. You can look elsewhere.
...I have no intention of being your servant. Our crew's mission is to prevent Earthlings from subjugating us.
So, this has been going on long enough that civilians take it for granted. If it was discovered right before space travel developed, it may be your name for our energy source.
Do you know when it was introduced? If it was around the frontier era, then we may be thinking of the same thing.
The Paksis is our crystal energy core that powers starships. I know Earth has access to it, but your term might be different.
...The "Paksis Pragma." The energy core that allows for space travel. Is "Puyo" Earth's name for that?
...I am from a different world. Humans developed space travel centuries ago, Nami.
...What are you saying? Earth has settled dozens of extraplanetary colonies through space travel. Has that been kept hidden here?
...Of course there's "space sailing." That's how Mejare and other Earth colonies were settled---don't you have that?
...You're unaware of space travel? No wonder Earthlings are xenophobic---centuries-old technology is being hidden from you.
That's what you do, right? Research them in the field?
So you're a field researcher? You look like you have specialized equipment.
I'm not even sure what it means. Why is it so offensive?
I just overheard it. Were they making fun of you?
That wasn't an insult. But I understand if you'd rather be left alone.
I'm not trying to start a fight. If you don't want to socialize, then just say so.
...I meant that I've spent most of my life seeing men as the enemy. Mejare's population is all female.
There aren't any men on my homeworld. It wasn't until recently that we even saw them as human.
I don't try them very much myself. I heard she recently built a machine that would calculate crew members' romantic compatibility.
Typically they're not computer games---more designing custom Dread parts. But her "romance calculator" got a lot of crew attention.
Why did you need to become pirates to live out your dreams? Most of us turned to piracy after our world government failed to address an energy crisis.
So, your planet's government didn't provide for your crew when they needed it, either, I take it. We formed after Mejare's energy disasters left girls homeless.
We've found several populated planets in our current nebula, so your homeworld might be among them. Where is it?
We can't go off course just for a vacation, but it might be on our path to Mejare. What sector is it in?
...Well, they still don't tend to me much. I'd rather sit in the jacuzzi than have their hands all over me.
...Usually I tell them I can take care of myself. The jacuzzi is much easier.
I usually stay behind when we encounter a new planet. I have to command the Dread team in case of an attack.
I'm not frequently on away teams myself. It'd be a waste to have the wing commander stuck on a planet's surface if anything happened.
I understand. I figured the technology of this era might be more primitive. This isn't the Earth I know from my time.
That's fine. Your airships might be early steps in developing frontier-era space travel. Not much is known about Earth's history in my time.
Oh, I---don't know enough about her work to describe it. It couldn't have been that groundbreaking if she just gave it to me.
Oh, it's...just some green fluid. I don't really know any chemistry...it was probably just some souvenir from her lab.
Dreads are our ship's fighter crafts. I lead our team of pilots to defend it from enemies.
A Dread is my homeworld's standard combat craft, individually piloted. Our ship deploys an assault team of them that I command.
It's not surprising that Earth might have more advanced programs. What's the purpose of these simulations? Combat training?
I heard the men of planet Tarak sometimes use "combat" computer games for training soldiers. Is that what your simulations are for, too?
I see. Our Dread fighters were reconfigured after they were exposed to the light of our ship's crystal core. I know one exists on Earth, as well---a royal child might have had access to it.
Are you sure nothing happened when you were a baby? It's possible that Earth royalty might be brought before Paksis crystal---it's the same light that changed our Dreads.
I ask because I know Earth has a crystal energy core just like our ship's, and its light has transformed our fighter crafts. If any Earthling knows about it, it'd be a princess.
...Is he accomplishing all this by himself? How are you battling these robots?
...And you've been battling him? I didn't take you for a soldier. I assume he's got forces of his own to build these robots.
The typical response of a girl with something to hide.
Your sudden panic is very convincing.
...The least you could do is make an effort to convince me of that.
...Right. That's obvious from the worry on your face.
I'm sure we have a lot of different words for the same things. But if Earth's conditions are as harsh as I've heard, they might be more ferocious.
Knowing what I do about Mejare, it must have hundreds of alternate names for things. But these "Pokémon" sound so fierce, maybe they were never brought over.
...Just "male anatomy"? What do they usually look up? I'm curious how that rod manages to transform the way it does.
...That's awfully vague. What is it that's not obvious even to Earth girls? If I were reading, I'd look up how that erection process can be so dramatic.
It even interacts with us? We might be thinking of the same thing, then. Do you use aether as some kind of power source?
...So, it can affect us, too. This is sounding even more like what I thought. If you use it to power energy cores, that would all but confirm it.
This wouldn't be the first time Paksis has shown me visions, whether it's our Paksis or Earth's. I don't suppose you have an explanation?
I can accept shared supernatural visions if you can explain what's causing them. Especially if it matches what I think the explanation is.
Maybe this is only a short time before space exploration began. That's an easy solution to overpopulation, especially with a terraforming process.
I've never heard anything about Earth being overpopulated. But if terraforming was developed to combat it, maybe it eventually led to space travel.
...What exactly does that mean? It might be another foundation for what Mejare uses today---even the men praise our medicine.
My homeworld has impressed others with how we treat injuries. If you could explain a bit more, maybe this is another case of its beginnings on Earth.
I see. Maybe Earthlings have just developed other skin colors. Has this planet been facing any environmental damage?
...Knowing what happens to Earth's environment in my time, maybe new skin colors are just another adaptation. Have you seen any damage like that?
...That's hard to believe. But I don't know much about animals in the first place---civilians aren't allowed to see them on Mejare.
...My homeworld keeps animals in strict captivity. I wouldn't have thought they're so gentle.
I always have to take her word for it when she's servicing my Dread. Still, if a male doctor could get through to her, an animal scientist might, too.
If they're fellow scientists, they might be able to bond over it. That's how Duero piqued her interest, as a doctor.
I can still understand you. It's lucky we can talk to our male prisoners, since they use different writing.
Our engineer tried building an "inter-prico" machine just to read men's writing. Luckily, we could still talk to them, and to you.
I don't think it's just "estrogen." It's the core's crystals themselves, and it's formed some kind of hot spring. There's been rumors about breast growth and pain relief.
...I don't know much about chemicals, but it's the actual crystal core. Girls have taken a bath in it and apparently had their breasts grow.
...What's drinking got to with it? I was talking about the crystals. They're responsible for fusing the male and female ships in the first place.
Alcohol? Our crystal core's made plenty of bizarre changes to the ship without any "solvent." They grew on their own when our ships merged.
It could be there's more variation on Earth than in the people sent out on frontier missions. The history of that era isn't clear.
All foreign colonists are descended from the first groups of settlers. Maybe they didn't include anyone from your race.
...That sounds familiar. Mejare's elders would all insist our women are the last descendants of Earthlings---and that there's no reason to leave.
...I see. We were always told there was nothing beyond the Mejarian system, and that we were the only human colony.
"Inspired" by? Are you saying you two have---experimented after coming here?
..."Inspiring"---sexuality? With ~player~, you mean?
...My homeworld once called men the "enemy of humans." What do they look like?
I'm still not sure what you mean. My own planet used to describe men as far worse.
...I'd say the same thing, in a cockpit.
...I see. I only have that sort of confidence in a Dread.
It's not a problem, it's just---you look like a lot like my mother. And she did the same kind of work.
...My mother was a scientist. Dressed like you, with glasses and the same haircut.
What I meant was...you look just like my mother. She was a scientist, too. For terraforming.
...That's the same kind of thing my mother studied. You---look a lot like her.
There's no risk of war? Especially if you're talented...I guess I didn't have much of a choice when it came to piloting. There's no peace for pirates, or Mejare.
...Mejare is always at war, and our crew is always fighting. So the second I showed promise in a Dread, I tried to learn everything.
...Does that mean you spend all your time with men?

I'm---just as confused. The "best part" is something called..."birth control"?
...Nothing about the term "birth control" sounds like the best part of sex. What is it?
I---you're confused, too, Rin? So this isn't just an Earth term---what's "birth control"?
...Birth...control? Do Earth girls make birth some kind of erotic experience? ...Rin, what is she talking about?
...I remember that. We fell for such a simple trap...all three of us got along much better after that.
...I wasn't unscathed that day myself. I was searching for you two with bandages still around my eye.
...It wasn't just you two. I think I warmed up to you a little myself after that...it was too close of a call for all of us.
...The entire assault team could've been killed that day. We had twenty-five injured pilots...but everyone made it out alive. I couldn't believe it when I found you two.
That's right...the entire Dread team seemed to get along better after that. But I still wasn't prepared to walk in on you two in the briefing room a few days later.
...It's true. I couldn't stand either of you back then...and no one could stand Barnette, right from the moment she came aboard the hideout with her gun collection.

condition.saying: Meia doesn't seem to get much attention

case.state: I'm not interested in their attention, Jura. Leave me out of this.
...Jura, don't drag me into personal romance. The men's attention is not my concern.
...Mhmhm. I guess she does make the perfect advertisement for the gym.
...Ahaha. I guess she's more convincing than I'd ever be, huh?
...So this is the kind of language they use. As if we're the aggressors, just for existing.
It's hard to hear ourselves being described this way. But it's just like how we dehumanized Tarak.
...Do you have a Jura in your life, Jean?
...Hopefully you've found an arrangement that works for you, Jean.
I---tch. What an obnoxious girl.
I'm not---tch. Fine.
If only you could ignore me more often...
Ignore---never mind. You're baiting me...
Tight clothing is common on our planet, but revealing clothing is more so. Technically, this is a flightsuit.
This is a flightsuit, Miss Jessie. We're from another planet, not "space." Mejarians wear many things.
Is that your perception of women from other planets? We all wear "spacesuits"? This is for piloting my Dread.
Don't women wear many different outfits on Earth, Miss Jessie? Mejarians are the same. This is a piloting suit, not a spacesuit.
Tight clothing is common on our planet, but revealing clothing is more so. Technically, I was wearing a flightsuit.
My suit is for flying, Jessie, and we're from another planet, not "space." Mejarians wear many things.
Is that your perception of women from other planets? We all wear "spacesuits"? I wear that suit to pilot my Dread.
Don't women wear many different outfits on Earth, Jessie? Mejarians are the same. I was wearing a piloting suit, not a spacesuit.
You have to be your own person eventually. I didn't get much choice when, but I was already starting to strike out from under mine.
I did everything I could to be independent. It's important to take that step...but you should still appreciate them.
...I guess if you know a lot of men, you get to pick and choose.
...You have the luxury of choice, I suppose.
...It must be nice.
...Even the stylists gave up on mine.
Done what? Should I not have said that? I don't---oh.
What do you mean, Mahiru? Is she---o-oh no, you don't have to. It's fine.
...Does Chiaki really like video games that much? Does---oh. Oh dear.
Now I've done it? What do you me---oh. Oh. Uh...please don't.
Jura just carries that for fashion's sake. Not that it's particularly useful next to a laser ring, anyway...
We use violence when necessary. Mejare's government are the real aggressors...
Mejare's military is full of the violent types you're looking for. We fight to survive.
Swords are too heavy. They'd just weigh me down in combat...like I keep telling Jura to remember.
A pilot has little use for a sword. Even our ground raids usually end far too quickly to get in close.
...You're certainly trusting. I guess you can tell how Jura's not actually very skilled with that thing.
No. A pilot should focus on just that, not playing with knives.
My job is to pilot a Dread. Any time I could spend with a sword would be better used for that.
No. I don't share her fascination with swords---a pilot's job is to destroy targets quickly and from a distance.
No. A sword is a limited ground weapon, and we try to avoid ground engagements in the first place. We're pilots.
...Jura is always trying to set me up with girls. She doesn't understand I lack the time for that.
I don't have the desire nor the time for a relationship. You can save the niceties.
Maybe if you did any work, you'd understand why I don't have the schedule for a relationship...
...She thinks because she has time for a girlfriend, we all do. I'm not interested.
...If a few conversations in the communal spa makes us friends, then sure. We're friends.
Is that all it takes for a girl to be your friend? Some time in the spa together? ...Fine, then. Friends.
Jura's definition of friend is certainly looser than mine if a spa visit is all it takes. But...I can live with that.
We've been through a lot more together than a few spa trips. But if that satisfies you...then we're friends.
Laid? What kind of...is this the vulgar language Earth girls use?
I'd be a lot less sour if you stopped pestering me...and cleaned up your vulgar slang.
It's a leader's job to be sour. Subordinates and soldiers seem content with...sex-talk.
Wha---what are you talking about? I would never be with a girl who---who phrases romance as getting laid.
...Of course I haven't. Don't you know where we're from? Jura's been making it abundantly clear.
I'd be far more ashamed if I had been with a man. Pirates or not, we're still Mejarians.
As if I would even want to be. Mejare is the planet of women...and we still adhere to that.

state.text: It seems you've spent more time honing your gauntlets than your listening skills. No Mejarian has been with a man.

case.state: ...The last thing I need is a drink.
...I do not drink. You understand that?
...Keep offering drinks, and you'll really see me mad.
...I can't drink...I have responsibilities. Unlike you.
Don't worry---I've learned not to be too trusting. Actions are more important than whatever she says.
Misato isn't the first military woman who's tried to make herself sympathetic. We'll see what story her actions tell.
How gullible do you take me for? We'll see how Misato conducts herself and decide from there.
I always start from place of distrust for soldiers. If Misato's corrupt, she'll make it obvious soon enough.
Don't even think about sharing drinks with her, Jura. You do enough of that back on the ship.
Don't you dare touch her beer, Jura. I know how you get...and Barnette's not around.
You can strip all you want, Jura, but you're staying sober tonight, you hear me? Don't join in with this woman.
We've got a long flight home, Jura...so don't touch Misato's beer. You don't handle it as well as you think.
...Some sort of former celebrity, then? Don't feel bad, Nayru...so am I.
...You don't need to deny your past, Nayru. If you're avoiding some former fame...I am, too.
...Does Navi know you from media appearances? If there's a past you're running from...I used to be the poster girl for my Oma's company.
...Seems there's some confusion for all of us. If you're some kind of celebrity in hiding, Nayru...you're not alone.
I don't think she was teasing at all. A soldier's first instinct is to crush any dissent.
That didn't sound like a tease, Misato. This medic business is just her attempt to seem polite.
If Sei really were just a teasing medic, I would hope it'd take more than one insult to set her off.
Misato might buy your saving throw to make that look like a joke, but I don't. You didn't do anything because we're in public.
I don't trust you either, Misato. Especially with how quickly you side with your fellow military personnel.
It figures the other soldier would immediately side with her. You're both despicable.
I don't know what I expected, running my mouth. Even the unarmored soldier is quick to circle the wagons.
Don't offer her alcohol! She's still a child!
I---you couldn't be a worse influence if you tried. Never drink alcohol, Rin.
Don't take it, Rin. Drinking is a disgusting habit.
...Rin, stay in school and don't accept drinks from strange women.
For your own sake, stay in your corner. And you should be ashamed of yourself for giving drinks to schoolgirls.
Are you sure you can handle all those drinks?
I don't know where you're putting all that alcohol. You're tiny.
Sei reminds me of when you got Dita drunk, Jura. Of course, I'd rather forget that evening.
I can't believe you have room for all that alcohol...I'd rather finish them if it meant Rin didn't have to.
Can you really drink all that? ...If it's between Rin and me to finish those drinks for you, give them to me. She doesn't need that in her life.
Where is all that alcohol being stored? ...Give them to me if anyone. Not Rin...
...You're so short, but you can drink more than I ever could...if you need help, let me do it, not Rin.
...It's strange. We can trust our lives to each other, but it's still uncomfortable trusting our bodies.
We must be born that way. Our doctor's saved my life, but I blushed when he saw me walking towards the hot spring.
Maybe it's my homeworld talking, but you get used to stripping around other girls pretty quickly.
Have you never been nude around other girls? Mejare's not shy about that, and our crew even less so.
You're the specialist, then, and I'm the all-around...
I might win by average performance...
I'm sorry. I heard something similar actually befalls this planet in my time---a wasteland surface, at least.
From what we've heard in my time, Earth has a similar fate. Not winter, but some kind of acidic surface where nothing can live.
I've made myself clear. I don't need your assurances.
I'll see for myself. Just get on with it.
That's what bothers me---I can't. But I can feel it.
...It doesn't make sense to me, either. But the feeling is unmistakable.
...Sure. Girls already look to me to stay calm.
...I guess that's my job, for girls to rely on me.
I was on my own for a long time already. What I worry about now is that I'll die, and it'll be like I never lived at all.
I already got pushed out of "the nest." Now, it's more like...I want to pass something on to the future.
Have you ever tried anything like it?
Don't tell me you've tried one. I might win by average performance...
...I guess---even a machine can transform.
That sounds dramatic, but...machines can do it. Maybe everything can.
...Is that why you hide your face?
...Your mask, right? To avoid attention...
...Am I prying?
Would you...rather not share?
...What do you consider yourself to be?
...What category do you fall into?
...If this is serious, you should be up-front with us.
...Whatever you're getting at, it sounds like we might need to know.
Thanks, but I doubt it. We might get some time off on the ship at best.
You're talking like I get paid. Our captain tells me to relax sometimes, but I don't think she'd waste that much time.
...It took me some time to learn that. Don't wait until they're already gone to say so.
You might not realize that until you're already separated. And you wish you could thank them in person.
Are you drinking? ...I didn't even know this place served alcohol.
Are you drinking? Jura drinks too much. Sometimes she's hungover at the next morning's meeting.
Are you drinking? ...Well, keep it to yourself.
I don't drink, Sei...not anymore.
Are you drinking? The state-approved Mejarian libations are all full of hormones...
Half-naked and liquored-up seems like a bad combination...
Drinking...just like a soldier.
Birth...control? What's that?
...What did you just say? "Birth control"? What does that mean?
Birth control? You control birth on Earth? That sounds---barbaric.
...What's "birth control"?
Earth? Oh, I see...this must be Earth from a time before the frontier era. Whatever divisions you have as nations, I think they exist as different planets now.
What? Oh...this is a pre-colonial Earth, when it still had nations. I guess humans are still hardly united in my time---it's just on the scale of planets.
I thought it'd have something to do with our energy core. I know Earth has one, as well, and what they're both capable of. Visions of the past, or shared dreams.
Both our ship and this planet have access to a "Paksis core" that feeds off of emotions. It's shown us supernatural visions before. Ghosts aren't far off.
Maybe a normal citizen just isn't aware of the Earth's Paksis. It's a core fueled by emotional energy signatures---sometimes that means it shows memories.
...Maybe I'm still not cut out for that sort of thing.
...Leading my squadron sounds a lot easier now.
It's more important that someone's there to stand up to it.
If you're fighting to change things, that's what matters more.
...You don't have to believe me. We're not looking for any more trouble from Earth.
...It's your choice. Our crew has enough enemies already.
People say that, but a meal and a bath are usually enough for me.
Sitting in the jacuzzi isn't "fun," but that's the kind of thing I relax with.
...This is the last time I try to make small talk about an Earth girl's interests.
And Jura wonders why I don't bother talking to people...
...At least you're passionate about it.
What's "1983"? I have no context for Earth years, Chiaki.
...Would you like it if I started rattling off my Dread's specifications?
Ah, yes. The enn-ee-ess. That explains everything. Thanks, Chiaki.
Men are nothing to be afraid of, Florina. Most are simpletons, anyway.
Listen. I've helped stage raids on Tarak's military. Men are easily dealt with.
You don't have to be afraid of men, Florina. They probably relish that.
You've got to assert yourself around men. They'll try to lord themselves over you otherwise.
Jura...? She's the closest thing to a friend I have, yes. But we're colleagues. What's this about?
...Why is an image of Jura worrying you, Nayru? ...Not that she's my friend, necessarily.
...Jura is my colleague, but it depends how you define friend. More importantly, what are you so agitated about?
...What did Jura scheme this time that's got you so worried? She's more teammate than friend, but...
Friend? ...You mean Jura? What did she hide from me this time?
Friend? ...You must mean Jura, though that's stretching the definition. None of her schemes are ever good for me.
...I assume you mean Jura. It was bad enough dragging me here, and now she's planning something else?
...Jura, you mean? I guess I spend the most time with her...but she's always scheming something.
...Why are you being evasive? I pirate for a living---of course there's going to be conflict. It's why I asked.
Are you surprised to be seeing fighting? That's what I do...it's why I wanted to know my future.
My future is always uncertain, Nayru...that's the nature of being a fighter pilot. And the reason I even asked.
Why do you think I asked about my future? I could die any given day...that's the risk of being a fighter pilot, and a pirate especially.
...I understand you may not like fighting, Nayru, but that's what a pirate does. It's why I wish to know the future at all...
...You said this was "Din's Power"? It's certainly intense...it sounds like a ritual.
Nothing more appropriate, huh...it sounds like something we should chant to.
Hmm...it sounds like a song some primitive tribe would dance to. Fiery.
So, "Din's Power"...energetic, like a bubbling pot. But why is it so appropriate?
...This is somber. And it just came to you? It's like death...
...The "Elegy of Emptiness," you said? It sounds as if it's trying to live up to the name.
Hmm...like a funeral dirge. Or maybe the war bells that preceded it.
Harsh notes...but with little tying them together. It feels like it's dying.
..."Farore's Courage," this was called? It reminds me of piloting...
...Oh, this is nice. It's freeing...like the first time I piloted.
...You seem uncertain about this. But the tune is nice and bubbly...like flying.
So, you know the woman who wrote this? You called it Farore's Courage...it sounds like flying feels.
I'd be hard-pressed to find music that didn't make me feel a certain way...I see why it's named after sailing.
Are you sure? Hmm...it sways like a boat on the ocean. Fitting for the "Song of Storms."
Swaying back and forth...like a stormy sea. I'm sure if you give it time, a feeling will emerge for you, too.
...I didn't think you'd be so quick to dismiss it. To me, it's as its name implies---a gentle storm.
...Four people? And three of them men? I couldn't imagine...the three men with us are surrounded by a hundred women.
...You're the only woman? Small as it is, I couldn't work like that...
Working with three men on a ship full of women is awkward enough for me. I can't imagine being alone with just men...
...And you're OK without women around? Even with all the women around them, the three men we have aboard...are quite the presence.
Who is this Rock you keep mentioning? It sounds as if he irritates you...as men tend to do, in my experience.
...This "Rock"... If you've had to deal with a frustrating foil of a man, then you have my sympathy.
...It sounds as if you could start by defusing your relationship with "Rock," whoever that is.
...If this Rock is a man you find yourself having to work with, despite your differences...well, I have a crewmate like that, too.
...I don't want to fight you, Revy. I don't know why you want to fight me. You could probably make a nice guide to Earth culture.
I'm sorry for not backing down when you bark at me. You sound like you're opinionated...which would help me learn about this planet.
I wasn't interested in fighting the first Earth girl I met, Revy. I think you could teach me a lot about this place.
Maybe Earth girls cower when you shout at them, but I've been shouted at for a long time. Maybe we could get along, and you could teach me about Earth.
And invite a sucker punch? No, thank you. We deal with enough Earth robots as it is.
My squadron already has its hands full with killer Earth machines. Just stay where you are.
My squadron's mission for months now has been to identify hostile Earth machines. I don't need to feel your arm.
I'd rather not put myself in such a vulnerable position against yet another hostile Earth mech. Why not throw a piece of yourself here?
I see. Well, as I said, you look like a normal girl. What need you have for a disguise still eludes me.
...Either way, I don't see why you would need a disguise in the first place. Nothing about this form suggests you're a "goddess."
If the insect is your disguise, then why do you need one? You look like a girl in ornate clothing, not a goddess.
With that transformation, I don't doubt some sort of "goddess-like" power. But this form already disguises you as a normal human girl.
...Again, what women are you interacting with where that would be the case?
...I can only imagine the perspective of the women you work with. Butterfly-catcher hobbyists?
Your prior experience? Girls have responded well to you transforming in front of them in the past?
...I have a hard time believing that. Complete strangers haven't been shocked by you transforming into a butterfly and back?
...You're mocking me. Fine---I won't waste my time asking any more questions.
You...hadn't thought of that. If you're not going to take me seriously, then I won't bother.
"Whoops"? ...You're certainly a goddess in the sense that you think the questions of mortals are beneath you.
...If you're just going to mock me for asking questions, I'll take the hint. I guess I'm not worth a goddess's time.
Demonstrating strange powers without explanation does not put mortals in a charitable mood, Yuelia.
...Is that a threat? I'm already wary of the powers you've shown---as most mortals would be.
...Are you saying I should treat a "goddess" with respect? You should learn now how mortals act when threatened---it isn't "nice."
I'm well within my rights to demand an explanation of your powers. A goddess may not understand, but mortals value their safety.
...Why is that? I'd be wary of being crushed or otherwise attacked.
...I'd much prefer to stay at human size. An insect form may be good for eavesdropping, but you could be stepped on.
...More convenient? Even if you can fly, a butterfly's motion seems more limited. Your body is much frailer...
...Being a butterfly seems far less convenient. You're vulnerable to even a casual smack from a bystander...
...Complete strangers don't mind? Who exactly do you associate with?
I'm sure even I'd get used to you transforming over time, as well. Or do you really mean girls you've never met before?
...Are you referring to your colleagues, or are you really saying most girls you meet aren't alarmed by your transformation?
Most people don't mind, even upon first meeting you? ...I should've figured a "goddess" would be difficult to figure out.
...The Student Council? You use that uniform to battle your own school...what have they done to you?
...What do you mean? Your enemy is the Student Council of your school? Just how authoritarian is it?
If it helps me understand Earth's culture as a whole, then I wouldn't mind an explanation at all...but you don't seem cooperative.
...If the "Internet" is important to Earth's culture, then yes, I'd like that. Surely you can summarize if you're so familiar with it.
There's no need for that. I understand wanting to be armed in a place like this...
That's---not what I wanted. Someone might take advantage of you here---you shouldn't disarm yourself completely.
I...why would you even bring it if you'd so quickly discard all of its ammunition? There's nothing wrong with being armed...
...What are you doing? You're supposed to always treat guns as loaded. I didn't begrudge you for having a weapon.
If you're not in conflict, why do you all exist as separate nations? Planets typically unify to ensure stability.
You're already peacefully coexisting? In that case, it makes sense to unify. My own homeworld would have collapsed if it were split into nations.
G-forces can be intense with a Dread's rapid acceleration, so every small advantage matters. But it's not purely how I'd choose a pilot.
Obviously, height doesn't determine a pilot's success, but our Dread fighters' main tool is their acceleration, which puts a lot of stress on the body. It was worth mentioning.
It occurred to me because a man about your height has recently joined my squadron. It's a marginal benefit, but a Dread's acceleration is difficult to adapt to.
...I'm sorry. Girls under my command have lost limbs in combat. I'm not always sure what to say to them.
...I see. Being a fighter pilot risks injuries like that every day. Not all of my pilots have come out unscathed.
I'm sorry. I've come close to losing a limb myself, and some of my pilots have been less fortunate.
I see. Earth must not yet be unified as a planet in this time. Mejare is one society, as are most Earth colonies.
...So, Earth must still be split into smaller nations in this time. My homeworld has enough issues even as a unified planet.
...If you don't have a global military, then this must be an Earth from pre-colonial times, before it was united. Planets like Mejare are almost always one nation.
Oh. Are you in a relationship with a man? I could gain some insight on how men and women date from a young age.
Are you dating the man you crashed into? I hadn't given much thought to relationships between male and female students, but that makes sense to look into.
...Wait. Are you dating a man? I've considered men from the perspective of having children with them, but obviously romance starts earlier...
I actually had a similar experience myself. I nearly died of brain trauma in a battle a few months ago, and I've tried to be more open with my crewmates since.
I understand. Not long ago, a crash lodged refuse from our energy core into my head. According to our doctor, I was clinically dead for a few minutes---that changed my perspective on things.
That's exactly what taught me to trust my crewmates. Just a few months ago, I was shot down in a battle and nearly went into a coma. I had some time to reflect in that moment.
In that case, a civilian probably has to deal with those attitudes more than I do. For a pilot, there's a certain expectation of fitness.
Since you're a civilian, you probably hear it even more, then. That was the case for me---slimmer, sportier girls are stereotyped into becoming Omas.
I'm sorry to hear that. Since I became a pilot, that attitude's been less prevalent---when I was a civilian like you, the ideal girl was well-endowed.
...Combat training, but not for armed service? What exactly are the duties of a "huntress"?
...Is a "huntress" some sort of paramilitary role, then? Where else would combat training be officially sanctioned?
...If you're not being trained for military service, then what do huntresses do? I'm surprised the armed forces tolerate that activity.

state.text: ...Tch. I didn't come to this planet looking for conflict. And if it came, I expected an organized assault.
...I was so concerned about Harvest operations on this planet, and instead the threat is a lone attacker.
...Out of all the ambushes this planet's elite could have plotted, I encounter a knife-wielding maniac who'd just as easily target an Earth girl.
I've made myself clear. Whatever you've come here to prove, you won't.
I maintain the safety of myself and my pilots. Whatever your goal is, this is your warning.

case.state: ...You call priestesses "Hex Maniacs"? So there isn't much respect for superstition on this world.
...Our captain is over a hundred years old, but that might be the first time someone has called her a "Hex Maniac." I guess priestesses don't hold much clout here.
How ironic. The men we captured from Tarak love our food, as well---they only ate tasteless synthetic pills before.
...So, you came from a world of tasteless food and appreciate Earth's cooking. Our prisoners are the same way with Mejarian cooking--- nothing grows on Tarak, so they only eat nutrition pills.
...That's not as strange as it sounds. The male planet Tarak has no real food at all---just synthetic pills. The man on my Dread team gorges himself on women's cooking.
Even boiled vegetables would be a delicacy on Tarak, the planet our prisoners came from. Before they met us, their entire diet was nutrition pills---I hope they don't get fat.
...Our quartermaster lost her older sister helping refugees evacuate. It's the one thing that seems to bother her.
Gascogne, our quartermaster, served under her late sister in Mejare's military. I think losing her is why she does her best to stay collected.
And Mejare has many war hawks who'd like to see the male planet Tarak wiped out. I've learned it's just propaganda.
The women of Mejare would call themselves a "peaceful race" that's merely defending itself from the aggression of the men of Tarak.
"Is likely"? If you were constructed somewhere, surely there would be design documents, or an engineer responsible.
Isn't there documentation on your design? Such a lifelike robot would surely have engineers taking credit for your creation.
I see. And...after that, what did you come to understand about them?
But...you understand them now. What was it about men that you finally made sense of?
...I'm not sure I've found any, either. But they seem to bring good fortune wherever they go, especially in a battle.
...I didn't say I was interested in them. I'm not sure if I am or not. But every battle they take part in, we suddenly find ourselves cheating the odds.
Romance might drive at the heart of the issue. I already have some experience working alongside men as colleagues.
...I'm not looking for romance, but that might show men and women's relationships most clearly. I already know what men are like professionally.
Are you saying these fruits are just growing out in the open, where anyone can pick them and gain superpowers? Maybe Earth's government has been studying Paksis energy's effects on plant life.
So they are plants. If they're rare, maybe you stumbled across some kind of farm for fruits exposed to Paksis energy---probably research by Earth's government.
I've made myself clear. What happened to your previous servants if you treat them with such respect?
I already serve under a woman who's earned my respect. Why are you shorthanded in the first place?
It's unbelievable that Earth would hide knowledge of its colonies from civilians. Mine is Mejare, settled only by women.
Earth's leaders may not have told you this, but it has colonies throughout the galaxy. Mejare, the planet of women, is my homeworld.
Anpathos, Melanus, Tarak---settlers have been spreading out across the galaxy for generations. I come from Mejare, the planet of women.
Even among Earth's colonies, my homeworld is unusual for only having women on it. The male planet is close by...
...I understand. Girls on my homeworld used to spread rumors about me when I walked the streets.
...I remember girls whispering things about me, as well. It's easy to pick out loners to make fun of.
...So it was just gossip. I try not to participate in that sort of thing.
...If it's just gossip, then I'm not interested in spreading it. Ask around yourself.
It's how Mejare was settled. We do have male prisoners onboard---one is under my command in the Dread team.
Mejare is the only colony without them. I've actually had to mentor a man that joined my Dread team as our prisoner.
I saw you handling some balls earlier. Are they one of those instruments?
You had some big balls in your hands when I first arrived. I assume they're delicate instruments.
Actually, I hate the crash they give me. I prefer lean, filling foods so I can stay out on patrol for longer.
I said that because most of my crewmates prepare sweets for holidays. I hate the feeling of a sugar crash.
I usually take fish or soup from our cafeteria. There's desserts, but I don't want to lose energy while I'm scouting.
...I think I understand. As far as the Mejarian Empire is concerned, no one should ever want to leave.
...The Mejarian Empire isn't known for its freedom, either. If people were allowed to leave, they might see men for themselves.
People? So...could it be that the Paksis crystal was introduced here by colonists from the future? We haven't developed any way to manipulate time...
You mean...some kind of time displacement? Colonists using that energy to space travel---and then bringing it to Earth in the first place?
...People came here with that energy? The Paksis should have made space travel possible in the first place---it couldn't have been colonists. Unless it allowed time travel...!
The Paksis crystal is a living thing. Our engineer has told me it even feeds off our emotional signatures...maybe it's an evolved state for those creatures.
...No one's quite sure of the Paksis's origin anymore. But apparently it develops its own feelings from harnessing the energy of ours. Maybe those creatures are its basic form.
I just tend to believe myself when I get a bad feeling. It helps when I'm on scouting patrols.
My scouting missions wouldn't do much good if I never rightly got a bad feeling. Just don't make any sudden moves.

W-what the---oh my God! What are you---?

If you want my favor, hurry up.
